name: Moong Dal Roti
ingredients:
1 tbsp split moong dal (boiled)
30g whole wheat flour
2-3 mint leaves, chopped
½ tsp ginger and garlic paste
1 green chili, finely chopped
¼ tsp sesame seeds
¼ tsp turmeric powder
¼ tsp red chili powder
¼ tsp garam masala
¼ tsp chaat masala
¼ tsp dry mango powder (amchur)
¼ tsp roasted cumin powder
Salt to taste
1 tsp oil
nutrition:
Calories: 150-160 kcal
Protein: 6-7 grams
Carbohydrates: 25-28 grams
Fat: 3-4 grams
Fiber: 3-4 grams
method:
1. In a bowl, combine the boiled and mashed moong dal. Add all the spices, including turmeric powder, red chili powder, garam masala powder, chaat masala powder, dry mango powder (amchur), roasted cumin powder, and salt. Also, add sesame seeds, ginger-garlic paste, and oil.

2. Incorporate the whole wheat flour, chopped mint leaves, and finely chopped green chili into the mixture. Mix thoroughly. Note that no additional water is needed for this dough; the boiled moong dal provides sufficient moisture.

3. Take a portion of the dough and shape it into a ball. Dust it with a little flour and roll it out into a circular shape.

4. Heat a flat pan or griddle and place the roti on it. Cook until golden spots appear on one side.

5. Flip the roti to the other side and apply a small amount of oil. Cook until both sides are golden and crispy.

6.Your Moong Dal Roti is now ready to be served. Enjoy!

name: Okra Omelette
ingredients:
100g chopped okra (ladyfinger)
2 eggs
20g chopped onion (optional)
1 tsp rice flour
¼ tsp chopped garlic
¼ tsp ground black pepper
Salt to taste
Chili powder (based on personal preference)
1 tsp oil
nutrition:
Calories: 210-230 kcal
Protein: 11-12 grams
Carbohydrates: 11-12 grams
Fat: 14-15 grams
Fiber: 3-4 grams
method:
1. In a mixing bowl, beat the eggs thoroughly.

2. Add the chopped okra, garlic, black pepper, salt, chili powder (if using), chopped onions (if desired), and rice flour to the beaten eggs.

3. Gently stir the mixture until all the ingredients are well combined. Allow it to sit for up to 10 minutes to allow the flavors to meld.

4. Heat a small amount of oil in a pan over medium heat. Pour a large spoonful of the mixture into the pan, forming a round circular shape.

5. Cook the omelette for 3-4 minutes on each side, or until it turns golden brown and is cooked through.

6. Serve hot and enjoy your nutritious Okra (Ladyfinger) Omelette!

name: Broken Wheat Uttapam With Mint And Black Gram Chutney
ingredients:
For Wheat Uttapam:
30g broken wheat
1 tsp whole green gram
1 tsp whole wheat flour
1 tsp besan flour
1 tbsp curd
1 or 2 green chilies
1 tsp chopped coriander
Salt to taste
½ tsp lemon juice
¼ tsp fennel seeds
¼ tsp sesame seeds
1 tsp oil

For Green Chutney:
20g mint leaves
Onion
Tamarind
1 pod garlic
1 green chili
Salt to taste

For Black Gram Chutney:
1 tbsp black gram
1 red chili
1 pod garlic
Tamarind
Curry leaves
Salt to taste
nutrition:
Calories: 200-220 kcal
Protein: 6-7 grams
Carbohydrates: 35-40 grams
Fat: 4-5 grams
Fiber: 5-6 grams
method:
For Wheat Uttapam:

1. Soak broken wheat in hot water for 20-30 minutes and then drain out the water.

2. Combine the soaked broken wheat, curd, and half a cup of water. Blend until you achieve a smooth consistency.

3. Transfer the broken wheat mixture into a bowl. Add wheat flour, besan flour, green chilies, sesame seeds, lemon juice, fennel seeds, chopped coriander, and salt. Mix well.

4. Grease a mini uttapam pan with oil.

5. Pour the batter into the pan and cook until it turns golden brown.

6. Serve hot with your choice of green chutney or black gram chutney.

*For Green Chutney:*

1. Blend all the ingredients listed for the green chutney, adding a little water to achieve the desired consistency.

*For Black Gram Chutney:*

1. Dry roast all the ingredients mentioned for the black gram chutney. Let them cool for some time.

2. Blend the roasted ingredients by adding a small amount of water until you achieve the desired consistency.

name: Puttu With Kadala Curry
ingredients:
For Puttu:
30g rice flour
2 tsp grated coconut (optional)
2 tsp water for sprinkling
Salt to taste

For Kadala Curry (Chickpea Curry):
30g chickpeas, soaked overnight and pressure cooked
2 cups water
20g onion
25g tomato
2 cloves garlic
¼ tsp turmeric powder
¼ tsp chili powder
¼ tsp coriander powder
¼ tsp garam masala powder
½ tsp mustard seeds
½ tsp fennel seeds
½ dried chili
A few curry leaves
2 tsp oil
Salt to taste
nutrition:
Calories: 300-320 kcal
Protein: 9-10 grams
Carbohydrates: 50-55 grams
Fat: 8-9 grams
Fiber: 8-9 grams
method:
For Puttu:

1. Sieve rice flour and salt into a bowl.

2. Sprinkle water in batches into the rice flour and mix until it binds together.

3. Take a puttu maker and layer it with grated coconut (if using) and rice flour.

4. Steam the mixture to cook the puttu.

For Kadala Curry (Chickpea Curry):

1. In a large kadai, heat oil and splutter mustard seeds, fennel seeds, dried red chili, and a few curry leaves.

2. Add onions and tomatoes. Sauté until the onions turn translucent. Let it cool down and blend into a paste.

3. Transfer the paste into a saucepan, heat it, and then add the cooked chickpeas.

4. Add chili powder, turmeric powder, coriander powder, garam masala, and salt. Mix well.

5. Add water and cook the curry until it reaches your desired consistency.

6. Serve hot Kadala Curry with Puttu.

name: Chana Dal Idli With Peanut Chutney
ingredients:
For Idli:
30g bengal gram dal (chana dal)
30g urad dal
30g rice
1 tsp grated ginger
1 tsp finely chopped green chili
Pinch of turmeric
¼ tsp mustard seeds
1 sprig of curry leaves
Salt to taste
1 tsp oil for greasing
Pinch of baking soda

For Peanut Chutney:
30g peanuts
nutrition:
Calories: 180-200 kcal
Protein: 6-7 grams
Carbohydrates: 30-35 grams
Fat: 3-4 grams
Fiber: 2-3 grams
method:
For Idli:

1. Wash chana dal, urad dal, and rice, and soak them for 4-5 hours.

2. Grind them together with a little water to make a smooth batter. Cover the lid and allow it to ferment overnight.

3. After fermenting, add some water to adjust the consistency.

4. Season the batter with salt, turmeric powder, green chili, ginger, and baking soda. Mix well.

5. Grease the idli pan and pour the idli batter into it using a ladle.

6. Place it in a pressure cooker or idli maker with a little water. Ensure that the water doesn't touch the idli pan's plate to prevent sogginess.

7. Steam for 10-12 minutes and allow to cool for 5 minutes before demolding. Serve hot with peanut chutney.

For Peanut Chutney:

1. Roast the peanuts until they turn golden brown.

2. Grind the roasted peanuts to a fine powder.

name: Oats Besan Chila/Dosa
ingredients:
For Oats Chila:
40g rolled oats
20g besan flour (gram flour)
20ml curd/yogurt
1/2 cup water
¼ tsp turmeric
½ tsp ginger paste
1 or 2 green chilies, finely chopped
¼ tsp crushed cumin (jeera)
30g onion, finely chopped
30g tomato, finely chopped
Salt to taste
Olive oil, for roasting
1 tsp rava (semolina)
1 tsp olive oil (or preferred oil)

For Green Chutney:
20g mint leaves
Onion
Tamarind
1 pod garlic
1 green chili
Salt to taste
nutrition:
Calories: 250-270 kcal
Protein: 8-9 grams
Carbohydrates: 36-40 grams
Fat: 8-9 grams
Fiber: 7-8 grams
method:
For Oats Chila:

1. Dry roast the rolled oats until they turn crisp. Ensure you use unflavored oats as we are adding spices later.

2. Cool the roasted oats completely, and then blend them into a fine powder without adding any water.

3. Transfer the powdered oats into a large mixing bowl and add 1 tsp rava for binding.

4. Add 20ml curd and 1/2 cup of water. Whisk and mix to make a smooth, lump-free batter.

5. Additionally, add ¼ tsp turmeric, ½ tsp ginger paste, chopped green chilies, ¼ tsp crushed cumin, chopped onion, chopped tomato, and salt. Mix well to form a thick, flowing consistency chila batter.

6. Heat a tawa (griddle) and pour a ladleful of batter onto it. Spread gently.

7. Drizzle ½ tsp olive oil over the chila, cover it, and allow it to cook on a medium flame for about a minute.

8. Flip the chila and cook both sides while pressing gently.

9. The Oats Chila is now ready to serve with Green Chutney.

For Green Chutney:

1. Blend all the mentioned ingredients for the green chutney, adding a little water to achieve the desired consistency.

name: Aval Upma
ingredients:
30g aval (flattened red rice)
20g onion, finely chopped
½ inch ginger, finely chopped
1 green chili, finely chopped
2 tsp coriander leaves, chopped
Few drops of lemon juice
Pinch of turmeric
¼ tsp mustard seeds
Pinch of asafoetida
1 tsp oil
Curry leaves
1 dry chili
Salt to taste
15g roasted groundnuts
nutrition:
Calories: 150-160 kcal
Protein: 3-4 grams
Carbohydrates: 20-25 grams
Fat: 7-8 grams
Fiber: 2-3 grams
method:
1. Wash the aval (flattened red rice) in running water and let it soak for 15 minutes.

2. Heat a pan and add mustard seeds. Allow them to crackle, then add a pinch of asafoetida, dry red chili, and curry leaves. Sauté well.

3. Add the finely chopped onion, green chili, ginger, and turmeric powder. Sauté for a minute until the onions become translucent.

4. Now, add the soaked aval and roasted groundnuts. Sprinkle some water if necessary to moisten the mixture. Add salt to taste and mix well.

5. Finally, add a few drops of lemon juice and chopped coriander leaves. Mix well.

6. Serve the Aval Upma hot.

name: Steamed Chana Dal Bufauri
ingredients:
60g chana dal (split chickpeas)
30g onion, finely chopped
5-6 bulbs garlic, finely chopped
1 inch ginger, finely chopped
2 green chillies, finely chopped
1 tsp chilli powder
1 tbsp ajwain (carom seeds)
1 tsp baking soda
1 tsp turmeric powder
1/3 cup chopped cilantro
1/2 cup chopped sweet pea leaves
1 tsp oil
Water as required
Salt as required
nutrition:
Calories: 250-270 kcal
Protein: 10-12 grams
Carbohydrates: 45-50 grams
Fat: 3-4 grams
Fiber: 7-8 grams
method:
1. Soak chana dal (split chickpeas) for 3-4 hours. Drain the water and grind it to a smooth paste. Add a little water while grinding if required. The paste should resemble a thick lumpy texture.

2. Transfer the ground dal paste to a mixing bowl.

3. Add finely chopped green chillies, sweet pea leaves, cilantro, chopped onions, ginger, and garlic to the bowl.

4. Mix in baking soda, turmeric powder, chilli powder, ajwain (carom seeds), and salt.

5. Add oil and water to the mixture and stir until you have a thick batter.

6. Grease your steamer plate with cooking spray or oil if desired. Pour a spoonful of the batter into each mold.

7. Steam these cakes for 20-30 minutes on medium flame.

8. Once done, open the steamer and carefully de-mold the bufauri.

9. Serve the Chana Dal Bufauri with some spicy green chutney or tomato chutney.

name: Ragi And Oats Rava Idli
ingredients:
20g ragi flour
20g oats
10g semolina (Rava)
25ml curd (yogurt)
1 green chili, finely chopped
¼ tsp ginger, finely chopped
Pinch of baking powder
1 tsp oil
3-4 curry leaves
½ tsp mustard seeds
Salt to taste
1 tsp coriander leaves, chopped
nutrition:
Calories: 180-200 kcal
Protein: 6-7 grams
Carbohydrates: 30-35 grams
Fat: 4-5 grams
Fiber: 4-5 grams
method:
1. In a large mixing bowl, combine the ragi flour, oats, semolina (rava), yogurt, and a little salt.

2. Gradually add about one cup of water, little by little, to make a thick batter. Allow the mixture to rest for 10 to 15 minutes.

3. Heat oil in a pan over medium flame. Add mustard seeds and curry leaves and allow them to crackle. Turn off the heat and set aside.

4. After the batter has rested for 15 minutes, adjust its consistency to that of thick pouring consistency.

5. Next, add the seasoning: green chilies, ginger, baking powder, and the tablespoon of oil. Stir well to combine.

6. Preheat an idli steamer with enough water and grease the idli plates.

7. Pour the ragi oats rava idli batter into the idli mold cavities.

8. Place them in the preheated steamer and steam the idlis for 10-15 minutes or until a skewer inserted in the center comes out clean.

9. Once steamed, remove the ragi oats rava idli from the steamer and let them sit for 5 minutes. Sprinkle some water over the idlis to help release them cleanly from the cavities. Use a spoon to gently loosen the idlis from the sides of the cavities.

10. Serve the Ragi and Oats Rava Idli with your favorite chutney.

name: Lauki Paratha
ingredients:
For Paratha Dough:
60g wheat flour
1 tsp salt
Water as required

For Filling:
1 cup lauki (bottle gourd), grated
1 onion, finely chopped
Small piece of ginger, grated or finely chopped
2 green chillies, finely chopped
Handful of coriander leaves, finely chopped
1/4 tsp turmeric powder
1/2 tsp coriander powder
1/4 tsp cumin powder
1/4 tsp raw mango powder (optional)
1/2 tsp red chilli powder
Salt to taste
nutrition:
Calories: 320-350 kcal
Protein: 9-10 grams
Carbohydrates: 65-70 grams
Fat: 2-3 grams
Fiber: 7-8 grams
method:
For Paratha Dough:

1. In a bowl, add wheat flour and salt. Gradually add water as required to prepare a soft dough. Set aside.

For Filling:

1. In another bowl, combine the finely chopped or grated lauki, onion, green chillies, red chilli powder, turmeric powder, coriander powder, cumin powder, raw mango powder (if using), salt, and coriander leaves. Mix all the ingredients well.

*Assembling and Cooking Paratha:*

1. Pinch out a ball-sized portion of the dough and flatten it to make a small roti.

2. Place a portion of the lauki filling in the center of the roti.

3. Fold the sides of the roti to cover the filling and seal it, then gently roll it out with a rolling pin to make a paratha.

4. Heat a pan and cook the paratha. Apply a little oil and cook on both sides until it's golden and crispy.

5. Serve the Lauki Stuffed Paratha with yogurt or your favorite chutney.

name: Phulka
ingredients:
1 cup Whole Wheat Flour
½ teaspoon Salt (optional)
½ teaspoon Oil (optional)
nutrition:
Calories: 70-80 kcal
Protein: 2-3 grams
Carbohydrates: 14-15 grams
Fat: 1-2 grams
Fiber: 2-3 grams
method:
1. In a large bowl, combine the whole wheat flour and salt (if using). Gradually add a little water at a time to make a firm dough. Add a teaspoon of oil (if using) to coat the dough and knead it for a few more minutes until smooth.

2. Set the dough aside to rest, covered, for 15 minutes. After resting, knead the dough once again and divide it into 8 equal portions.

3. Preheat an iron skillet or a flat pan on medium heat.

4. Roll each portion of the phulka (roti) dough into a ball and flatten these balls with the palm of your hand.

5. Take one portion of the phulka dough, dust it in dry flour, and roll it out into thin circles to approximately 6 inches in diameter. You can keep dusting the dough with dry flour while rolling to prevent it from getting sticky.

6. Place the rolled dough onto the hot skillet. After a few seconds, small air pockets will start to form. At this point, flip the rolled dough to the other side on the skillet.

7. After a few seconds, turn the flame to high, and using tongs, take the rolled phulka dough off the skillet and place it directly on the flame. It should balloon into a spherical shape and puff up. This is known as the phulka.

8. Remove the phulka from the heat and place it on a flat plate. Continue the same process for the remaining portions of the rolled phulka dough, stacking them one on top of the other.

name: Plain Rice
ingredients:
30 grams white rice
¼ cup water
nutrition:
Calories: 50-60 kcal
Protein: 1-2 grams
Carbohydrates: 11-12 grams
Fat: 0 grams
Fiber: 0 grams
method:
1. Add white rice and water to a medium saucepan and bring it to a boil over high heat.

2. Once it starts boiling, lower the heat to a simmer and cover the saucepan. Ensure that it's simmering and not boiling vigorously, as this can cause the rice to cook too quickly.

3. Simmer the rice until all the water is completely absorbed, and the rice becomes tender. This usually takes about 15-25 minutes, but the cooking time can vary depending on the size and freshness of the rice. There should not be any excess water; drain it if necessary.

4. Turn off the heat, remove the lid, and fluff the rice with a fork. Put the lid back on and let it rest for 10 minutes. This resting period allows the moisture to redistribute and prevents the rice from becoming mushy.

Tip:

Store any cooled leftovers covered in the refrigerator for up to 5-6 days or in the freezer for up to 1 month. Reheat in the microwave or on the stovetop with a little oil or water until warm.

name: Carrot Stuffed Idli With Veg Sambar
ingredients:
125ml idli/dosa batter
1/2 cup carrots (Gajjar), grated
Salt to taste
nutrition:
Calories: 150-160 kcal
Protein: 3-4 grams
Carbohydrates: 30-35 grams
Fat: 0-1 gram
Fiber: 2-3 grams
method:
1. Preheat the idli steamer with water.

2. Grease idli plates with a drop or two of sesame oil for each cavity.

3. Fill each idli mold with less than half of the idli batter.

4. Spoon in the grated carrot, spreading it evenly on the batter.

5. Finally, top this layer with another round of the idli batter to make a sandwich idli.

6. Steam the idlis in an idli steamer for about 10 minutes on high heat, then turn off the heat.

7. After 10 minutes, the idlis should be steamed completely.

8. Allow the steamed idlis to rest for a few minutes, then remove them from the molds and cut them into quarters.

9. Serve the carrot-stuffed Idli recipe along with bean sambar.

Vegetable Sambar

Ingredients for 1 Serving:

For Pressure Cooking Dal and Vegetables:
10g toor dal (arhar dal/split pigeon peas)
Pinch of turmeric powder (haldi)
10g radish (mooli), chopped
2 pieces drumstick
10g carrot, chopped
5ml tamarind juice
20g tomato, finely chopped
Few curry leaves
10g onion, cubed
Salt to taste
1 tsp sambar powder

For Tempering:
½ tbsp coconut oil (or cooking oil)
½ tsp mustard seeds (rai)
Pinch of hing (asafoetida)
½ dried red chilli
Few curry leaves

Nutritional Information (Approximate) for 1 Serving:

Calories: 150-160 kcal
Protein: 6-7 grams
Carbohydrates: 20-25 grams
Fat: 6-7 grams
Fiber: 4-5 grams

Method:

Pressure Cooking Dal and Vegetables:

1. In a pressure cooker, take half a cup of washed toor dal.

2. Add 2 cups of water to cook the dal, along with a pinch of turmeric powder. Place a small bowl into the pressure cooker, and add the vegetables (radish, carrot, drumstick) or vegetables of your choice into the bowl. Do not add any water.

3. Cover the cooker and pressure cook for 5 whistles on medium flame.

4. Once the pressure releases, remove the cooked vegetables and mash the dal well.

Mix Veg Sambar:

1. In a large kadai, squeeze 1 cup of tamarind juice.

2. Add chilli, tomatoes, curry leaves, turmeric powder, and jaggery. Bring the tamarind water to a boil.

3. Further, add onions and salt. Mix well and boil for 5 minutes.

4. Add the cooked vegetables and bring to a boil again. Do not overcook as the vegetables are already cooked.

5. Add the mashed dal and give it a good mix.

6. Bring the sambar to a boil. Do not over boil after adding dal, as it can result in indigestion.

7. Add udupi style sambar powder and mix well to prevent lumps.

8. Boil for a minute and switch off the stove.

9. Prepare the tempering by heating oil in a small kadai. Add mustard seeds, hing, red chilli, and curry leaves. Once they splutter, pour the tempering into the sambar.

10. Give the vegetable sambar a good mix and serve it with hot steamed idli.

name: Chickpea Chila With Ridge Gourd
ingredients:
30g chickpeas (boiled and mashed)
1 tbsp wheat flour
100g grated ridge gourd
1 onion, finely chopped
¼ tsp turmeric powder
1 tsp whole cumin (jeera)
1 tsp coriander leaves, finely chopped
Salt to taste
1 tsp oil
nutrition:
Calories: 170-180 kcal
Protein: 6-7 grams
Carbohydrates: 25-30 grams
Fat: 5-6 grams
Fiber: 6-7 grams
method:
1. In a bowl, mix the wheat flour with mashed chickpeas and enough water to make a thick, lump-free batter.

2. After preparing the batter, add grated ridge gourd, chopped onion, chopped coriander leaves, whole cumin, turmeric powder, and salt. Mix everything well to form a batter.

3. Heat a tava (flat skillet) and grease it with oil. Add the mixture to the tava and spread it out into a round shape.

4. Cover the tava with a lid and cook the chila over medium heat for 3 to 4 minutes.

5. Open the lid and flip the chila to the other side. Allow it to cook for a few more minutes or until the edges appear crispy.

6. Serve the chickpea and ridge gourd chila hot with curd.

name: Poha With Capsicum Aan Paneer
ingredients:
30g poha (flattened rice)
100g capsicum
50g paneer
20g onion
1 green chilli
2 tsp coriander leaves
Few drops of lemon juice
Pinch of turmeric
¼ tsp mustard seeds
1 tsp oil
Curry leaves
Salt to taste
nutrition:
Calories: 220-230 kcal
Protein: 7-8 grams
Carbohydrates: 28-30 grams
Fat: 9-10 grams
Fiber: 3-4 grams
method:
1. Wash poha in running water and let it soak for 15 minutes. Drain any excess water.

2. Heat a pan and add mustard seeds. Allow them to crackle, then add curry leaves and sauté well.

3. Add chopped onion, green chilli, capsicum, and turmeric powder. Sauté for a minute until the vegetables start to soften.

4. Now add the soaked poha and paneer. If needed, sprinkle some water to prevent sticking. Add salt and mix well.

5. Finally, add lemon juice and coriander leaves. Mix well and serve hot.

name: Bajra Methi Thelpa
ingredients:
30g bajra flour (pearl millet flour)
30g wheat flour
½ tsp sesame seeds
30g finely chopped methi (fenugreek leaves)
¼ tsp ginger-garlic and chilli paste
Pinch of turmeric
Salt to taste
nutrition:
Calories: 170-180 kcal
Protein: 5-6 grams
Carbohydrates: 34-36 grams
Fat: 1-2 grams
Fiber: 4-5 grams
method:
1. In a bowl, combine the bajra flour, wheat flour, sesame seeds, and finely chopped methi.

2. Add ginger-garlic paste, green chilli paste, turmeric powder, and salt to the dry ingredients. Mix well.

3. Gradually add water in batches to knead a soft dough.

4. Divide the dough into 6 equal portions and roll each portion into a roti.

5. Heat a tava (flat skillet) and cook the rotis on both sides until they turn golden brown.

6. Serve the Bajra and Methi Roti with curd.

name: Godhuma / Wheat Dosa With Tomato Chutney
ingredients:
20g wheat flour
10g rice flour
20g finely chopped onion
1 small finely chopped green chilli
1-inch piece of ginger, finely chopped
¼ tsp whole cumin
1 tsp finely chopped curry leaves
Salt to taste
2 tsp curd
2 tsp water
nutrition:
Calories: 130-140 kcal
Protein: 3-4 grams
Carbohydrates: 28-30 grams
Fat: 1-2 grams
Fiber: 2-3 grams

Ingredients for Tomato Chutney (1 Serving):

20g onion
30g tomato
1 dry red chilli
¼ tsp mustard seeds
¼ tsp whole cumin
Few curry leaves
½ tsp urad dal
Pinch of sugar
1 tsp oil
2 garlic cloves

Nutritional Information for Tomato Chutney (Approximate):

Calories: 60-70 kcal
Protein: 1-2 grams
Carbohydrates: 6-8 grams
Fat: 3-4 grams
Fiber: 1-2 grams
method:
For Wheat Dosa:

1. In a bowl, combine wheat flour, rice flour, chopped onion, green chilli, ginger, whole cumin, curry leaves, salt, curd, and water. Mix all the ingredients well to form a thin consistency batter. Set it aside for a while.

2. Take a skillet, pour the batter from a little distance, and cook to make thin, crispy dosa.

For Tomato Chutney:

1. Heat oil in a pan. Add mustard seeds and let them crackle, then add cumin, curry leaves, urad dal, garlic cloves, dry chilli, and sauté well.

2. Add onion and tomato. Sauté for 3 minutes, then add sugar and salt. Mix well and let it cool down. Blend it to make chutney.

3. Serve the Tomato Chutney with Wheat Dosa.

name: Idiyappam
ingredients:
30g rice flour
50ml water
Salt to taste
10ml oil
nutrition:
Calories: 120-130 kcal
Protein: 1-2 grams
Carbohydrates: 24-26 grams
Fat: 2-3 grams
Fiber: 1-2 grams
method:
1. Heat water in a bowl, add oil, rice flour, and salt. Mix well to form a soft dough.

2. Grease an idiyappam maker and stuff it with the required amount of dough.

3. Grease an idli tray and press out idiyappam onto it.

4. Steam the idiyappam for 10-12 minutes.

5. Serve hot with curry.

name: Vegetable Jowar Upma
ingredients:
30g whole Jowar
5g onion
5g tomato
5g beans
5g capsicum
5g peas
5g urad dal
1 green chilli
½ tsp finely chopped ginger
½ tsp mustard seeds
½ tsp whole cumin
1 pinch hing
½ tsp Jeera
1 tsp lemon juice
1 tsp oil
Salt to taste
nutrition:
Calories: 150-160 kcal
Protein: 5-6 grams
Carbohydrates: 30-32 grams
Fat: 2-3 grams
Fiber: 5-6 grams
method:
1. Wash and soak jowar for at least 8 hours. Drain and add 1 cup of water, then pressure cook.

2. Chop all the vegetables into cubes.

3. Heat a pan with oil, cumin, and mustard seeds to allow them to crackle.

4. Add urad dal, onion, green chilli, ginger, and sauté them.

5. When onions are cooked, add vegetables and sauté. Cover and cook until soft, adding some water if necessary.

6. Add salt and stir.

7. Add pressure-cooked jowar and cook for 5 minutes.

8. Add lemon juice and coriander leaves, and stir well.

9. Serve hot.

name: Vegetable Oats And Egg Chila With Mint Chutney
ingredients:
30g oats
2 egg whites and 1 egg yolk
20g finely chopped onion
30g chopped tomato
20g chopped capsicum
20g cabbage
1 small finely chopped green chilli
Salt to taste
4 tsp curd
2 tsp water
1 tsp oil

Mint Chutney

Ingredients:

50g mint leaves
2 green chillies
Salt to taste
Pinch of whole cumin
nutrition:
Calories: 300-320 kcal
Protein: 15-16 grams
Carbohydrates: 30-32 grams
Fat: 12-14 grams
Fiber: 6-7 grams
method:
For Vegetable Oats and Egg Chila:

1. Roast oats and keep them aside.

2. Finely chop onion, tomato, capsicum, cabbage, and green chillies.

3. Take a bowl and beat 2 egg whites and 1 egg yolk. Add the chopped vegetables, oats, curd, salt, and combine well.

4. Heat a pan, grease it with oil, and pour the batter on the pan to make a dosa.

For Mint Chutney:

1. Grind mint leaves and green chillies into a chutney. Add oil and a pinch of whole cumin to it.

2. Mix everything together and serve with vegetable oats and egg chila.

name: Daliya Idli
ingredients:
Ingredients for 1 Serving:

30g dalia (broken wheat)
50ml yogurt/curd
30g onion
50g capsicum (finely chopped)
50g green peas
1 tbsp carrot (optional)
¼ tsp mustard seeds
1 green chili (optional)
2 tsp oil
Salt according to taste

For Steaming Idli:

500ml water
nutrition:
Calories: 250-270 kcal
Protein: 7-8 grams
Carbohydrates: 40-42 grams
Fat: 7-8 grams
Fiber: 6-7 grams
method:
Roasting Vegetables:

1. Heat oil over medium flame in a pan.

2. Once the oil is hot, add mustard seeds and roast for 5 seconds.

3. Add chopped onion, cook for some time, and then add carrots, peas, capsicum, and salt. Mix well and let it cook on medium flame for 2 minutes to help soften the vegetables.

4. Switch off the stove and transfer the vegetables to a bowl.

Preparing Dalia Mixture:

1. Add dalia (broken wheat) and curd to the bowl with vegetables. Mix well.

2. Add water and mix it well. Cover the lid and keep it aside for 10 minutes.

Steaming Idli:

1. Grease the idli stand with oil.

2. Add the dalia mixture to the greased idli stand holes.

3. For steaming idli, add 500ml of water in a pressure cooker. Place the idli stand inside the cooker.

4. Cover the cooker with its lid and remove the whistle.

5. Let it steam/cook on medium flame for 20 minutes.

6. After 20 minutes, switch off the stove.

7. Serve the Dalia Idli with chutney or veg sambar.

name: Quinoa Chia Pudding
ingredients:
Ingredients for 1 Serving:

30g quinoa
10g chia seeds
100ml milk
2 tsp honey
1 tsp oil
2 cups water
1 kiwi fruit
nutrition:
Calories: 320-340 kcal
Protein: 7-8 grams
Carbohydrates: 50-55 grams
Fat: 9-10 grams
Fiber: 10-12 grams
method:
1. Measure and wash quinoa in water, then drain away the water using a sieve.

2. Heat oil in a pan and add quinoa. Toast for a minute, then add water and start cooking.

3. Simmer the flame and cook for 15 minutes. You will see small tails coming out from quinoa; it should have absorbed all the water. Then switch off the flame and fluff it up.

4. In a cup, take milk and add chia seeds. Soak it for 15 minutes.

5. Mix the soaked chia seeds into the cooked quinoa. Add honey, finely diced kiwi, and chill it.

6. Serve it with kiwi or other fruit toppings.

name: Ragi Banana Pancake
ingredients:
15g ragi flour
1 tsp wheat flour
1 tsp besan (gram flour)
1 tsp rice flour
50g banana
2 tsp egg white
1 tsp oil
nutrition:
Calories: 180-200 kcal
Protein: 6-7 grams
Carbohydrates: 30-35 grams
Fat: 4-5 grams
Fiber: 4-5 grams
method:
1. In a bowl, mash the banana thoroughly.

2. Add the ragi flour, wheat flour, besan (gram flour), and rice flour to the mashed banana. Mix well to create a smooth batter.

3. Add the egg white and a small amount of water to the batter, ensuring it has a thick consistency. Let the batter rest for about 10 minutes.

4. Heat a pan (tawa) and add 1 teaspoon of oil to it.

5. Pour the batter onto the pan and spread it evenly to form a thick pancake.

6. Cook the pancake on medium heat until it's golden brown on one side, then flip it and cook the other side until it's also golden brown.

7. Once both sides are cooked and the pancake is firm, remove it from the pan.

8. Serve the Ragi Banana Pancake hot and enjoy.

name: Sprouts-Palak Dhokla
ingredients:
10g green gram sprouts
100g spinach
30g besan (gram flour)
1 tsp green chillies, finely chopped
1 tsp curry leaves, chopped
1 tsp lemon juice
2 tsp oil
Salt to taste
nutrition:
Calories: 150-170 kcal
Protein: 7-8 grams
Carbohydrates: 17-20 grams
Fat: 6-7 grams
Fiber: 4-5 grams
method:
For Dhokla:

1. In a bowl, combine the green gram sprouts, spinach, besan (gram flour), chopped green chillies, chopped curry leaves, lemon juice, and salt. Mix everything well to form a coarse mixture.

2. Grease a flat thali (plate) with a little oil and spread the mixture evenly in it.

3. Steam the mixture in a pressure cooker without a whistle or use a steamer for approximately 45 minutes or until the dhoklas are fully cooked. Cooking time may vary due to the sprouts, so ensure they are thoroughly cooked.

For Tadka (Tempering):

1. Heat 2 teaspoons of oil in a small pan.

2. Add the ingredients for the tadka (tempering) one by one and sauté for a few seconds until they release their aroma and the mustard seeds splutter.

3. Pour this tadka over the cooked dhoklas.

4. Cut the dhoklas into pieces in any shape you prefer.

5. Serve the Sprouted Moong Dhoklas with mint chutney or your favorite dipping sauce.

name: Green Peas Pancake With Bottle Gourd Chutney
ingredients:
30g green peas (fresh)
1 tbsp wheat flour
1 tbsp besan (gram flour)
20g grated carrot
25g chopped tomato
30g grated paneer (optional)
½ tsp chopped green chilli
¼ tsp turmeric powder
Salt according to taste
1 tsp oil
nutrition:
Calories: 200-220 kcal
Protein: 8-9 grams
Carbohydrates: 22-25 grams
Fat: 8-9 grams
Fiber: 4-5 grams
method:
1. First, boil the green peas until they are tender. Then, blend them into a coarse paste and transfer it to a mixing bowl.

2. To the bowl with the green pea paste, add wheat flour, besan, grated carrot, chopped tomato, grated paneer (if using), chopped green chilli, turmeric powder, and salt. Mix everything well. You can add a little water to achieve a pancake batter-like consistency.

3. Heat a non-stick pan and grease it with 1 teaspoon of oil.

4. Pour a ladleful of the mixture onto the hot pan and spread it into a round pancake shape. Shallow fry until both sides are golden brown and the pancake is cooked through.

5. Repeat the process for the remaining batter, adding a little oil to the pan as needed.

6. Serve the Peas and Carrot Pancakes hot with your favorite chutney or sauce.

name: Moonglet
ingredients:
30g moong dal (green gram)
¼ tsp turmeric powder
1 tsp rice flour
½ tsp whole cumin seeds
1 green chili, finely chopped
½ tsp ginger paste
20g onion, finely chopped
25g tomato, finely chopped
50g capsicum, finely chopped
¼ tsp eno fruit salt (optional)
A pinch of chili powder
1 tbsp fresh coriander leaves, finely chopped
Salt to taste
1 tsp oil
nutrition:
Calories: 220-240 kcal
Protein: 10-11 grams
Carbohydrates: 33-35 grams
Fat: 5-6 grams
Fiber: 7-8 grams
method:
1. Preparation: Soak 30g of moong dal in water for 30 minutes to 1 hour. Drain the water and blend the soaked moong dal into a smooth paste.

2. Making the Batter: Transfer the moong dal paste to a large mixing bowl. Add turmeric powder, rice flour, and salt. Mix well to form a thick batter.

3. Add Vegetables: To the batter, add whole cumin seeds, finely chopped green chili, ginger paste, finely chopped onion, finely chopped tomato, and finely chopped capsicum. Mix everything well to ensure even distribution of vegetables.

4. Eno Fruit Salt: Heat a pan and spread 1 teaspoon of oil. Once the pan is hot, add eno fruit salt to the batter. You can also add a little water at this stage. Gently mix until the batter turns frothy.

5. Cooking: Pour: the batter onto the hot pan, spreading it evenly. Sprinkle a pinch of chili powder and chopped fresh coriander leaves on top. Cover and cook for about 2 minutes or until the base is cooked well.

6. Flip and Cook: Carefully flip the moonglet over and press it gently. Make a slit in the center if needed. Simmer for another minute or until it is cooked completely.

7. Serving: Once cooked, cut it into pieces if desired. Serve the moonglet with green chutney and yogurt.

name: Mini Oats Khakhra
ingredients:
1 tbsp oats (powdered)
20g wheat flour
⅛ tsp sesame seeds
Chilli powder to taste
⅛ tsp turmeric powder
Salt to taste
½ tsp oil
nutrition:
Calories: 110-120 kcal
Protein: 3-4 grams
Carbohydrates: 20-22 grams
Fat: 2-3 grams
Fiber: 2-3 grams
method:
1. Preparation: Start by blending the oats into a powder form. Transfer the powdered oats to a mixing bowl.

2. Mix Ingredients: To the powdered oats, add wheat flour, sesame seeds, chili powder (adjust to your taste), turmeric powder, and salt. Mix all the dry ingredients well.

3. Make Dough: Sprinkle a little water and add oil to the mixture. Mix everything to form a dough. Add water gradually to achieve the right consistency.

4. Roll Out Khakhra: Take a small portion of the dough (about the size of amla) and roll it out into a thin circle using a rolling pin.

5. Cook Khakhra: Heat a tawa (griddle) and place the rolled khakhra on it. Cook it on medium flame until it becomes crispy. You can use a cloth to press the khakhra gently while cooking.

6. Serve: Once the khakhra is crispy, remove it from the tawa and let it cool. Serve it with curd or your favorite dip.

name: Lobia Dosa With Lady's Finger Chutney
ingredients:
30g black-eyed beans (lobia), soaked for 8 hours
3 tsp rice, soaked for 30 minutes
1-2 small green chillies
¼ tsp chopped ginger
¼ tsp whole cumin seeds (jeera)
Salt to taste
1 tsp oil
1 tsp chopped coriander leaves

Ingredients for Lady's Finger Chutney (Approximately 2 Servings):

50g lady's finger (okra)
10g groundnut (peanuts), roasted and husked
1 green chilli
1 pod garlic
⅛ tsp jeera
Salt to taste
¼ tsp oil
nutrition:
Calories: 150-160 kcal
Protein: 5-6 grams
Carbohydrates: 30-32 grams
Fat: 2-3 grams
Fiber: 5-6 grams

Nutritional Information (Approximate) for Lady's Finger Chutney (1 Serving):

Calories: 70-80 kcal
Protein: 2-3 grams
Carbohydrates: 6-7 grams
Fat: 4-5 grams
Fiber: 2-3 grams
method:
For Lobia Dosa:

1. Drain the soaked black-eyed beans and rice.

2. In a mixer grinder, combine the soaked rice, drained black-eyed beans, green chillies, chopped ginger, whole cumin seeds, and water. Blend until you have a smooth batter.

3. Add chopped coriander leaves to the batter and mix well.

4. Adjust the batter's consistency by adding salt and water as needed.

5. Preheat a dosa tawa and grease it with a small amount of oil.

6. Pour a ladleful of dosa batter onto the tawa and spread it gently to form a round dosa.

7. Drizzle ½ tsp of oil around the dosa and cook on medium flame until it turns brownish and starts leaving the pan.

8. Fold the dosa and serve hot with lady's finger chutney.

For Lady's Finger Chutney:

1. Dry roast the groundnuts in a pan until they are slightly browned. Let them cool and then remove the husks by rubbing them between your palms.

2. Heat oil in the same pan and add lady's finger (okra). Cook for 5-10 minutes until it becomes tender.

3. Add green chilli and jeera to the pan and cook for a few more minutes. Then, turn off the stove.

4. In a blender or mixer jar, combine the roasted groundnuts, cooked lady's finger mixture, garlic, salt, and a little water.

5. Blend into a smooth paste to make the chutney.

6. Serve the lady's finger chutney with lobia dosa.

name: Moringa Leaves Idli
ingredients:
30g rice, soaked overnight
1 tbsp urad dal (black gram lentils), soaked overnight
100g chopped drumstick leaves
Salt to taste
nutrition:
Calories: 140-150 kcal
Protein: 5-6 grams
Carbohydrates: 29-30 grams
Fat: 0.5-1 gram
Fiber: 2-3 grams
method:
1. Drain the overnight soaked rice and urad dal.

2. In a blender or mixer, combine the soaked rice and urad dal. Add a small amount of water to blend it into a batter with a smooth consistency.

3. Add salt to the batter and mix it well. Set the batter aside.

4. Heat the idli steamer.

5. In the idli maker, place the chopped drumstick leaves.

6. Pour the idli batter over the drumstick leaves.

7. Close the lid of the idli maker.

8. Steam the idli for 15 minutes or until they are cooked through.

9. Serve the drumstick leaf idli with vegetables, sambar, or chutney.

name: Sprout Bajra Khichdi
ingredients:
30g sprouted bajra (pearl millet)
15g moong dal (green gram lentils), soaked
25g chopped tomato
50g chopped capsicum
20g chopped carrot
20g chopped onion
1/8 tsp turmeric powder
1/8 tsp chili powder
1/8 tsp whole cumin seeds (Jeera)
1/4 tsp ginger garlic paste
1 piece cinnamon
1 piece cardamom
Salt to taste
1 tsp oil
nutrition:
Calories: 220-230 kcal
Protein: 7-8 grams
Carbohydrates: 41-42 grams
Fat: 4-5 grams
Fiber: 9-10 grams
method:
1. Heat a pressure cooker and add oil.

2. Add whole cumin seeds (Jeera), cinnamon, and cardamom.

3. Add chopped onions and sauté until they turn translucent.

4. Add ginger garlic paste, chili powder, and turmeric powder. Sauté for a minute.

5. Add all the chopped vegetables and cook for 2 minutes.

6. Add soaked moong dal and sprouted bajra. Mix well.

7. Add enough water to cover the ingredients and salt to taste.

8. Close the pressure cooker and cook for 2-4 whistles or until the bajra and dal are cooked and soft.

9. Serve the bajra and moong dal vegetable stew hot.

name: Lauki Dosa
ingredients:
100g bottle gourd (shredded)
30g wheat flour
30g onion (optional)
1 chili (chopped)
1 tsp chopped coriander
Salt to taste
1 tsp oil

Black Gram Chutney:

Ingredients (Chutney for Multiple Servings - Adjust to Your Needs):

1 tbsp black gram
1 red chili
1 pod garlic
Tamarind (small piece)
Onion (optional)
Curry leaves
Salt to taste
nutrition:
Calories: 150-160 kcal
Protein: 4-5 grams
Carbohydrates: 30-32 grams
Fat: 2-3 grams
Fiber: 4-5 grams
method:
For Lauki Dosa:

1. In a bowl, combine all the ingredients for the dosa, except for the oil.

2. Add a little water to make a batter with a dosa-like consistency.

3. Heat a non-stick pan or griddle and add a teaspoon of oil.

4. Pour a ladleful of the dosa batter and spread it into a round shape.

5. Cook on both sides until it turns golden brown.

6. Serve the Lauki Dosa with chutney.

For Black Gram Chutney:

1. Dry roast the black gram, red chili, garlic, and tamarind in a pan. Let them cool for some time.

2. Blend the roasted ingredients along with optional onion, curry leaves, and salt, adding a little water to achieve the desired chutney consistency.

name: Lemon Chia Seed Pancake
ingredients:
30g wheat flour
½ tsp lemon juice
¼ tsp lemon zest
1 egg white
1 tsp chia seeds
1 tsp sugar
1 tsp oil
50g banana (for garnishing)
nutrition:
Calories: 180-190 kcal
Protein: 6-7 grams
Carbohydrates: 28-30 grams
Fat: 5-6 grams
Fiber: 4-5 grams
method:
1. In a bowl, combine wheat flour, lemon juice, lemon zest, egg white, chia seeds, and sugar. Mix well by adding a little amount of water to form a pancake batter.

2. Heat a non-stick pan and add a teaspoon of oil.

3. Pour the pancake batter onto the pan and spread it into a round shape.

4. Cook the pancake on both sides until it is golden brown and cooked through.

5. Garnish the pancake with banana slices.

name: Vaghareli Roti(Chapati In Sliced Buttermilk Gravy)
ingredients:
15g besan (gram flour)
50ml curd (for buttermilk)
2 chapatis (approximately CD size)
Pinch of turmeric
⅛ tsp coriander powder
Chilli powder according to taste
Pinch of mustard seeds
2-3 curry leaves
1 dried red chilli
1 chopped garlic clove
1 tsp jaggery (optional)
Salt according to taste
1 tsp oil
nutrition:
Calories: 250-270 kcal
Protein: 6-7 grams
Carbohydrates: 45-50 grams
Fat: 6-7 grams
Fiber: 6-7 grams
method:
1. In a mixing bowl, add besan and curd. Whisk well to ensure there are no lumps.

2. To the besan and curd mixture, add red chilli powder, turmeric, coriander powder, salt, and mix well. Set this mixture aside.

3. Heat a cooking pan on the stove, add oil, and let it heat up.

4. Once the oil is hot, add mustard seeds. As they start to sputter, add curry leaves, dried red chilli, chopped garlic, and jaggery (if using). Sauté for about a minute.

5. Pour the prepared buttermilk mixture into the pan and let it boil on a low flame.

6. While the buttermilk mixture is boiling, cut the chapatis into small pieces.

7. You may add a little water to the buttermilk mixture to adjust its consistency.

8. As the buttermilk mixture starts boiling, add the chapati pieces and mix well. Let it cook for about 3 minutes on medium flame.

9. Once it's cooked properly, add chopped coriander leaves and switch off the flame.

10. Serve hot.

name: Missi Roti With Capsicum Mushroom Semi Dry
ingredients:
20g wheat flour (atta)
20g besan (gram flour)
¼ tsp turmeric powder
½ tsp crushed black pepper
¼ tsp ajwain (carom seeds)
½ tsp amchur (mango powder)
Pinch of hing (asafoetida)
½ tsp ginger garlic paste
½ tsp chilli powder
½ tsp salt
Water, for kneading
Wheat flour, for dusting
Oil or ghee, for roasting
nutrition:
Calories: 220-240 kcal
Protein: 7-8 grams
Carbohydrates: 35-40 grams
Fat: 6-7 grams
Fiber: 4-5 grams
method:
1. In a large mixing bowl, combine ½ cup of wheat flour and ½ cup of besan.

2. Add turmeric powder, crushed black pepper, ajwain, amchur, a pinch of hing, ginger garlic paste, chilli powder, and salt. Mix well to combine the spices.

3. Gradually add water as required and knead the dough until it's smooth and soft. You can also add a teaspoon of oil while kneading.

4. Pinch a medium-sized ball of dough, roll it, and flatten it. Dust it with some wheat flour.

5. Roll it into a slightly thick circle, similar to a chapati.

6. Heat a tawa (griddle) and place the rolled roti on it. Cook for about a minute.

7. When the base is partly cooked, flip the roti and cook the other side. Brush it with oil or ghee and press slightly.

8. Flip the roti once or twice more until both sides are cooked properly.

9. Serve hot.

Capsicum Mushroom Sabzi:

Ingredients (1 Serving):

1 cup sliced capsicum (green pepper)
½ cup finely chopped tomato
1 tablespoon lemon juice
½ teaspoon black pepper
Pinch of salt
10 button mushrooms
½ finely chopped onion
1 tablespoon chaat masala
1 tablespoon oil

Nutritional Information (Approximate):

Calories: 120-140 kcal
Protein: 3-4 grams
Carbohydrates: 15-18 grams
Fat: 6-7 grams
Fiber: 4-5 grams

Method:

1. Heat a little oil in a pan over medium heat. Saute the onions until they turn slightly pinkish in color.

2. Add capsicums and saute them for 5 minutes.

3. Then add tomatoes, mushrooms, and a pinch of salt. Mix all the ingredients well. Cook for another 5 minutes on medium heat.

4. After a few minutes, add chaat masala powder, lemon juice, and black pepper powder. Stir to mix well.

5. Serve hot.

name: Chila Pizza
ingredients:
¾ cup besan (gram flour)
30g tomato puree
20g capsicum
20g onion
15g paneer (cottage cheese)
½ tsp oil for greasing
1 cup water
1 tsp salt
½ tsp chilly flakes
Coriander leaves (for garnish)
Oregano (for garnish)
nutrition:
Calories: 300-350 kcal
Protein: 15-18 grams
Carbohydrates: 40-45 grams
Fat: 9-11 grams
Fiber: 6-8 grams
method:
1. Mix besan with water to form a smooth batter. Add salt, chilly flakes, and chopped coriander leaves to the batter.

2. Heat a non-stick pan and lightly grease it with oil.

3. Pour a ladleful of the besan batter onto the pan to make chilas (pancakes). Cook until both sides are lightly browned. Set them aside.

4. While the chilas are cooking, prepare the toppings. Chop capsicum, onion, and paneer into small pieces.

5. Take a ready chila and spread a layer of tomato puree on it.

6. Add the chopped veggies and paneer on top of the puree.

7. Place the prepared chila pizza in a microwave and heat on high temperature until the cheese melts nicely.

8. Sprinkle oregano and more chilly flakes if desired.

9. Enjoy your yummy and healthy besan chila pizza!

name: Erissery With Rice
ingredients:
100g yellow pumpkin
30g masoor dal (red lentils)
1 small green chilli
¼ tsp turmeric powder
¼ tsp red chilli powder
¼ tsp cumin powder
¼ tsp fenugreek seeds
¼ tsp mustard seeds
20g onion
A few curry leaves
50ml water
1 tsp oil
Salt to taste
nutrition:
Calories: 150-180 kcal
Protein: 7-9 grams
Carbohydrates: 25-30 grams
Fat: 2-3 grams
Fiber: 5-7 grams
method:
1. In a pressure cooker, add diced yellow pumpkin, masoor dal, green chilli, red chilli powder, turmeric powder, cumin powder, salt, and water. Cook for 1 whistle or until the dal and pumpkin are soft.

2. In a pan, heat oil. Add mustard seeds and fenugreek seeds. When they start to splutter, add finely chopped onion. Sauté until the onion becomes translucent.

3. Add curry leaves and sauté for a moment.

4. Transfer the onion and curry leaves mixture to the cooked pumpkin and dal in the pressure cooker. Mix everything well.

5. Serve the pumpkin and masoor dal curry with rice.

Note: You can include additional vegetables like bottle gourd, ridge gourd, ash gourd, etc., for added flavor and nutrition.

name: Kerala Style Chicken Curry
ingredients:
- 100g chicken

- 20g onion

- 25g tomato

- 1 small green chili

- ¼ tsp ginger-garlic paste

- ¼ tsp red chili powder

- ¼ tsp coriander powder

- ¼ tsp turmeric powder

- ¼ tsp garam masala

- 1 tbsp milk

- A few curry leaves

- 2 tsp oil

- Salt to taste
nutrition:
- Calories: 180-200 kcal

- Protein: 20-22 grams

- Carbohydrates: 4-6 grams

- Fat: 10-12 grams

- Fiber: 1-2 grams
method:
In a pan, heat oil and add chopped onion, green chili, ginger-garlic paste, red chili powder, turmeric powder, garam masala, and curry leaves. Sauté until the onions turn translucent and the spices release their aroma.

Add chopped tomatoes and continue to cook until they soften.

Add the chicken pieces and cook for 4-5 minutes until they turn opaque.

Season with salt and add a little water. Continue cooking until the chicken is cooked through and has absorbed the flavors.

Pour in the milk and simmer for another minute, ensuring the chicken is cooked and tender.

Serve the hot and flavorful chicken curry with pathiri or your choice of accompaniment.

name: Nadan Mutta Curry With Wheat Parotha
ingredients:
- 1 whole egg

- ¼ tsp fennel seeds

- 20g finely chopped onion

- 1 crushed garlic clove

- ½ inch crushed ginger

- 1 sprig curry leaves

- ¼ tsp turmeric powder

- ¼ tsp chili powder

- ¼ tsp pepper powder

- ¼ tsp garam masala powder

- ¼ tsp coriander powder

- 25g tomato

- 100ml water

- 1 tsp chopped coriander leaves

- Salt to taste

- 1 tsp oil
nutrition:
- Calories: 160-180 kcal

- Protein: 8-10 grams

- Carbohydrates: 6-8 grams

- Fat: 10-12 grams

- Fiber: 2-3 grams
method:
1. Start by hard-boiling the egg, remove the shell, and set it aside.

2. Heat oil in a saucepan, add fennel seeds, chopped onion, crushed garlic, ginger, and curry leaves. Sauté until the onions turn golden brown.

3. Add turmeric powder, chili powder, pepper powder, coriander powder, and garam masala. Sauté the spices for a couple of minutes until they release their aroma.

4. Add chopped tomatoes and cook until they become soft and mushy.

5. Season with salt and add water. Allow the mixture to simmer for a while.

6. Cut the boiled egg into two halves and add it to the curry.

7. Garnish with chopped coriander leaves.

8. Serve the flavorful egg masala curry with wheat parotta or your choice of accompaniment.

name: Barley Khichdi
ingredients:
- 30g Barley

- 25g Red Gram (Masoor Dal)

- 25g Bengal Gram (Chana Dal)

- 20g Onion

- 25g Tomato

- 10g Peas (Optional)

- 1 tsp Oil

- Salt to taste

- ¼ tsp Turmeric Powder

- ¼ tsp Whole Cumin
nutrition:
- Calories: 300-320 kcal

- Protein: 10-12 grams

- Carbohydrates: 50-55 grams

- Fat: 6-8 grams

- Fiber: 12-14 grams
method:
1. Heat oil in a pressure cooker. Add the whole cumin seeds and sauté for a few seconds.

2. Add the chopped vegetables (onion, tomato, and peas if using) and turmeric powder. Sauté for about 10 seconds on medium heat.

3. Add the barley and both dals (red gram and bengal gram). Mix well.

4. Add 2 cups of water and salt to taste. Stir to combine all the ingredients.

5. Close the pressure cooker with its lid and cook for 2 whistles.

6. Allow the steam to escape naturally before opening the lid.

7. Serve the delicious barley and lentil khichdi immediately with a side of yogurt raita.

name: Shepu Akki Roti With Hyacinth Beans
ingredients:
30g Rice Flour
20g Poha (Flattened Rice)
20g Dill Leaves, Chopped
1 Green Chilli, Chopped
¼ tsp Whole Cumin
Salt to Taste
nutrition:
Calories: 120-130 kcal
Protein: 2-3 grams
Carbohydrates: 27-30 grams
Fat: 0.5-1 gram
Fiber: 1-2 grams
method:
1. Soak the flattened rice (poha) in 1/2 cup of water for about 30 minutes. Mash it until it becomes a soft dough.

2. Add rice flour, chopped dill leaves, green chilli, whole cumin, and salt to the mashed poha.

3. Bind the ingredients together using 1/4 cup of lukewarm water. Knead it into a wet dough that is not sticky.

4. Cover the dough with a damp cloth and let it rest for about 10 minutes.

5. To prepare the roti, place a non-stick tawa (griddle) on the heat. Spread out a large piece of plastic or parchment paper on your work surface.

6. Grease your palms with oil. Take a large ball of dough and place it in the center of the parchment or plastic. Gently flatten it to form a hand-patted disc.

7. Lift the paper, along with the roti, and turn it over. Place it on the hot skillet with the roti side down.

8. Carefully peel off the paper. Drizzle a little oil along the edges of the roti and in the center, into the hole made on the roti. Allow it to sizzle and crisp up.

9. When it appears to be half-cooked, flip the roti over with a spatula to cook the other side.

10. Cook until both sides have brown patches.

11. Serve the shepu roti hot.

Hyacinth Beans Sabzi:

Ingredients (1 Serving):

40g Hyacinth Beans
20g Onion, Finely Chopped
25g Tomato
½ tsp Ginger-Garlic Paste
1 Green Chilli, Finely Chopped
¼ tsp Mustard Seeds
3-4 Curry Leaves
½ tsp Red Chilli Powder
¼ tsp Turmeric Powder
¼ tsp Coriander Powder
¼ cup Finely Chopped Coriander Leaves
1 tsp Oil
½ tsp Kasuri Methi (Dried Fenugreek Leaves)
1 cup Water
Salt to Taste

Nutritional Information (Approximate):

Calories: 130-140 kcal
Protein: 4-5 grams
Carbohydrates: 20-25 grams
Fat: 4-5 grams
Fiber: 6-8 grams

Method:

1. Clean and peel the hyacinth beans, rinse them, and soak for 30 minutes.

2. Heat a pan, add oil and mustard seeds. Let them splutter, then add curry leaves followed by ginger-garlic paste, chopped onion, green chillies, and tomato. Sauté well.

3. Add red chili powder, turmeric powder, coriander powder, and mix well.

4. Add hyacinth beans and mix well. Add 2 cups of water, cover the lid, and let it cook for 9-10 minutes.

5. Afterward, add coriander leaves and kasuri methi, and mix well.

6. Serve the hyacinth beans sabzi with akki roti.

name: Palak Daliya Khichdi
ingredients:
30g Dalia (Broken Wheat)
1 tbsp Moong Dal (Split Yellow Lentils)
100g Finely Chopped Palak (Spinach)
1 Onion, Chopped
1 Tomato, Chopped
1/2 tsp Ginger Garlic Paste
1/4 tsp Whole Cumin
1 Green Chilli, Chopped
1/4 tsp Turmeric Powder
1 Stick Curry Leaves
1/4 tsp Mustard Seeds
1/4 tsp Garam Masala
Salt to Taste
1 tsp Oil
nutrition:
Calories: 250-270 kcal
Protein: 8-10 grams
Carbohydrates: 45-50 grams
Fat: 2-4 grams
Fiber: 6-8 grams
method:
1. Heat 1 tsp of oil in a pressure cooker. Add mustard seeds, whole cumin, and curry leaves.

2. Add chopped onions and green chillies. Cook for a while until the onions become translucent.

3. Add chopped tomatoes and mash them to make a pulp. Stir in ginger garlic paste and mix well.

4. Add chopped spinach (palak), broken wheat (dalia), moong dal, turmeric powder, garam masala, and salt to taste.

5. Stir everything well and then add water. Close the lid of the pressure cooker and cook for 4 whistles on medium flame.

6. Remove from heat and allow the pressure to settle down.

7. Serve the hot and nutritious palak dalia with curd.

name: Khasta Roti
ingredients:
30g Whole Wheat Flour
20g Semolina (Rava)
1 tsp Melted Ghee or Oil
Salt to Taste
nutrition:
Calories: 150-160 kcal
Protein: 5-6 grams
Carbohydrates: 25-30 grams
Fat: 3-4 grams
Fiber: 2-3 grams
method:
1. Combine the whole wheat flour, semolina, melted ghee or oil, and salt in a mixing bowl. Use your fingertips to mix them together until you get a crumbly mixture.

2. Add enough water to the mixture to make a semi-soft dough. Be cautious not to over-knead the dough, as it should retain its crumbly texture. Cover the dough with a lid and set it aside for 10 to 15 minutes.

3. Divide the dough into 2 equal portions and roll each portion into a 100mm diameter thick circle. You should not need any additional flour for rolling.

4. Heat a non-stick tawa (griddle) over high heat. When it's hot, gently place one roti on it. Cook until small bubbles appear on both sides.

5. Cook the roti on an open flame until it puffs up and brown spots appear on both sides.

6. Repeat the process with the remaining dough portion to make 1 more pair of rotis.

7. Serve the rotis immediately with the sabji (vegetable dish) of your choice.

name: Matar Ghugni
ingredients:
1 cup Green Peas

Salt to Taste

1 tbsp Oil

1 tbsp Fennel Seeds

20g Chopped Onions

1 tsp Grated Ginger

½ tsp Turmeric Powder

½ tsp Chilli Powder

½ tsp Freshly Ground Black Pepper

¼ tsp Garam Masala

½ tsp Coriander Powder

25g Chopped Tomatoes

1 tbsp Finely Chopped Coriander
nutrition:
Calories: 200-220 kcal

Protein: 6-7 grams

Carbohydrates: 25-30 grams

Fat: 8-10 grams

Fiber: 8-10 grams
method:
1. In a microwave-safe bowl, combine the green peas and salt along with 2 tbsp of water. Mix well and microwave on high for 3 minutes. Set aside.

2. In another microwave-safe bowl, combine the oil, fennel seeds, and onions. Mix well and microwave on high for 1 minute, stirring once every 30 seconds.

3. Add all the spices - grated ginger, turmeric powder, chilli powder, freshly ground black pepper, garam masala, and coriander powder. Mix well.

4. Add the chopped tomatoes and continue to mix. Microwave on high for 2 minutes, stirring once every 1 minute.

5. Finally, add the boiled green peas and salt. Mix well and microwave on high for an additional 2 minutes, stirring once every 1 minute.

6. Serve the green peas masala immediately, garnished with chopped coriander.

name: Stuffed Ragi Roti
ingredients:
25g Ragi Flour
25g Whole Wheat Flour
10g Cauliflower
20g Fenugreek Leaves
1 Green Chilli
½ tsp Ginger
1 tsp Oil
Salt to Taste
nutrition:
Calories: 150-160 kcal
Protein: 4-5 grams
Carbohydrates: 25-30 grams
Fat: 3-4 grams
Fiber: 4-5 grams
method:
1. In a bowl, combine the ragi and whole wheat flour with enough warm water to make a dough. Set the dough aside.

2. Chop the cauliflower, fenugreek leaves, green chilli, and ginger into fine pieces.

3. In another bowl, mix all the chopped vegetables, adding salt to taste.

4. Divide the dough into equal parts and roll each part into a small circle (roti).

5. Place a small amount of the vegetable stuffing in the center of the circle, then bring together all the sides to the center and seal it tightly.

6. Roll out the stuffed dough again.

7. Heat a non-stick tawa (griddle) and cook the stuffed ragi roti with a little oil until it's golden brown on both sides.

8. Serve the stuffed ragi roti with coriander chutney or garlic chutney.

name: Rainbow Burrito Bowl
ingredients:
15g Bajra (Pearl Millet)
15g Brown Rice
15g Green Gram (Moong Dal)
20g Cabbage
20g Yellow Bell Pepper
20g Red Bell Pepper
20g Capsicum
30g Tomato
20g Onion
1 tsp Chopped Mint Leaves
1 tsp Lemon Juice
1 Finely Chopped Green Chilli
Salt to Taste
nutrition:
Calories: 160-180 kcal
Protein: 5-6 grams
Carbohydrates: 35-40 grams
Fat: 1-2 grams
Fiber: 7-8 grams
method:
1. Soak the bajra overnight. The next morning, pressure cook the soaked bajra for 8-10 whistles until it's soft and cooked. Drain any excess water and set it aside.

2. Cook the brown rice and boil the green gram separately. Allow them to cool and set them aside.

3. Chop all the vegetables, including cabbage, yellow bell pepper, red bell pepper, capsicum, tomato, and onion, into small cubes.

4. Chop the mint leaves and remove the seeds from the green chilli.

5. Take a large serving bowl and start layering the ingredients in the following order:
Begin with a layer of cooked bajra at the bottom.
Add a layer of capsicum.
Follow with a layer of boiled green gram.
Then, add a layer of chopped tomatoes.
Next, include a layer of yellow bell pepper.
Continue with a layer of cabbage.
Add a layer of red bell pepper.
Sprinkle the finely chopped green chilli.
Layer with brown rice.
Finish with a layer of grated carrot.

6. Sprinkle salt to taste, squeeze lemon juice over the top, and garnish with mint leaves.

7. Mix all the layers well before eating to combine the flavors.

name: Spinach Kati Roll With Chicken And Hung Curd
ingredients:
For Spinach Paratha:

30g Wheat Flour
30g Spinach
Salt to Taste
Water
1 tsp Oil

For Chicken Filling:

100g Boneless Chicken
½ tsp Black Pepper Powder
1 tsp Lemon Juice
Salt to Taste

For Hung Curd Filling:

50g Hung Curd (Greek Yogurt)
30g Finely Chopped Onion
30g Diced Cucumber
30g Sliced Capsicum
Salt to Taste
½ tsp Red Chilli Flakes
Pinch of Pepper
Pinch of Salt
nutrition:
Calories: 350-400 kcal
Protein: 30-35 grams
Carbohydrates: 35-40 grams
Fat: 12-15 grams
Fiber: 4-5 grams
method:
For Spinach Paratha:

1. In a bowl, combine wheat flour, salt, and finely chopped spinach.
2. Add water as needed to knead the dough. Set it aside for a while.
3. Roll out the dough into thin parathas, ensuring they have layers.
4. Cook the parathas on both sides with a little oil until they become golden brown. Set them aside.

For Chicken Filling:

1. Marinate the finely minced chicken with lemon juice, black pepper powder, and salt for 1 hour.
2. Heat a pan and cook the marinated chicken over low flame for about 10 minutes until it's cooked thoroughly.

For Hung Curd Filling:

1. In a bowl, beat the hung curd well.
2. Add red chilli flakes, pinch of pepper, pinch of salt, finely chopped onion, diced cucumber, and sliced capsicum. Mix well.

Assembling the Paratha:

1. Take one of the spinach parathas.
2. Spread the chicken filling evenly over the paratha.
3. Roll the paratha with the chicken filling inside.
4. Serve hot with mint chutney or hung curd.

name: Ridge Gourd-Mutton Keema With Phulka
ingredients:
For Mutton and Ridge Gourd Curry:

100g Ridge Gourd (Peeled and Diced)
100g Minced Mutton
20g Chopped Onion
25g Diced Tomato
¼ tsp Ginger-Garlic Paste
1 tsp Chopped Green Chillies
¼ tsp Coriander Powder
¼ tsp Red Chilli Powder
½ tsp Mustard Seeds
½ tsp Whole Cumin
¼ tsp Fenugreek Seeds
¼ tsp Turmeric Powder
Pinch of Asafoetida
1 tsp Coriander Leaves
2 tsp Oil
Salt to Taste
2 cups Water

For Roti:

30g Wheat Flour
2 tsp Oil
Pinch of Salt
1 cup Water
nutrition:
Calories: 500-550 kcal
Protein: 25-30 grams
Carbohydrates: 45-50 grams
Fat: 22-25 grams
Fiber: 4-5 grams
method:
For Mutton and Ridge Gourd Curry:

1. Heat a pressure cooker, add oil, mustard seeds, and let them splutter. Then add cumin and fenugreek seeds. Be cautious not to let the fenugreek seeds turn bitter.

2. Add asafoetida and turmeric powder, and sauté.

3. Add ginger-garlic paste and sauté until the raw smell disappears.

4. Add chopped onions and stir-fry until translucent.

5. Add minced mutton and sauté well.

6. Add red chilli powder and coriander powder. Mix well.

7. Add water and close the lid. Pressure cook for 2 whistles.

8. Release the pressure and open the cooker. Add ridge gourd and tomato. Mix well and cook for 6-7 minutes. Add water if needed.

9. Add salt and mix well. Add coriander leaves and green chillies. Cook for an additional 2-3 minutes.

For Roti:

1. Combine wheat flour, oil, salt, and water in a bowl.

2. Knead the dough and set aside for a while.

3. Divide the dough into equal portions and roll them out into thin rotis.

Serve the Mutton and Ridge Gourd Curry hot with the roti.

name: Fish Biryani With Capsicum Bharta
ingredients:
For Marinating Fish:

1 piece Katla Fish
¼ tsp Ginger-Garlic Paste
¼ tsp Red Chilli Powder
¼ tsp Turmeric Powder
¼ tsp Garam Masala
½ tsp Lemon Juice
¼ tsp Black Pepper
1 tsp Oil
Salt to Taste

For Rice:

30g Rice
1 tsp Oil
1 Clove
1 Cardamom
½ inch Cinnamon
½ tsp Ginger-Garlic Paste
30g Onion
¼ tsp Red Chilli Powder
30g Tomato
1 tbsp Curd
1 tsp Lemon Juice
1 tsp Finely Chopped Coriander Leaves
1 Green Chilli
1 Spring of Mint Leaves

For Capsicum Bharta:

100g Capsicum
20g Onion
20g Tomato
¼ tsp Mustard Seeds
¼ tsp Whole Cumin
1 Sprig Curry Leaves
1 Green Chilli
½ tsp Ginger Garlic Paste
¼ tsp Red Chilli Powder
¼ tsp Coriander Powder
¼ tsp Turmeric Powder
¼ tsp Roasted Cumin, Black Pepper, and Fenugreek Powder
¼ tsp Sugar
1 tsp Finely Chopped Coriander Leaves
1 tsp Oil
Salt to Taste
nutrition:
Calories: 600-650 kcal
Protein: 35-40 grams
Carbohydrates: 60-65 grams
Fat: 25-30 grams
Fiber: 5-6 grams
method:
For Marinating Fish:

1. In a bowl, combine ginger-garlic paste, red chilli powder, turmeric powder, garam masala powder, lemon juice, black pepper, salt, and mix well.

2. Apply the marinade generously to the fish and let it rest for some time.

3. Shallow fry the fish and set it aside.

For Rice:

1. In a casserole dish, heat oil. Add cinnamon, cardamom, and clove, and sauté.

2. Add chopped onion and sauté until translucent.

3. Add ginger-garlic paste and sauté until the raw aroma disappears.

4. Stir in red chilli powder, tomato, coriander leaves, mint leaves, and cook for a while.

5. Turn off the stove and add curd and lemon juice. Mix well.

6. Finally, add the shallow-fried fish and cook for a while.

7. In another vessel, boil water, add salt, rice, and cook until 70 percent done. Strain excess water and add the rice to the fish broth. Cover the casserole and cook for a while. Turn off the flame and let it rest.

For Capsicum Bharta:

1. Heat oil in a pressure cooker. Add mustard seeds and allow them to crackle. Then add whole cumin and sauté.

2. Add curry leaves and fry them.

3. Add finely chopped onion, ginger garlic paste and sauté for a while.

4. Add tomato, red chilli powder, turmeric powder, and coriander powder. Cook well.

5. Add capsicum and cook.

6. Then add the dry roasted powder of cumin, fenugreek, and pepper, and mix well.

7. Add some water, close the pressure cooker, and allow it to whistle once.

8. Open the cooker, add sugar and mix well. Finally, top it up with coriander leaves.

Serve the Fish Biryani with Capsicum Bharta.

name: Matta Tomato Rice
ingredients:
For Tomato Rice:

60g Matta Rice
100g Tomato
20g Onion
2 tsp Coriander Leaves
¼ tsp Garlic-Garlic Paste
1 small Green Chilli
¼ tsp Red Chilli Powder
¼ tsp Coriander Powder
¼ tsp Turmeric Powder
Pinch of Asafoetida
¼ tsp Mustard Seeds
¼ tsp Whole Cumin
Salt to Taste
1 tsp Oil
1 tsp Curry Leaves
3 cups Water

For Cucumber Raita:

100ml Curd
100g Cucumber
nutrition:
Calories: 280-300 kcal (excluding raita)
Protein: 5-6 grams (excluding raita)
Carbohydrates: 60-65 grams (excluding raita)
Fat: 2-3 grams (excluding raita)
Fiber: 2-3 grams (excluding raita)
method:
For Tomato Rice:

1. Soak Matta rice for at least 30-40 minutes.

2. Heat oil in a cooker. Add mustard seeds and allow them to crackle.

3. Add whole cumin, curry leaves, asafoetida, ginger-garlic paste, and sauté.

4. Then add chopped onion and green chilli. Sauté until the onion becomes translucent.

5. Add finely chopped tomato, red chilli powder, coriander powder, turmeric powder, salt, and mix well. Let it cook for a while.

6. Add the soaked rice and coriander leaves. Mix well.

7. Finally, add water, close the cooker, and cook for 3-4 whistles.

8. Serve hot with cucumber raita or salad.

For Cucumber Raita:

1. Peel and finely chop the cucumber.

2. In a bowl, whisk the curd until smooth.

3. Add the finely chopped cucumber to the curd and mix well.

Serve the Tomato Rice with Cucumber Raita.

name: Brown Rice Khichdi
ingredients:
½ cup Brown Rice, soaked for 30 minutes and drained
½ cup Masoor Dal, washed and drained
2 Cloves (Laung)
½ small stick Cinnamon
2 tsp Ghee
1 Bay Leaf
½ cup Finely Chopped Onion
1 tsp Ginger Garlic Paste
¼ tsp Turmeric Powder
½ cup Chopped Carrot
½ cup Green Peas
2 tsp Finely Chopped Green Chillies
Salt to Taste
nutrition:
Calories: 350-370 kcal
Protein: 15-18 grams
Carbohydrates: 65-70 grams
Fat: 5-7 grams
Fiber: 8-10 grams
method:
1. Wash and soak the brown rice for 30-45 minutes.

2. Wash and soak the masoor dal for 10 minutes.

3. Combine the cloves, cardamom, and cinnamon in a mortar and pestle and grind into a coarse powder.

4. Heat the ghee in a pressure cooker. Add a bay leaf and the prepared coarse powder. Sauté on medium flame for a few seconds.

5. Add the onions and sauté on medium flame for 2 minutes.

6. Add the ginger-garlic paste, turmeric powder, brown rice, masoor dal, carrots, green beans, and peas. Mix well and sauté on medium flame for 2 minutes.

7. Add 2 cups of water, green chillies, and salt. Mix well and pressure cook for 4 whistles.

8. Allow the steam to escape before opening the lid.

9. Serve immediately.

name: Palak Paneer Khichdi
ingredients:
30g Rice
100g Spinach (Pureed)
50g Paneer (Indian Cottage Cheese)
20g Onion
25g Tomato
¼ tsp Jeera (Cumin Seeds)
1 Cinnamon Stick
½ tsp Ginger Garlic Paste
¼ tsp Turmeric Powder
Salt to Taste
1 tsp Oil
Fresh Coriander for Garnishing
nutrition:
Calories: 250-270 kcal
Protein: 9-11 grams
Carbohydrates: 30-35 grams
Fat: 10-12 grams
Fiber: 4-6 grams
method:
1. Heat a pan or pressure cooker, add oil, jeera, and the cinnamon stick.

2. Add chopped onion, ginger-garlic paste, turmeric powder, and sauté until the onions turn translucent.

3. Stir in the spinach puree and paneer. Cook for some time.

4. Add salt to taste.

5. Add the soaked rice and the required amount of water. Close the lid and cook for 2 whistles (if using a pressure cooker).

6. Garnish with fresh coriander.

name: Lady'S Finger(Okra) Kadhi
ingredients:
5 Bhindi (Lady's Finger/Okra), de-stemmed and cut into half
10g Onion, sliced
1 tsp Oil for cooking the bhindi and onion
1 cup Curd (Dahi/Yogurt)
Pinch of Turmeric Powder (Haldi)
1 teaspoon Coriander Powder (Dhania)
¼ teaspoon Red Chilli Powder
Salt to Taste
nutrition:
Calories: 250-270 kcal
Protein: 8-10 grams
Carbohydrates: 20-25 grams
Fat: 12-14 grams
Fiber: 4-6 grams
method:
1. In a large saucepan, combine curd, turmeric powder, coriander powder, red chilli powder, and salt.

2. Add 1 cup of water and whisk it all together until it forms a smooth paste without lumps.

3. Place the saucepan on medium heat and bring the kadhi mixture to a boil. Keep whisking it continuously while it boils to ensure it stays smooth.

4. Once it starts to boil and thickens, reduce the heat to low and let the kadhi simmer.

5. In a separate wok, heat 1 teaspoon of oil. Add the cut bhindi (okra) and sliced onion, sprinkle some salt, and stir-fry on medium heat until the bhindi is cooked through and slightly crispy.

6. Add the roasted bhindi and onion into the kadhi and serve hot.

name: Protein Chila Wrap
ingredients:
60g Yellow Moong Dal (Split)
20g White Urad Dal (Whole)
½ inch Ginger, finely chopped
1 Green Chili, finely chopped
Salt, to taste
½ teaspoon Whole Cumin (Jeera)
Pinch of Turmeric Powder (Haldi)
Coriander Leaves, finely chopped
2 tsp Oil/Ghee

Ingredients for Paneer Filling:

60g Paneer (Homemade Cottage Cheese), grated
10g Onion, finely chopped
10g Tomatoes, finely chopped
1 Green Chili, finely chopped
1 teaspoon Chaat Masala Powder, for seasoning
Salt, to taste
Coriander Leaves, finely chopped
nutrition:
Calories: 220-240 kcal
Protein: 12-14 grams
Carbohydrates: 25-30 grams
Fat: 8-10 grams
Fiber: 4-6 grams
method:
For Moong Dal Chila:

1. Soak the moong dal and urad dal together for at least 6 hours or overnight.

2. Grind the soaked moong dal along with green chilies and ginger into a smooth batter, adding just enough water to grind the dal. The consistency should be like that of pancake batter (do not add too much water).

3. Add salt, whole cumin, turmeric powder, and finely chopped coriander leaves to the batter. Mix well.

4. Heat a skillet and pour a ladle full of moong dal chila batter in a circular fashion from the center going outwards, making a diameter of approximately 6 inches.

5. Drizzle oil/ghee around the spread chila batter. Allow the moong dal chila to cook over medium heat. You will notice brown spots appearing inside and around the sides. Let it get crisp, then flip and cook the chila for about a minute.

For Paneer Filling:

1. Combine grated paneer, finely chopped onion, tomatoes, green chili, chaat masala powder, and salt in a bowl. Mix well.

Assembling:

1. Remove the moong dal chila from the skillet, place it on a platter with the bottom side facing down.

2. Spread a scoop of the paneer filling along the center diameter of the chila.

3. Roll it lengthwise tightly. Cut the roll diagonally into 2 or 3 pieces and sprinkle more chaat masala on top.

name: Bengali Style Okra
ingredients:
1 cup Lady's Finger (Okra)
1 tsp Poppy Seeds
½ tsp Mustard Seeds
1 tsp Oil
1 ½ finely chopped Green Chili
Salt, to taste
A pinch of Sugar
¼ tsp Turmeric Powder
½ tsp Chili Powder
nutrition:
Calories: 80-90 kcal
Protein: 2-3 grams
Carbohydrates: 10-12 grams
Fat: 4-5 grams
Fiber: 3-4 grams
method:
1. Wash the lady's finger thoroughly and pat them dry completely on a kitchen towel. Trim off both ends and cut them into half horizontally. Keep aside.

2. Combine the poppy seeds and mustard seeds, then grind them in a mixer to a fine powder. Keep this powder aside.

3. Heat the oil in a non-stick kadhai or pan. Add the lady's finger and cook over medium flame for 8 to 10 minutes or until they become soft, stirring occasionally.

4. Add the finely chopped green chilies, prepared poppy seed and mustard seed powder, salt, sugar, turmeric powder, and chili powder. Mix well and continue to cook over medium flame for 2 to 3 minutes, stirring occasionally.

5. Serve the stir-fried lady's finger hot.

name: Paneer Bhapa
ingredients:
100g Paneer (Cottage Cheese)
¼ tsp Turmeric Powder
¼ tsp Chilli Powder
¼ tsp Coriander Powder
2 tsp Curd (Yogurt)
1 inch piece of Coconut
¼ tsp Mustard Seeds
¼ tsp Poppy Seeds
Salt, to taste
1 tsp Mustard Oil
2 Green Chillies
nutrition:
Calories: 260-280 kcal
Protein: 14-15 grams
Carbohydrates: 6-8 grams
Fat: 21-23 grams
Fiber: 2-3 grams
method:
1. In a blending jar, add coconut, mustard seeds, poppy seeds, and curd. Blend the mixture until it becomes a smooth paste.

2. Heat mustard oil in a pan. Add red chilli powder, turmeric powder, coriander powder, and salt. Sauté briefly until the raw smell of the spices is gone.

3. Add paneer cubes to the pan and sauté for a while until they become slightly brown.

4. In a tiffin box or a heatproof container, add the sautéed paneer, followed by the blended curd paste. Also, add green chillies.

5. Close the tiffin box or container tightly and steam it using a steam cooker for a few minutes.

6. Serve the Bhapa Paneer hot.

name: Doi Potol
ingredients:
100g Pointed Gourd (Parwal), peeled and cut into halves
¼ tsp Turmeric Powder
Salt, to taste
2 tsp Mustard Oil
1 Cardamom
2 Cloves (Laung)
1 Bay Leaf
1 small stick Cinnamon
½ cup Grated Onions
1 tsp Ginger Paste
½ tsp Green Chilli Paste
¼ tsp Chilli Powder
½ tsp Cumin Powder
½ tsp Garam Masala
½ tsp Coriander Powder
250g Curd (Yogurt)
½ tsp Sugar
nutrition:
Calories: 220-240 kcal
Protein: 6-7 grams
Carbohydrates: 21-23 grams
Fat: 12-14 grams
Fiber: 3-4 grams
method:
1. Boil enough water in a deep non-stick pan. Add the parwal (pointed gourd) and cover with a lid. Cook on a medium flame for 3 minutes. Then, drain.

2. In a deep bowl, combine the parwal with turmeric powder and a little salt. Mix gently and keep aside for 5 minutes.

3. Heat 1 tsp of mustard oil in a deep non-stick pan. Add the parwal turmeric mixture and sauté on a medium flame for 2 minutes. Remove and keep aside.

4. In the same non-stick pan, add the remaining 1 tsp of mustard oil. Add the cardamom, cloves, bay leaf, and cinnamon stick. Sauté for a few seconds.

5. Add the grated onions, ginger paste, and green chilli paste. Sauté on medium flame for 2 minutes.

6. Add the chilli powder, cumin powder, garam masala, and coriander powder. Sauté on medium flame for 2 minutes.

7. Add the curd, sugar, a little salt, and ½ cup water. Mix well and cook on a low flame for 2 minutes, while stirring continuously.

8. Add the cooked parwal turmeric powder mixture, cover with a lid, and cook on a slow flame for 3 to 4 minutes, stirring occasionally.

9. Serve the Pointed Gourd Curry hot.

name: Gobi Paneer Palya
ingredients:
40g Cauliflower
30g Paneer (chopped)
20g Onion (chopped)
25g Tomato (chopped)
½ tsp Ginger-Garlic Paste
1 tsp Oil
½ tsp Red Chilli Powder
¼ tsp Turmeric Powder
½ tsp Coriander Powder
Salt, to taste
nutrition:
Calories: 180-200 kcal
Protein: 8-9 grams
Carbohydrates: 7-8 grams
Fat: 12-14 grams
Fiber: 2-3 grams
method:
1. In a pressure cooker, add oil and chopped onions. After the onion turns golden in color, add ginger-garlic paste and cook until the raw smell goes away.

2. Add chopped tomatoes and the masala powders (red chilli powder, turmeric powder, and coriander powder). Cook until the tomato becomes soft.

3. Add cauliflower and mix well.

4. Add paneer and water. Close the lid of the pressure cooker and pressure cook for 3 whistles.

5. Serve the Paneer and Cauliflower Curry hot.

name: Methi Tomato Paneer
ingredients:
50g Fenugreek Leaves
50g Tomato Puree
50g Paneer (cubed)
25g Onion (finely chopped)
1 tsp Oil
½ tsp Ginger-Garlic Paste
½ tsp Red Chilli Powder
½ tsp Coriander Powder
½ tsp Garam Masala Powder
¼ tsp Turmeric Powder
Salt, to taste
nutrition:
Calories: 180-200 kcal
Protein: 7-8 grams
Carbohydrates: 8-9 grams
Fat: 12-14 grams
Fiber: 3-4 grams
method:
1. Wash and cut the fenugreek leaves. Cube the paneer and set aside.

2. In a pan, add oil and chopped onions. Fry the onions until they become translucent.

3. Add ginger-garlic paste and salt, and cook until the raw aroma disappears.

4. Stir in the tomato puree and the masala powders (red chilli powder, coriander powder, garam masala, and turmeric powder). Cook until the water from the tomato puree evaporates.

5. Add the cut fenugreek leaves and 50ml water. Stir well and cook.

6. When the gravy thickens, add the cubed paneer and cook until it's heated through.

7. Serve the Methi Paneer Curry hot.

name: Lucknowi Pulao With Dal
ingredients:
50g Rice
50g Mutton
1 Big Cardamom
2 Cloves
1 Star Anise
2 Cardamom Pods
1 Tej Patta (Indian Bay Leaf)
2 tsp Oil
½ tsp Ginger-Garlic Paste
1 Small Potato
10ml Curd (Yogurt)
Salt, to taste

For Dal (1 Serving):

30g Chana Dal (Split Bengal Gram)
15g Bottle Gourd
20g Onion, chopped
25g Tomato, chopped
½ tsp Red Chilli Powder
½ tsp Garam Masala
¼ tsp Turmeric Powder
Salt, to taste
1 tsp Oil

Nutritional Information (Approximate) for 1 Serving (Pulao and Dal combined):

Calories: 450-500 kcal
Protein: 15-18 grams
Carbohydrates: 60-65 grams
Fat: 15-18 grams
Fiber: 8-10 grams
method:
1. In a mixer, add the big cardamom, cloves, star anise, and grind them into a powder. Set it aside.

2. In a pot, bring 1 cup of water to a boil. Add salt, ½ tsp of oil, and a few drops of lemon juice. Then, add the washed rice and partially cook it. Drain and set aside.

3. In a pressure cooker, add 2 tsp of oil, tej patta, ginger-garlic paste, and the spice powder you prepared earlier. Stir well.

4. Add the diced potato and mutton, season with salt, and mix well. Add 1 cup of water, then pressure cook for 2 whistles.

5. In a separate vessel, create layers by alternating between the partially cooked rice and the mutton gravy. Top with saffron-infused curd and fried onions. Cook for 10 minutes.

6. Garnish with fried onions and serve hot with dal.

Method for Dal:

1. Pressure cook chana dal, bottle gourd, water, salt, and turmeric powder for 1 whistle.

2. In a separate pan, heat 1 tsp of oil, add chopped onions, and sauté until golden brown. Add ginger-garlic paste and spices.

3. Add chopped tomatoes and cook until softened.

4. Add the cooked dal, bottle gourd, and water. Simmer until well combined and serve hot with the pulao.

name: Kudampuli Fish Curry With Rice
ingredients:
100g Fish
¼ tsp Chilli Powder
¼ tsp Mustard Seeds
¼ tsp Fenugreek Seeds
¼ tsp Turmeric Powder
20g Shallots
2 Garlic Cloves
2 tsp Tamarind Paste
Few Curry Leaves
½ inch Ginger
2 tsp Oil
Salt, to taste
nutrition:
Calories: 150-200 kcal
Protein: 15-20 grams
Carbohydrates: 5-10 grams
Fat: 8-10 grams
Fiber: 1-2 grams
method:
1. Heat oil in a pan and add mustard seeds and fenugreek seeds. Allow the mustard seeds to crackle, then add curry leaves and sauté.

2. Add ginger, garlic, and shallots, and cook them until the shallots are golden brown.

3. Reduce the flame and add turmeric and red chilli powder. Add water and allow it to cook for a while until the raw aroma of the spices is gone.

4. Stir in the tamarind paste and mix well.

5. Add the fish and let it cook for about 10 minutes over low heat.

6. Serve hot with rice.

name: Quinoa Pulao With Lauki Raita
ingredients:
30g Quinoa
20g Finely Chopped Onion
20g Finely Chopped Tomato
20g Diced Carrot
20g Diced Beans
20g Capsicum
20g Finely Chopped Spinach
2 tsp Finely Chopped Coriander
2 tsp Finely Chopped Green Chilli
¼ tsp Ginger-Garlic Paste
¼ tsp Whole Cumin
¼ tsp Red Chilli Powder
¼ tsp Turmeric Powder
¼ tsp Coriander Powder
¼ tsp Garam Masala Powder
2 cups Water
Salt, to taste
1 tsp Oil
2 tsp Finely Grated Bottle Gourd
½ cup Curd (Yogurt)
nutrition:
Calories: 250-300 kcal
Protein: 8-10 grams
Carbohydrates: 40-45 grams
Fat: 6-8 grams
Fiber: 6-8 grams
method:
1. Heat oil in a pan and add whole cumin seeds. Sauté briefly.

2. Add chopped onion and ginger-garlic paste. Cook until the onion turns translucent.

3. Stir in tomatoes, carrots, beans, capsicum, spinach, and green chilli. Cook for a few minutes.

4. Add water, red chilli powder, coriander powder, turmeric powder, garam masala, and salt. Mix well and cook until the raw aroma of the spices dissipates.

5. Add washed quinoa and more water. Cook for about 10 minutes until the quinoa is cooked and has absorbed the flavors.

6. Finally, add chopped coriander leaves.

7. Serve hot with grated bottle gourd raita.

name: Healthy Stuffed Lucchi
ingredients:
For the Luchi:

30g Wheat Flour
Salt, to taste
1 tsp Oil
1¼ tsp Ghee (for cooking)

For the Filling:

30g Green Moong Dal (Soaked)
1 tsp Oil
