- Red chilli powder, to taste

- ¼ tsp turmeric

- ¼ tsp mustard seeds

- 1 tsp oil

Optional:

- 1 tsp roasted peanuts (crushed coarsely) or roasted sesame seeds
nutrition:
- Calories: Around 120 kcal

- Protein: Around 3g

- Fat: Around 4g

- Carbohydrates: Around 20g

- Fiber: Around 5g
method:
- Heat oil in a kadhai on low flame.

- Add mustard seeds and curry leaves. Let them sizzle.

- Add chopped onions and saute until translucent.

- Add beetroot cubes and stir for a few minutes.

- Season with salt, red chilli powder, and turmeric. Mix well.

- Cover and cook on low flame until the beetroot becomes soft.

- Check and stir occasionally to prevent sticking.

- Once cooked, consider adding roasted peanuts or sesame seeds before serving (optional).

name: Sukha Moong Dal
ingredients:
- 30g moong dal

- 1-2 cups water

- 1 tsp oil or ghee

- 1 big onion, chopped

- 1 big tomato, chopped

- ¼ tsp ginger paste or 1 tsp grated ginger

- ¼ tsp whole jeera (cumin seeds)

- Salt, to taste

- Red chilli powder, to taste

- ¼ tsp turmeric powder

- ¼ tsp amchur (dry mango powder)

- 1 green chilli, chopped
nutrition:
- Calories: Around 120 kcal

- Protein: Around 6g

- Fat: Around 3g

- Carbohydrates: Around 18g

- Fiber: Around 5g
method:
- Wash moong dal and place it in a cooker. Add water, salt, and ½ tsp turmeric.

- Cook until just before the first whistle. Allow the pressure cooker to release the pressure naturally.

- Heat oil in a kadhai. Add whole jeera. After a few seconds, add chopped onions and sauté until translucent.

- Add ginger. If it begins to burn, add 1 tbsp water and continue sautéing.

- Incorporate chopped tomatoes. After a few minutes, add a pinch of salt and turmeric.

- Mix in red chilli powder. Cook until the masala becomes soft and mashed.

- Add the cooked dal to the kadhai. Stir well to combine all ingredients.

- Transfer to a serving bowl.

- Garnish the top with ghee, amchur, and chopped green chilli.

- Serve.

name: Chana Dal With Bottle Gourd
ingredients:
- 30g dal (any variety)

- 100g Bottle gourd, cut into cubes

- 1 big onion, chopped

- 1 big tomato, chopped

- 1 tsp grated ginger

- 2-3 garlic cloves, chopped

- ½ tsp whole jeera (cumin seeds)

- Salt, to taste

- Red chilli powder, to taste

- ¼ tsp turmeric powder

- Pinch of asafoetida (optional)

- 1 tsp chopped coriander
nutrition:
- Calories: Around 120 kcal

- Protein: Around 6g

- Fat: Around 1g

- Carbohydrates: Around 24g

- Fiber: Around 5g
method:
- Heat oil in a cooker. Add whole jeera.

- After a few seconds, add chopped onions. Sauté for a few minutes.

- Add grated ginger and chopped garlic. Sauté until the onions turn translucent.

- Mix in chopped tomatoes. Sauté for a few minutes.

- Add salt, red chilli powder, and turmeric. Sauté until the masala becomes mashed. Add half of the chopped coriander and stir for a few minutes.

- Put dal into the cooker. Cook for 7-8 minutes on low flame after the first whistle. Let the pressure release naturally.

- Add the bottle gourd cubes. Mix and cook for one whistle. Let the pressure release naturally.

- Add the remaining coriander and mix.

- Serve.

name: Tava Cooked Fish
ingredients:
- 100g fish fillet

- ¼ tsp turmeric powder

- 1 tsp coriander powder

- ¼ tsp jeera (cumin) powder

- 1 tbsp red chilli powder

- 1 tsp garam masala

- 1 tsp ginger paste

- 1 tsp garlic paste

- 1 tsp lemon juice

- Salt, to taste

- 1 tsp chopped coriander leaves

- 2 tsp finely chopped curry leaves

- 1 tsp oil
nutrition:
- Calories: Around 200 kcal

- Protein: Around 20g

- Fat: Around 7g

- Carbohydrates: Around 10g

- Fiber: Around 2g
method:
- In a bowl, combine the fish with all the ingredients (except oil). Mix well and let it marinate for at least 1 hour.

- Heat oil on a tava (pan).

- Place the marinated fish onto the tava.

- Cook on low flame for 1-2 minutes on both sides.

- Cook each side for a longer time until the fish is thoroughly cooked.

- Serve with mint chutney and salad.

name: Spicy Chickpea'S (Chole)
ingredients:
- 30g chickpeas (soaked and cooked)

- 1 big onion (grated)

- 1 big tomato (chopped)

- 1 tsp ginger garlic paste

- 1 cinnamon stick

- 1 green cardamom

- 1 clove

- 1 bay leaf

- Pinch of turmeric

- 1 tsp red chilli powder

- 1 tsp garam masala

- Salt to taste (considering salt has been used while cooking chickpeas)

- 1 tbsp chole masala

- 1 tsp amchur (dried mango powder)

- ½ tsp kasuri methi (dry fenugreek leaves)

- 1 tsp oil/ghee
nutrition:
- Calories: Around 200 kcal

- Protein: Around 8g

- Fat: Around 4g

- Carbohydrates: Around 35g

- Fiber: Around 9g
method:
- Soak chickpeas for a minimum of 8 hours after washing thoroughly.

- Just before cooking, wash the chickpeas again and put them in the cooker. Add 3-4 cups of water and salt. Cook for 30 minutes on low heat after the first whistle. Allow it to open naturally.

Method:

- Heat oil in a kadai.

- Add bay leaf, cardamom, clove, and cinnamon. Stir for a few seconds.

- Add ginger garlic paste. Sauté on low heat until the raw smell disappears.

- Add grated onions. Sauté until the onions turn brown.

- Add tomatoes, a pinch of salt, turmeric, and garam masala. Sauté until the masala is well combined.

- Add the chole masala. Sauté until the oil separates, and the masala becomes brown. You can add a tablespoon of water in between to prevent the masala from sticking to the bottom of the kadhai.

- Add the cooked chickpeas along with the water used for cooking.

- Mash some chickpeas to thicken the gravy to the desired consistency.

- Adjust the consistency as required.

- Add kasuri methi leaves and amchur. Mix well.

- Done.

name: Prawn Do Pyaza
ingredients:
- 100g prawns

- 1 onion (sliced)

- 1 tomato (chopped)

- ¼ tsp ginger paste

- ½ tsp garlic paste

- 1 chopped green chili

- Salt to taste

- ¼ tsp red chili powder

- ¼ tsp turmeric

- 1 green cardamom

- 1 cinnamon stick

- 1 clove

- 1 bay leaf

- 1 tsp oil (preferably mustard oil)

- 1 tbsp chopped coriander leaves
nutrition:
- Calories: Around 150 kcal

- Protein: Around 15g

- Fat: Around 5g

- Carbohydrates: Around 10g

- Fiber: Around 2g
method:
- Heat oil in a kadhai (preferably mustard oil).

- Add cardamom, cinnamon, clove, and bay leaf. Stir for a few seconds.

- Add onions. Sauté until translucent.

- Add chopped green chili and stir.

- Mix in ginger-garlic paste, and sauté until the raw smell disappears.

- Add chopped tomatoes, and stir for a few minutes.

- Add salt, turmeric, and red chili powder. Stir until the tomatoes become soft.

- Add the raw prawns and stir on high flame for a few minutes.

- Once the prawns are cooked, add chopped coriander. Mix well and keep on low flame for a few more minutes.

- Ready to serve.

name: Chana Masala Paratha
ingredients:
For Boiling Chickpeas:

- 1 cup raw chickpeas

- A pinch of baking soda

- Salt (to taste)

For the Masala:

- 1 ½ tbsp ghee/oil

- 1 tsp whole cumin (jeera)

- ½ tsp red chili powder

- 1 tsp amchur (dried mango powder)

- 1 tsp roasted cumin powder

- 1 ½ tsp coriander powder

- ½ tsp Garam masala

- ¼ tsp hing (asafoetida)

- Salt (to taste)

- 1 large onion, chopped

- Green chilies (chopped, to taste)

- ½ cup chopped coriander leaves

- ½ tsp ginger paste
nutrition:
- Calories: Around 300 kcal

- Protein: Around 10g

- Fat: Around 8g

- Carbohydrates: Around 50g

- Fiber: Around 8g
method:
- Wash the chickpeas and soak them overnight or for 7-8 hours.

- In a pressure cooker, add the soaked chickpeas with a pinch of baking soda and some salt. Pressure cook for 30 minutes on low flame after the first whistle. Let the cooker release pressure naturally.

- In a kadhai or frying pan, heat ghee/oil. Warm it a little.

- Add hing and whole cumin. After a few seconds, add all the dry masalas (red chili powder, amchur, roasted cumin powder, coriander powder, Garam masala). Stir well for less than a minute.

- Add the boiled chickpeas along with ginger paste. Mix well and add salt according to taste. Cook until the gravy dries up.

- Add chopped onions, green chilies, and coriander leaves. Mix and mash the chickpeas. Allow it to cool down completely.

For Making Parathas:

- Take a small ball of dough, roll it out, and place a portion of the chickpea masala in the center. Close the edges and carefully roll it out into a paratha.

- Heat a tava or pan, cook the stuffed paratha on both sides until it becomes slightly brown. Smear some ghee or oil on top while cooking.

- Serve hot with chutney or raita.

name: Hara Bhara Fried Rice
ingredients:
- 1 cup cooked rice

- ½ tsp chopped garlic

- ½ tsp green chilies

- 100g chopped onion

- 20g finely chopped carrot

- 20g thinly sliced capsicum

- 20g finely chopped cabbage

- 50g spring onion

- ⅛ tsp pepper

- ⅛ tsp sugar (optional)

- ½ tsp dark soya sauce

- ½ tsp vinegar

- Salt according to taste

- 1 tsp oil
nutrition:
- Calories: Around 290 kcal

- Carbohydrates: Around 50 g

- Protein: Around 5 g

- Fat: Around 6 g

- Fiber: Around 5 g
method:
- In a kadhai or wok, heat oil over medium heat.

- Add chopped garlic and stir-fry for a few seconds.

- Stir in the green chilies for a brief moment.

- Add chopped onions and sauté for a few seconds until translucent.

- Toss in carrots and stir-fry briefly.

- Add thinly sliced capsicum and continue to stir-fry.

- Introduce chopped cabbage and stir-fry for a few seconds.

- Season with pepper.

- Add the cooked rice and chopped spring onions, gently mixing everything.

- Sprinkle salt and optional sugar, stir-fry for a few seconds. Adjust salt as per taste.

- Pour in the dark soya sauce and vinegar, gently toss for a few seconds.

- Once done, garnish with additional chopped spring onions.

name: Egg Fried Rice
ingredients:
- ½ tsp chopped garlic

- ½ tsp green chili

- 100g chopped onion

- 20g finely chopped carrot

- 20g thinly sliced capsicum

- 20g finely chopped cabbage

- 50g spring onion

- ⅛ tsp pepper

- ⅛ tsp sugar (optional)

- ½ tsp dark soya sauce

- ½ tsp vinegar

- ¼ tsp red chili flakes

- Salt according to taste

- 1 tsp oil

- 1 egg

- 1 cup cooked rice
nutrition:
- Calories: Around 270 kcal

- Carbohydrates: Around 35 g

- Protein: Around 7 g

- Fat: Around 10 g

- Fiber: Around 3 g
method:
- In a kadhai or wok, heat oil over medium heat.

- Add chopped garlic, stir-fry for a few seconds.

- Stir in the chopped green chili for a brief moment.

- Add chopped onions and sauté until translucent.

- Toss in carrots and stir-fry briefly.

- Add thinly sliced capsicum, cabbage, and continue to stir-fry.

- Crack the egg into the mixture, sprinkle red chili flakes, and cook until the egg is partially set.

- Season with pepper.

- Add the cooked rice and chopped spring onions, gently mixing everything.

- Sprinkle salt and optional sugar, stir-fry for a few seconds. Adjust salt as per taste.

- Pour in the dark soya sauce and vinegar, gently toss for a few seconds.

- Once done, garnish with additional chopped spring onions.

name: Vegetable Paneer Fried Rice
ingredients:
- 50g paneer

- 1 cup cooked rice

- ½ tsp chopped garlic

- ½ tsp green chilies

- 100g chopped onion

- 20g finely chopped carrot

- 20g capsicum thinly sliced

- 20g finely chopped cabbage

- 50g spring onion

- ⅛ tsp pepper

- ⅛ tsp sugar (optional)

- ½ tsp dark soya sauce

- ½ tsp vinegar

- Salt according to taste

- 1 tsp oil
nutrition:
- Calories: Around 300 kcal

- Carbohydrates: Around 40 g

- Protein: Around 8 g

- Fat: Around 11 g

- Fiber: Around 4 g
method:
- In a kadhai, heat oil over medium heat.

- Add the chopped garlic, stir-fry for a few seconds.

- Stir in the chopped green chilies for a brief moment.

- Add chopped onions and sauté until translucent.

- Toss in carrots, stir-fry briefly.

- Add thinly sliced capsicum, cabbage, and continue to stir-fry.

- Sprinkle pepper and sugar (if using). Stir-fry for a few seconds.

- Add the cooked rice and chopped spring onions, gently mixing everything.

- Sprinkle salt, dark soya sauce, and vinegar. Stir-fry gently for a few seconds. Set aside.

- In another pan, heat oil over medium heat.

- Chop paneer cubes, season with salt and pepper. Stir-fry until slightly golden brown.

- Add the stir-fried paneer cubes to the prepared fried rice.

- Garnish with additional chopped spring onions.

name: Chicken Fried Rice
ingredients:
For the Chicken Marination:

- 50g chicken

- 1 medium-sized egg

- ½ tsp corn flour (optional)

- Salt (to taste)

- ⅛ tsp pepper

For the Fried Rice:

- 1 cup cooked rice

- ½ tsp chopped garlic

- ½ tsp green chilies

- 100g chopped onion

- 20g finely chopped carrot

- 20g capsicum thinly sliced

- 20g finely chopped cabbage

- 50g spring onion

- ⅛ tsp pepper

- ⅛ tsp sugar (optional)

- ½ tsp dark soya sauce

- ½ tsp vinegar

- Salt (to taste)

- 1 tsp oil
nutrition:
- Calories: Around 350 kcal

- Carbohydrates: Around 50 g

- Protein: Around 20 g

- Fat: Around 10 g

- Fiber: Around 5 g
method:
For the Fried Rice:

- In a kadhai, heat oil.

- Add chopped garlic, stir-fry for a few seconds.

- Stir in the chopped green chilies for a brief moment.

- Add sliced onions, stir-fry until translucent.

- Toss in carrots, capsicum, cabbage, and continue to stir-fry.

- Sprinkle pepper and sugar (if using). Stir-fry briefly.

- Add the cooked rice and chopped spring onions. Gently mix everything.

- Sprinkle salt, dark soya sauce, and vinegar. Stir-fry gently for a few seconds. Set aside.

For Marinating and Stir-frying the Chicken:

- In a bowl, mix egg, cornflour, salt, and pepper. Add chicken, coat well, and set aside.

- Heat a pan, add oil, and stir-fry the marinated chicken until cooked.

- Add the cooked chicken to the fried rice.

- Garnish with additional spring onions.

name: Soya Nuggets Fried Rice
ingredients:
- 50g soya chunks (boiled and water squeezed out)

- 1 cup cooked rice

- ½ tsp chopped garlic

- ½ tsp green chilli

- 100g chopped onion

- 20g finely chopped carrot

- 20g capsicum thinly sliced

- 20g finely chopped cabbage

- 50g spring onion

- ⅛ tsp pepper

- ⅛ tsp sugar (optional)

- ½ tsp dark soya sauce

- ½ tsp vinegar

- Salt (to taste)

- 1 tsp oil
nutrition:
- Calories: Around 300 kcal

- Carbohydrates: Around 40 g

- Protein: Around 20 g

- Fat: Around 7 g

- Fiber: Around 6 g
method:
Fried Rice:

- In a Kadhai, heat oil.

- Warm the oil a little.

- Add the chopped garlic, stir-fry for a few seconds.

- Stir in the chopped green chilli for a few seconds.

- Add the sliced onions and stir-fry for a few seconds.

- Add carrots and stir-fry for a few seconds.

- Add the sliced capsicum and stir-fry for a few seconds.

- Add cabbage and stir-fry for a few seconds.

- Sprinkle pepper and stir-fry briefly.

- Add the cooked rice, stir-fry gently.

- Mix in the chopped spring onions. Stir-fry for a few seconds.

- Add salt and sugar, stir-fry for a few seconds. (Use less salt as soya sauce will be added).

- Pour in the soya sauce and vinegar. Stir-fry gently for a few seconds. Set aside.

Preparing Soya Chunks:

- Take a pan, add oil and spread it.

- When the oil is warm, add a little chopped garlic to the pan and then put in the soya nuggets.

- Cook until the soya chunks turn crisp.

Combining:

- Add the crispy soya chunks to the prepared fried rice.

- Garnish with chopped spring onions.

name: Sukha Kala Chana
ingredients:
- 30g dried chickpeas (chana)

- 100g sliced onion

- ½ tsp ginger paste

- ½ tsp garlic paste

- 50g chopped tomatoes

- Red chilli powder (to taste)

- ¼ tsp turmeric powder

- 1 green chilli

- Salt (to taste)

- 1 tsp oil
nutrition:
- Calories: Around 200 kcal

- Carbohydrates: Around 25 g

- Protein: Around 7 g

- Fat: Around 7 g

- Fiber: Around 6 g
method:
- Preparation:
- Wash and soak the dried chickpeas for 7-8 hours.

- In a pressure cooker, add soaked chickpeas and sliced onions.

- Include ginger garlic paste, turmeric, red chilli powder, and salt.

- Add the whole slit green chilli.

- Pour in the oil and required water.

- Pressure Cooking:
- Pressure cook the chickpeas. After the first whistle, reduce the flame to low and cook for 30-35 minutes.

- Let the cooker release pressure naturally.

- Sautéing:
- Sauté the chickpeas until they achieve a nice brown color and all the ingredients are well combined.

- If needed, let excess water dry. You can add 1-2 teaspoons of water to continue sautéing.

- Garnish with coriander leaves.

- Serving:
- Serve Chana Masala with roti, salad, and lime.

name: Veg Chana Masala
ingredients:
- 30g chickpeas

- Pinch of baking soda (optional)

- Pinch of asafoetida (optional)

- ¼ tsp whole cumin seeds (jeera)

- Red chilli powder (according to taste)

- ⅛ tsp coriander powder (dhaniya powder)

- ⅛ tsp cumin powder (jeera powder)

- ⅛ tsp turmeric powder

- ⅛ tsp garam masala

- ⅛ tsp amchur (dry mango powder)

- 100g grated onion

- 1 tsp ginger paste

- ¼ tsp garlic paste

- 50g grated tomatoes

- 50g tomato, cut into big cubes

- Few pounded green chillies

- Few whole slit green chillies

- 1 tsp chopped coriander (for garnish)

- Salt (to taste)

- 1 tsp oil
nutrition:
- Calories: Around 200 kcal

- Carbohydrates: Around 25 g

- Protein: Around 6 g

- Fat: Around 7 g

- Fiber: Around 5 g
method:
Preparation:

- Wash and soak chickpeas overnight or for 7-8 hours.

- Cook the chickpeas in a pressure cooker for 30 minutes on low flame after the 1st whistle. Let it release pressure naturally.

Cooking:

- In a Kadhai, heat oil/ghee, let it warm a little.

- Add asafoetida and whole cumin seeds; let the cumin splutter.

- Sauté grated onion until beige in color.

- Add ginger-garlic paste, sauté till the raw smell goes.

- Add salt, red chilli powder, turmeric, coriander powder, and cumin powder. Add a few tablespoons of water to make a paste.

- Add grated tomatoes and pounded green chillies. Sauté for a few minutes.

- Add garam masala. Sauté until the masala turns brown.

- Add amchur powder, sauté for a few minutes, then add boiled chickpeas.

- Let the gravy bubble; cook on low flame till the gravy thickens and the masala infuses.

Tadka (Tempering):

- In a separate pan, heat oil.

- When warm, add cumin seeds, slit green chillies, and cubed tomatoes.

- Stir for a few seconds, then add this to the cooked chickpeas in the Kadhai.

Finishing:

- Use the residual masala in the tadka pan: add some cooked chickpeas, then add it back to the rest of the chickpeas.

- Finally, add crushed Kasuri methi leaves to the chickpeas.

- Garnish with chopped coriander and serve.

name: Morning Elixir Drink
categories: Pre Breakfast, Morning Snack, Sim's Family Recipes
ingredients:
- 1 nutmeg, grated

- 2 star anise

- 2 black cardamom pods

- 1 teaspoon pepper

- 1 teaspoon cloves

- 2-inch piece of Malathi sticks (licorice root)

- Fresh turmeric (or 1 tablespoon powder)

- 1 large piece cinnamon bark

- Ginger (as required)
nutrition:
- Calories: Around 20 Kcal

- Fat: 0g

- Protein: 0g

- Fiber: 0g
method:
- Grind the dry spices along with ginger into a fine powder and store it in the fridge for an extended shelf life.

- To prepare the drink, take approximately 1 heaped teaspoon of the spice mixture and add it to a cup of water.

- Boil the water with the spice mixture for 5 to 10 minutes. If available, add tulsi (holy basil) or beetle leaf to enhance flavor.

- Squeeze the juice of half a lime into the drink and consume it while it's warm.

- Optionally, sweeten with a bit of honey, although caution is advised when buying honey as many commercial brands might not be pure and could just be sugar syrup.

This recipe can be adjusted based on spice availability. For occasional consumption, you can use smaller quantities of each spice or make a larger batch of the dry spice mixture and store it for long-term use.

name: Creamy Mango Popsicle
categories: Morning Snack, Sim's Family Recipes, Evening Snack
ingredients:
- 125 ml homemade hung curd (made from 250 ml full-fat milk)

- 1 small Alphonso or sweet mango (approx. 100 grams)

- Jaggery/sugar to taste (if required)

- 1-2 tablespoons condensed milk or milk powder (optional)
nutrition:
- Calories: Around 220 Kcal

- Fat: Around 8 g

- Protein: Around 9 g

- Fiber: Around 2 g
method:
- Prepare Hung Curd: Turn 250 ml full-fat milk into homemade curd. Once set, refrigerate immediately to avoid sourness.

- Drain Excess Water: Transfer the curd to a muslin cloth, creating a potli, and place it on a sieve or big strainer over a bowl. Keep in the fridge to allow excess water to drip out. Leave it refrigerated until the curd thickens (about a day) to achieve a creamy consistency, similar to cream cheese.

- Blend Ingredients: Combine the hung curd with chopped sweet mangoes in a blender. Blend thoroughly.

- Adjust Sweetness: Taste the mixture; if needed, add sugar/jaggery to reach the desired sweetness. Blend again to incorporate.

- Aerate the Mixture: Blend on high speed to infuse air into the mixture. This step contributes to a smoother texture.

- Pour into Moulds: Pour the mixture into moulds, insert sticks or forks, and leave them in the freezer overnight to set.

name: Coconut Rice
ingredients:
- 2 tablespoons ghee/oil

- 1 cup rice (washed and soaked for at least 30 minutes)

- 1 cup thick coconut milk (from a can or packet)

- 1 teaspoon mustard seeds

- 2 green cardamom pods

- 2 pieces cinnamon stick

- 3 cloves

- 1 bay leaf (optional)

- 2 tomatoes, cut into quarters

- 5-6 curry leaves

- 1 large onion, sliced

- 2 onions, quartered

- 2-3 green chilies, chopped (optional)

- 1/2 teaspoon turmeric powder

- Salt to taste
nutrition:
- Calories: Around 450 Kcal

- Fat: Around 20 g

- Protein: Around 8 g

- Fiber: Around 4 g
method:
- Wash the rice thoroughly and let it soak for at least 30 minutes.

- In a pressure cooker, heat the ghee/oil.

- Add mustard seeds, cardamom, cloves, and cinnamon stick. Let the mustard seeds splutter.

- Add the quartered tomatoes and stir for a few minutes until they start to soften. Avoid overcooking.

- If using, add the bay leaf at this point. Then incorporate the curry leaves and stir briefly.

- Sauté the sliced onions until slightly translucent. Add the chopped green chilies (if using) and stir for a few seconds.

- Add the quartered onions, gently stirring until they slightly soften. Keep them intact without separating the layers (pearl onions can be used).

- Stir in the soaked rice, mix gently, and sauté for a few minutes.

- Add salt to taste and turmeric powder. Mix well.

- Pour in the coconut milk and gently combine everything.

- Close the pressure cooker and cook for 1 whistle. Remove from heat and allow the cooker to release pressure naturally.

- Let the rice rest in the cooker for a while before serving.

- Serve plain or with accompaniments like salad, raita, or chicken masala.

name: Mattar Chaat
ingredients:
- 4-5 tablespoons cooked white peas (mattar)

- 1/2 onion, chopped

- 1/2 cucumber, chopped

- 1/2 tomato, chopped

- Few green chilies, chopped (according to taste)

- 1 1/2 inch piece of ginger, chopped

- 1-2 tablespoons chopped coriander leaves

- 4-5 tablespoons tamarind sauce

- Few drops of lemon juice
nutrition:
- Calories: Around 200 Kcal

- Fat: Around 2 g

- Protein: Around 6 g

- Fiber: Around 6 g
method:
Preparing Cooked White Peas:

- Soak the white peas overnight.

- Drain the soaked peas and place them in a pressure cooker.

- Add double the amount of water (double the raw weight of peas).

- Pressure cook for 10 to 15 minutes on low flame.

- Carefully release the pressure. If the peas are not cooked, continue cooking without the lid until done. Set aside until needed.

Assembling the Chaat (One Portion)

- Finely chop all the vegetables.

- Take 4-5 tablespoons of cooked white peas in a bowl.

- Add chopped onion, cucumber, tomato, ginger, green chilies, and coriander to the peas.

- Mix in 3-4 tablespoons of tamarind sauce.

- Add a small amount of chaat masala and mix everything well.

- Garnish with additional chopped ingredients and a few drops of lemon juice.

Tamarind Sauce:

- Soak one ball of tamarind in 1/2 cup water until it forms a thick sauce.

- Strain the tamarind pulp and keep it in a bowl.

- Add black salt and red chili powder according to taste.

- Mix in 1/4 teaspoon roasted cumin powder, 1/4 teaspoon chaat masala, and 1/4 teaspoon roasted coriander powder.

name: Sticky Chinese Rice
ingredients:
- 50g rice

- Half packet of mushrooms

- 1 capsicum, diced

- 2 carrots, diced

- 1 cup peas

- 1 cup chicken, cut into small pieces

- 1 whole pod of garlic, chopped

- Stock (3 times the volume of rice, should be wet)

- Salt to taste

(Note: Vegetable quantity can be doubled if this is the primary vegetable serving in the meal)
nutrition:
- Calories: Around 400 Kcal

- Fat: Around 7 g

- Protein: Around 25 g

- Fiber: Around 8 g
method:
- Heat oil in a pressure cooker.

- Add finely chopped garlic and sauté until it slightly changes color.

- Incorporate the chicken and stir for a minute.

- Add the vegetables one by one, cooking each for about 30 seconds before adding the next - start with carrots, then peas, followed by mushrooms, and finally, capsicum.

- Pour in the stock.

- Wash and drain the rice, then add it to the cooker. Stir for a few minutes.

- Taste the water for seasoning, ensuring it is slightly salty.

- Pressure cook on high for one whistle until done.

name: Paneer Vegetable Manchurian
ingredients:
- 3 tablespoons oil

- 12-15 big pods of chopped garlic

- 5-6 (or more) chopped green chillies

- 5-6 chopped coriander leaves

- 1 big carrot, cut into semi circles

- 8-10 mushrooms, chopped

- 1/2 green capsicum, sliced

- 1/2 red capsicum, sliced

- 1/2 cup cabbage, cut into cubes

- 1 tomato, thickly chopped

- 100-150 grams paneer, cut into cubes or strips

- 2-3 tablespoons chopped spring onions

- 2 teaspoons dark soya sauce

- 1 teaspoon tomato sauce

- 1 cup hot water

- 1 teaspoon cornflour

- Salt to taste
nutrition:
- Calories: Around 350 Kcal

- Fat: Around 25 g

- Protein: Around 15 g

- Fiber: Around 7 g
method:
- Heat oil in a kadhai or wok.

- Once the oil is slightly warm, add chopped garlic and cook on low flame until the raw smell of garlic dissipates.

- Add chopped green chillies and stir for 20-30 seconds.

- Toss in the chopped coriander leaves and stir briefly.

- Add vegetables one by one, cooking each for about 30 seconds on high flame before adding the next one. Start with carrots, followed by mushrooms, then sliced capsicums, and cabbage.

- Stir in the soya sauce and mix well.

- Add chopped tomatoes and stir.

- Gently add the paneer cubes, being careful not to break them.

- Mix 1 teaspoon of cornflour in one cup of hot water, then slowly pour it into the kadhai.

- Reduce the flame and cook until the sauce thickens.

- Mix in chopped spring onions.

- Add tomato sauce, gently mix, and check for salt; adjust according to taste.

- Cook for a few seconds more.

- Remove from heat and serve hot.

name: Masala Stuffed Lady'S Finger
ingredients:
- 3 tablespoons oil

- 1/2 kg long lady's fingers (okra)

For Masala:

- 1 teaspoon coriander powder (dhaniya powder)

- 1 teaspoon cumin powder (jeera powder)

- 1 teaspoon garam masala

- 1 teaspoon amchur (dry mango powder)

- 1 teaspoon red chili powder (adjust to taste)

- 1 teaspoon black salt (adjust to taste, add white salt if needed)
nutrition:
- Calories: Around 250 Kcal

- Fat: Around 20 g

- Protein: Around 5 g

- Fiber: Around 7 g
method:
- Cut the heads of the lady's fingers and make a slit in the middle, being careful not to cut through the ends.

- Fill each lady's finger with the prepared masala mixture.

- Heat oil in a kadhai (Indian wok).

- Once the oil is warm, add the masala-filled lady's fingers and cook on low flame.

- Stir occasionally to prevent sticking and ensure even cooking.

- When the lady's fingers are cooked, remove from heat and serve.

Notes:

- In a separate pan, coat with a bit of oil.

- Add thickly sliced onions or whole baby onions.

- Sprinkle a pinch of salt and sauté until the onions turn translucent.

- Add these sautéed onions to the cooked masala-stuffed lady's fingers and mix well.

name: Chilli Paneer With Carrot And Capsicum
ingredients:
- 100-150 grams paneer, sliced into strips

- 1/2 red capsicum, cut into strips

- 1/2 green capsicum, cut into strips

- 1 big carrot, cut into thin strips

- 1 medium-size onion, sliced

- 4-5 green chillies, cut in halves

- 2 tablespoons chopped spring onions

- 10-12 pods of garlic, chopped

- Salt to taste

- 1/4 teaspoon pepper

- 2 tablespoons light soy sauce

- 1 teaspoon dark soy sauce

- 1 teaspoon tomato sauce

- 3 tablespoons oil
nutrition:
- Calories: Around 350 Kcal

- Fat: Around 25 g

- Protein: Around 10 g

- Fiber: Around 5 g
method:
- Heat oil in a kadhai (Indian wok) and once warm, add chopped garlic. Stir until the raw smell disappears.

- Add green chillies and stir for a minute.

- Toss in the sliced carrots and stir for another minute.

- Add the sliced onions and mix for 30-40 seconds.

- Now, add both the red and green capsicum strips and stir-fry for a few minutes.

- Add the sliced paneer strips and mix gently.

- In a bowl, combine salt, pepper, light soy sauce, dark soy sauce, and tomato sauce. Pour this mixture into the kadhai with the paneer and vegetables.

- Gently mix everything and let it cook for about 2 minutes.

- Add chopped spring onions and serve hot.

name: My Mom'S Green Chutney
ingredients:
- 200 grams coriander leaves (dhaniya patta)

- Salt to taste (approximately 1/4 teaspoon)

- 8-10 green chillies

- 8 pods of garlic

- 1 piece ginger

- 1 tablespoon lemon juice

- 2 to 2 1/2 teaspoons sugar
nutrition:
- Calories: Around 20 Kcal

- Fat: Around 1 g

- Protein: Around 1 g

- Fiber: Around 3 g
method:
- Ensure the coriander leaves and green chillies are washed and dried.

- Add all the ingredients (coriander leaves, green chillies, garlic, ginger, salt, lemon juice, sugar) to a grinder.

- Grind all the ingredients until you achieve a smooth mixture.

- Store the chutney in an airtight container in the refrigerator.

- Avoid using a wet spoon while serving from the main jar to maintain freshness.

name: Bhindi Chutney
categories: Lunch, Dinner, Evening Snack, Sim's Family Recipes
ingredients:
- 50 grams lady's finger (okra)

- 10 grams groundnut

- 1 green chilli

- 1 pod garlic

- 1/8 teaspoon jeera (cumin seeds)

- Salt according to taste

- 1/4 teaspoon oil
nutrition:
- Calories: Around 60 Kcal

- Fat: Around 4 g

- Protein: Around 3 g

- Fiber: Around 3 g
method:
- Heat a pan and dry roast the groundnuts. Once roasted, let them cool and remove the outer husk by rubbing them in your palm.

- Heat the pan again, add oil, and sauté the lady's finger for 5-10 minutes until cooked.

- Add cumin seeds (jeera) and green chilli to the pan and continue cooking for a short duration. Then turn off the stove.

- In a blender jar, combine the roasted groundnuts, cooked lady's finger mixture, salt, and garlic.

- Blend the ingredients into a smooth paste and serve.

name: Khatta Meetha Baigan
ingredients:
- 300 grams small brinjal (eggplant)

- 1 medium-size onion

- 10-12 curry leaves

- 3-4 cloves of garlic

- Red chilli powder and salt to taste

- Pinch of whole cumin seeds (jeera)

- 13-14 fenugreek seeds (methi dana)

- 1 1/2 - 2 teaspoons sugar or jaggery

- 1/4 level teaspoon powdered roasted cumin (jeera) powder

- Juice from 1/2 a big lime or tamarind pulp

- 1 tablespoon oil
nutrition:
- Calories: Around 200 Kcal

- Fat: Around 10 g

- Protein: Around 3 g

- Fiber: Around 6 g
method:
- Cut the small brinjals into quarters without cutting through the end. Rub them with salt and turmeric, and set aside.

- Heat oil in a kadhai (Indian wok).

- Add the brinjals and cook until they become brown and soft. Remove and set aside.

- Pound the garlic and grate the onion.

- In the same kadhai, add a little oil and then add fenugreek seeds (methi dana) and cumin seeds (jeera).

- Stir in the curry leaves and cook for a minute.

- Add grated onion and cook until it turns brown. Then add pounded garlic.

- Cook the mixture until the onions become brown, adding a little water to achieve a paste-like consistency.

- Add red chilli powder and salt as per taste and stir.

- Add the cooked brinjal to the masala and let it cook further.

- Once cooked, add lime juice or tamarind pulp, sugar or jaggery, and roasted cumin powder. Mix well and let it cook for a couple of minutes.

- Serve hot with rice and dal.

name: Quick Cabbage & Peas
ingredients:
- Cabbage, cut into thin strips

- 1/2 cup peas

- 2 bay leaves

- 1/2 teaspoon whole jeera (cumin seeds)

- 2 teaspoons grated ginger

- 2 green cardamom pods

- 1-inch cinnamon stick, pounded

- 1 tablespoon oil

- Green chillies (optional)

- Salt, turmeric, and red chilli powder according to taste
nutrition:
- Calories: Around 120 Kcal

- Fat: Around 6 g

- Protein: Around 4 g

- Fiber: Around 6 g
method:
- Heat oil in a kadhai or pan.

- Add bay leaves to infuse flavor into the oil.

- Add cumin seeds (jeera) and grated ginger. Be cautious as the moisture in the ginger may cause the oil to splutter.

- Add 4 to 5 tablespoons of water to create a paste-like consistency and allow the ginger to cook.

- Optionally, add slit green chillies at this stage.

- Add the cabbage, mix, and cook for a minute.

- Season with salt, turmeric powder, and red chilli powder. Mix well.

- Add peas, cover, and cook until they are done.

- Pound the cinnamon and green cardamom in a mortar and pestle.

- Once the cabbage and peas are cooked, add the pounded cinnamon and cardamom. Cook for a few more minutes to infuse flavors.

- Serve hot.

name: Thupa - Darjeeling Style
categories: Evening Snack, Dinner, Sim's Family Recipes
ingredients:
- 4 cups vegetables per person (carrots, capsicum, beans, pokchoy/spinach - cut into strips)

- Few green chillies, chopped

- 10-12 cloves of garlic, chopped

- 2 pieces ginger, chopped

- Chicken stock or vegetable stock

- 1 teaspoon soya sauce

- 2 teaspoons vinegar

- 2 teaspoons green chilli sauce

- Salt to taste

- Freshly ground black pepper to taste

- 1 tablespoon oil

- Cooked protein (chicken/paneer/tofu/prawn, etc.)
nutrition:
- Calories: Around 100 Kcal

- Fat: Around 5 g

- Protein: Around 4 g

- Fiber: Around 4 g
method:
- Heat oil in a wok or kadai.

- Add chopped garlic to the warm oil and stir-fry for a minute.

- Add chopped ginger and green chillies, stir until lightly browned.

- Add carrots and stir-fry for a minute.

- Follow with beans, then capsicum, and finally cabbage.

- Add pokchoy or spinach towards the end.

- Pour in hot stock.

- Season with salt, pepper, soya sauce, green chilli sauce, and vinegar.

- Taste and adjust seasoning as needed.

- Add the cooked protein (e.g., chicken) to the soup.

- Serve the soup as is or with noodles or momos.

name: Spinach Broccoli Soup
categories: Evening Snack, Dinner, Sim's Family Recipes
ingredients:
- 1 cup chopped and cleaned broccoli

- 1 cup cleaned and chopped spinach

- 1 teaspoon seed or nut powder (optional)

- 1/4 cup milk

- Salt & pepper to taste
nutrition:
- Calories: Around 90 Kcal

- Fat: Around 4 g

- Protein: Around 5 g

- Fiber: Around 5 g
method:
- Place the spinach and broccoli in a deep pan with 1/4 cup of water and bring it to a boil.

- Boil for approximately 10 minutes or until the broccoli is soft enough to be squashed with your fingers.

- Allow it to cool down.

- Blend the cooked spinach and broccoli in a mixer grinder along with milk and seed or nut powder (if using) until you get a smooth consistency.

- Transfer the mixture back into the pan and season it with salt and pepper according to taste.

- Adjust the consistency by adding more milk if desired for a thinner and creamier soup.

- Serve the soup with toasted bread and sprinkle some toasted sesame seeds on top.

name: Paneer Mix Veg
ingredients:
- 4 carrots

- 3 capsicum (green bell peppers)

- 3 tomatoes

- 2 big onions

- 2-3 ginger pieces

- 4-5 slit green chillies (optional, adjust for taste)

- 1/2 teaspoon whole jeera (cumin seeds)

- 400-500 grams paneer (Indian cottage cheese)

- Salt and red chilli powder to taste

- Oil for cooking
nutrition:
- Calories: Around 350 Kcal

- Fat: Around 25 g

- Protein: Around 20 g

- Fiber: Around 8 g
method:
- Cut carrots, capsicum, tomatoes, onions, and ginger into thin strips.

- Heat oil in a kadhai or pan.

- Add cumin seeds (jeera) to the warm oil and cook until fragrant.

- Add onions and cook for a minute.

- Add sliced ginger and cook for another minute.

- Add slit green chillies (if using).

- Put in the carrots and cook for 2-3 minutes.

- Add green capsicum and stir for a minute.

- Incorporate the sliced tomatoes gently into the mixture.

- Season with salt and red chilli powder, mix well.

- Cook for 5 minutes, then add sliced paneer.

- Gently mix, being careful not to break the paneer.

- Serve hot.

name: Palak Loaded Omlette
categories: Breakfast, Evening Snack, Sim's Family Recipes
ingredients:
- 1 whole egg

- 3 egg whites

- 1 tightly packed cup of spinach (palak)

- 1/2 onion, chopped

- 2 green chillies (optional)

- Salt to taste

- Pepper to taste

- Oil for cooking
nutrition:
- Calories: Around 180 Kcal

- Fat: Around 10 g

- Protein: Around 25 g

- Fiber: Around 4 g
method:
- Whisk whole egg and egg whites together until fluffy.

- Wash spinach thoroughly and remove excess water by squeezing it with your hands. Roughly chop or tear the spinach.

- Add spinach, chopped onion, chillies, and seasoning (salt, pepper) to the eggs. Mix well.

- Put a few drops of oil in a pan and heat it slightly. Spread the oil across the pan using a spatula.

- Pour the egg mixture onto the pan and cook until done.

name: Lauki With Prawns - Lau Chingri
ingredients:
- 250 grams prawns

- 375 grams lauki (bottle gourd), diced into cubes

- 1 teaspoon cumin seeds (jeera)

- 3-4 bay leaves

- 1/4 teaspoon turmeric powder (haldi)

- 1/2 teaspoon red chilli powder

- 3-5 whole green chillies, slit through the middle

- Handful of chopped coriander leaves

- Salt to taste

- Mustard oil (or any preferred cooking oil)
nutrition:
- Calories: Around 250 Kcal

- Fat: Around 10 g

- Protein: Around 25 g

- Fiber: Around 6 g
method:
- Marinate the prawns with turmeric powder and salt in a little oil. Set aside.

- Heat mustard oil in a pan, then add cumin seeds and bay leaves.

- Add a few slit green chillies into the hot oil.

- Add diced bottle gourd (lauki) into the pan.

- Season with salt, turmeric powder, and red chilli powder. Cook until the bottle gourd releases its natural water (do not add additional water).

- Stir in the remaining green chillies and chopped coriander leaves.

- Once the bottle gourd is cooked, add the marinated prawns. Cook for a few minutes.

- Serve hot, typically with rice.

name: Pumpkin Karela Sabzi
ingredients:
- 150 grams Pumpkin, small cubes with skin

- 1 medium Bitter Gourd (Karela), deseeded and sliced

- 1/4 teaspoon Turmeric Powder (Haldi)

- 1/4 teaspoon Red Chili Powder (Mirchi Powder)

- 2 whole Green Chillies, slit lengthwise

- 1 teaspoon Black Jeera (Onion Seeds/Kalonji)

- 2 teaspoons Mustard Oil
nutrition:
- Calories: Around 120 Kcal

- Fat: Around 9 g

- Protein: Around 3 g

- Fiber: Around 6 g
method:
- Cut and wash the pumpkin into small cubes.

- Scrape off some of the skin of the bitter gourd using a knife. Cut it in the middle and make slices.

- Heat oil in a pan until it releases its aroma. Let it cool slightly.

- Add black jeera and green chillies to the oil. Once it starts to splutter, add the pumpkin and bitter gourd.

- Add turmeric powder, red chili powder, cover the pan, and cook until the pumpkin is tender.

name: Apple Pie Oats
ingredients:
- 2 tablespoons Quick Oats

- 1 small Apple, chopped

- 1 small Banana, sliced

- ½ teaspoon Cinnamon Powder

- 2 Walnuts, chopped

- 1 teaspoon Raisins

- ¾ to 1 cup Water
nutrition:
- Calories: Around 250 Kcal

- Fat: Around 7 g

- Protein: Around 5 g

- Fiber: Around 8 g
method:
- Place the chopped apples in water and bring to a boil. Simmer for about 5 minutes.

- Add the quick oats to the apple mixture.

- Stir in the cinnamon powder.

- Cook for approximately 2 minutes or until the desired consistency is achieved.

- Pour the cooked oatmeal into a bowl.

- Top it with sliced bananas, chopped walnuts, and raisins.

- Dust with a little cinnamon powder.

- Serve the oatmeal warm.

name: High Protein Dosa
ingredients:
- 1/2 cup Green Moong Dal (can use sprouts)

- 1 Green Chilli

- 1/2 teaspoon Jeera (Cumin Seeds) - optional

- 1/2 inch Ginger

- 1 pinch Asafoetida (Hing) - optional

- 1/4 cup Chopped Coriander Leaves - optional

- Salt to taste

- Coconut Oil or Olive Oil for cooking

Toppings:

- Onions, finely chopped

- Green Chilli, finely chopped
nutrition:
- Calories: Around 200 Kcal

- Fat: Around 7 g

- Protein: Around 10 g

- Fiber: Around 6 g
method:
Making the Batter:

- Rinse the green moong dal and soak it overnight in sufficient water.

- Drain the soaked moong dal and put it in a grinder jar along with ginger, green chilli, asafoetida, coriander leaves, and salt.

- Add a little water and grind to form a smooth batter.

- The batter consistency should resemble that of a dosa batter or thick milkshake.

Making the Dosa:

- On a griddle or flat pan, add a few drops of oil and spread it evenly with a cut onion, coating the pan (use a non-stick pan for low oil usage).

- Sprinkle a little water. If it sizzles, your pan is hot enough.

- Pour one ladle of batter onto the pan and use the back of the ladle to spread the batter in a circular motion.

- Sprinkle finely chopped onions and green chillies onto the dosa.

- Press the toppings into the batter to ensure they stick as the dosa cooks.

- Flip the dosa and cook until both sides are crisp and browned.

- Serve hot with mint chutney or tomato chutney.

Notes:

- This dosa can be prepared using yellow moong dal, split green gram, or sprouted moong dal.

- If using yellow moong dal, soaking for 3-4 hours is sufficient.

- Toppings are optional; the dosa can also be enjoyed plain.

- Leftover batter can be stored in the refrigerator for up to 3 days.

name: Super Seed Powder
ingredients:
- 3/4 cup Flaxseeds

- 1/2 cup Hemp Seeds

- 1/2 cup Mixed Seeds (Pumpkin, Sesame, Sunflower, Watermelon)

- 1/4 cup Cacao Nibs

- 1 teaspoon Turmeric

- 1/2 teaspoon Ground Pepper
nutrition:
- Calories: Around 1800 Kcal

- Fat: Around 120 g

- Protein: Around 80 g

- Fiber: Around 60 g
method:
- Combine all the seeds in a mixing bowl.

- Use the chutney jar of the grinder.

- Ensure the seeds are completely dry.

- Pulse the mixture quickly, open and stir.

- Continue pulsing in short bursts until it reaches a powder-like consistency. Avoid over-grinding to prevent clumping.

- Store the powder in an airtight container in the refrigerator.

Notes:

- You can use any blend of seeds for variety and nutrients.

- Hemp seeds with the shell should be included as they are rich in protein.

- Additionally, chia seeds can be mixed into the powder, allowing them to remain whole.

name: Creamy Low Cal White Sauce
ingredients:
For White Sauce:

- 1.2 liters Milk

- 2 tablespoons Atta (wheat flour)

- Salt to taste

- Freshly ground Pepper to taste

- Herbs as required

For Vegetables:

- 1 cup Mixed Vegetables (carrot, beans, mushrooms, broccoli, cauliflower, colored capsicum), diced

- 1 tablespoon Finely Chopped Garlic

- 1 small Green Chilli (optional)

- Freshly ground Pepper to taste

- Herbs as required

- Oil for cooking

Additional Ingredients:

- Cooked Chicken Cubes (quantity as desired)

- Pasta (quantity as desired), cooked as per instructions
nutrition:
- Calories: Around 400 Kcal

- Fat: Around 15 g

- Protein: Around 20 g

- Fiber: Around 7 g
method:
Prepare White Sauce:

- In a bowl, mix atta with a little milk to form a smooth paste.

- Add this paste to a pan. Gradually add the remaining milk, stirring continuously to avoid lumps.

- Season with salt, pepper, and herbs.

- Cook the mixture on low heat, stirring continuously until it starts to thicken slightly.

Prepare Vegetables:

- Cut the mixed vegetables into uniform shapes for even cooking.

- Heat oil in a pan.

- Add chopped garlic and sauté for 2 minutes.

- Add the optional green chili, if using, followed by mixed vegetables. Cook for approximately 5 minutes until vegetables are tender.

Assemble:

- In a separate pan, stir-fry the chicken cubes until fully cooked.

- Combine the cooked chicken with the white sauce.

- Add the cooked vegetables to the white sauce and mix well.

- Mix in the cooked pasta before adding the sauce.

Notes:

- Use a variety of vegetables for enhanced flavor.

- The atta-milk mixture will continue to thicken.

- Varieties of vegetables can be used according to personal preference.

name: Quick Basil Fried Cauli-Rice
ingredients:
- 1/2 large Cauliflower

- 1/4 cup Carrot, chopped into small squares

- 1/4 cup Mixed Bell Peppers (all colors), chopped small

- 1/4 cup Beans, chopped small

- 1 heaped tablespoon Finely Chopped Garlic

- A handful of Fresh Basil Leaves, roughly torn (optional)

- 2 teaspoons Oil of choice

- 1 tablespoon Soy Sauce

- 1/2 teaspoon Sugar of choice

- Salt and Pepper to taste
nutrition:
- Calories: Around 100 Kcal

- Fat: Around 6 g

- Protein: Around 5 g

- Fiber: Around 6 g
method:
- Wash and thoroughly dry the cauliflower, removing all greens. Cut the cauliflower into chunks and grate using a grater or blend in small batches for a few seconds until it resembles "rice."

- Transfer the cauliflower rice onto a clean muslin cloth or paper towel and press to remove excess moisture.

- Heat 2 teaspoons of oil in a pan, add chopped garlic, and sauté until golden.

- Add the chopped vegetables and cook on high heat for 2-3 minutes.

- Add the cauliflower rice and torn basil leaves, cook for 5-8 minutes.

- Mix in the soy sauce, salt, pepper, and a pinch of sugar. Stir well.

- Serve hot with a side of chili sauce.

Notes:

- Cauliflower rice can be used in various recipes like stir-fries, fried rice, or pilaf.

- Leftovers can be stored in the refrigerator for up to 5 days.

- Uncooked cauliflower rice can be portioned and stored in the freezer for up to 1 month. Thaw in the refrigerator before cooking.

- Heat garlic with cold oil to infuse flavor and prevent quick burning.

name: Creamy Coleslaw
categories: Breakfast, Post Dinner, Dinner, Sim's Family Recipes
ingredients:
- 1 cup Homemade Set Curd

- 1/4 cup thinly sliced Cabbage

- 1/4 cup grated Carrot

- 1/4 cup thinly sliced Green Capsicum

- 1-2 large Garlic cloves

- 1 small Green Chilli (optional)

- Salt & Pepper to taste
nutrition:
- Calories: Around 80 Kcal

- Fat: Around 5 g

- Protein: Around 5 g

- Fiber: Around 2 g
method:
Preparing the Curd:

- Place the curd in a muslin cloth and squeeze out excess water. Keep it refrigerated until other ingredients are prepared.

Preparing the Vegetables:

- Slice or grate the vegetables thinly. Toss them with a pinch of salt and set aside.

- In a pan with a few drops of oil at room temperature, roast the chopped garlic on low flame until browned and crispy. Remove from heat.

Assembling the Salad:

- Squeeze out any excess water from the vegetables.

- Beat the curd into a smooth, creamy paste.

- Mix the vegetables, roasted garlic, and cold thick curd together.

- Season with salt, pepper powder, and a dash of lime juice.

- Store in the refrigerator until serving.

name: Chocolate Popcorn
categories: Evening Snack, Dessert, Sim's Family Recipes
ingredients:
- 1/2 cup Corn Kernels

- 2 pieces Chocolate (cooking/baking chocolate preferred)
nutrition:
- Calories: Around 200 Kcal

- Fat: Around 10 g

- Protein: Around 4 g

- Fiber: Around 3 g
method:
- Place the corn kernels in a cooker or a pan with a lid.

- Heat on medium and cover the cooker (if using), without the weight (whistle).

- Shake the cooker occasionally until you start hearing the corn popping.

- Lower the heat and continue shaking the cooker to ensure even popping.

- Once the popping sound stops, remove the popped corn from the cooker and place it in a separate bowl.

- In the warm cooker (with the heat off), add the chocolate to melt. Make sure it doesn't burn.

- Add the popped corn back into the cooker with melted chocolate. Stir well to coat the popcorn evenly.

- Serve immediately or store in an airtight container once cooled.

name: Hot Chocolate
categories: Evening Snack, Dessert, Sim's Family Recipes
ingredients:
- 1 teaspoon Unsweetened Cocoa Powder

- 1-inch square of Jaggery (or sweetener of choice)

- 1 cup Water
nutrition:
- Calories: Around 50 Kcal

- Fat: Around 0.5 g

- Protein: Around 0.8 g

- Fiber: Around (less than 0.5 g)
method:
- Mix the cocoa powder into room temperature water until there are no lumps.

- Add the jaggery or sweetener to the mixture and simmer on low heat for about 5 minutes.

- Let it boil down to reduce the liquid to about 3/4 cup.

- Switch off the heat when it thickens to your desired consistency.

- Sprinkle with additional cocoa powder just before serving.

- Serve hot.

name: Fudgy Chocolate Oats
ingredients:
- 1/4 cup quick oats

- 1 large ripe banana, mashed

- 1 tbsp unsweetened cocoa powder

- 1 tbsp my seed powder (optional)

- 1/2 cup water
nutrition:
- Calories: Around 270 Kcal

- Fat: Around 4.5 g

- Protein: Around 6 g

- Fiber: Around 8 g
method:
- Mash a large ripe banana (with black spots on the outside).

- To the mashed banana, add the cocoa or cacao powder, oats, and water.

- Cook on low flame, stirring continuously until it thickens and the oats are cooked, approximately 5 minutes.

- Add in the seed powder, if using.

- Once it reaches your desired consistency, transfer to a bowl and serve hot.

Notes:

- Oats: Quick oats can be used instantly. Rolled oats need a longer time to cook and a little more water. Steel-cut oats should be soaked overnight.

- Banana: Use a ripe banana with black spots on the exterior for sweetness.

- Sweetness: Jaggery can be added during cooking or top with a teaspoon of honey if desired.

- Cacao Powder: Nutritionally dense compared to cocoa powder, rich in antioxidants and magnesium.

- Almonds: Preferably soaked overnight and skin removed for better nutrition absorption.

- Liquid: Almond milk can be replaced with water for a simpler version.

name: Chinese Red Chilli Sauce
ingredients:
- 1 cup dried red chillies

- 3/4 cup Water (approximately)

- 1/4 cup garlic, crushed & roughly chopped

- 1 tsp Oil

- 1/4 cup Vinegar

1 tsp Salt

- 1 tbsp Sugar
nutrition:
- Calories: Around 50 Kcal

- Fat: Around 1 g

- Protein: About 1 g

- Fiber:Around 1 g
method:
- Remove the seeds from the red chilies as best as you can by breaking each chili in half; a few stray seeds are okay.

- Put the chillies in a pan with enough water to cover them. Heat on the stove for 4-5 minutes until the chillies become swollen and the water is nearly absorbed.

- In a pan, add half of the oil and chopped garlic. Roast on low flame until the garlic starts to brown around the edges.

- Coarsely grind the soaked chillies and roasted garlic.

- Heat the remaining oil in a pan and return the chilli-garlic mixture to it. Add the rest of the ingredients and cook until the sauce comes together and the oil separates at the sides.

- Cool the sauce completely and transfer it to a clean, dry jar. Store in an airtight container in the refrigerator.

Notes:

- Vinegar: Use vinegar of choice. Apple cider vinegar or any vinegar works well.

- Oil: Use an unflavored oil. Mustard or coconut oil might impart additional flavors.

- Sugar: Can be replaced with jaggery, honey, brown sugar, cane sugar, or any sweetener of choice. If using honey, add it at the end without cooking.

- Salt: Adjust to taste.

name: Marinated Chicken
ingredients:
- 100g Chicken

- 50ml Curd

- Few Chopped Green Chillies

- 1 tsp Lemon Juice

- 1/2 tsp Coarsely Ground Pepper

- 1 tsp Chopped Coriander Leaves

- 1/8 tsp Ginger Paste

- 1/8 tsp Garlic Paste

Other Ingredients:

- 1 Bay Leaf

- 1 Cinnamon Stick

- 1 Green Cardamom

- 1 Clove

- 1/4 tsp Whole Peppercorn

- Few Whole Slit Green Chillies

- 1/4 tsp Chopped Ginger

- 1/8 tsp Chopped Garlic

- Salt (according to taste)

- 1 tsp Oil or Ghee
nutrition:
- Calories: Around 250 Kcal

- Fat: Around 12 g

- Protein: Around 20 g

- Fiber: Around 1 g
method:
- Marinate the chicken in the given marination ingredients and set it aside for half an hour.

- In a Kadhai, warm oil/ghee slightly.

- Add the bay leaf, cinnamon, cardamom, and cloves. Stir for a few seconds.

- Add the whole peppercorn. Stir for a few seconds.

- Add chopped ginger and garlic to the Kadhai.

- When the ginger-garlic turns beige, add the marinated chicken pieces one by one.

- Reserve the remaining curd for later use.

- Let it cook on low flame for a few minutes, then flip the chicken pieces and continue cooking.

- The chicken will release water and cook in it. Cook on low flame.

- When the chicken is 3/4 done, add the remaining curd and the slit green chillies.

- Allow the chicken to cook completely.

- Serve hot.

name: Vegetable Paneer Bhurji
ingredients:
- 50g Homemade Paneer (Cottage Cheese)

- 100g Tomato, chopped

- 100g Capsicum (Bell Pepper)

- 2 tbsp Peas

- 1/8 tsp Whole Cumin

- 1/4 tsp Chopped Ginger

- 1/2 tsp Chopped Green Chillies

- Pinch of Turmeric Powder

- Chilli Powder (according to taste)

- 1 tsp Chopped Coriander Leaves

- Salt (according to taste)

- 1 tsp Oil
nutrition:
- Calories: Around 200 Kcal

- Fat: Around 12 g

- Protein: Around 10 g

- Fiber: Around 4 g
method:
- Crumble the homemade paneer and set it aside.

- Take a kadai and warm oil slightly.

- Add whole cumin and let it splutter.

- Stir in the chopped ginger for about a minute.

- Add chopped green chillies, stir for a few seconds.

- Add turmeric powder, stir it well.

- Add red chilli powder to taste and mix.

- Add peas and cook for a while.

- Stir in the chopped capsicum, cook for 1 minute.

- Add chopped tomato and sauté for a few minutes, ensuring the vegetables don't become too soft.

- Add salt according to taste.

- Mix in the crumbled paneer.

- Add chopped coriander leaves and mix thoroughly.

- Serve hot.

name: Masala Chicken
ingredients:
- 100g Chicken (marinated with salt, turmeric, and 1/2 a lemon juice)

- 1 Big Onion, chopped

- 1 Big Tomato, chopped

- 10-12 Curry Leaves

- 1 tsp Ginger Paste

- 3/4 tsp Garlic Paste

- Salt (to taste)

- 1 tsp Oil

For Grinding:

- 1 Bay Leaf

- 1/8 tsp Fennel Seeds (Sauf)

- 1/4 tsp Whole Peppercorns

- 1/4 tsp Whole Cumin

- 1/4 tsp Whole Coriander Seeds

- 1 Whole Red Chilli

- 1 tsp Grated Coconut (optional)

- 1/2 tsp Tamarind
nutrition:
- Calories: Around 270 Kcal

- Fat: Around 14 g

- Protein: Around 22 g

- Fiber: Around 4 g
method:
For Grinding:

- Dry roast the spices (excluding coconut) until they start changing color.

- Add grated coconut and roast for a few more minutes until it turns beige.

- Put the roasted spices and coconut in a grinder, add tamarind, and grind into a paste. Keep aside.

For Chicken:

- Put oil in a Kadhai, warm it, and add chopped onion.

- When onion turns translucent, add ginger-garlic paste.

- Sauté the masala until it turns slightly beige, then add curry leaves. Add a little water while sautéing if needed.

- Once onions become soft, add the chopped tomato. Sauté for 5-7 minutes.

- Add the marinated chicken. Sauté, cover, and cook until chicken is halfway done.

- Add the roasted ground masala. Sauté on low flame until the chicken is fully cooked.

- Ready to serve.

name: Schezwan Vegetables
ingredients:
- 50g Onion, sliced

- 50g Capsicum, sliced

- 50g Carrots, sliced into strips

- 1/2 tsp Chopped Garlic

- 1 Whole Red Chilli, cut into bits

- 1/8 tsp Ginger Julienne

- Few Slit Green Chillies

- 1/2 tsp Chopped Coriander Leaves

- 1/4 tsp Sugar

- 1/4 tsp Red Chilli Powder

- 1/2 tsp Red Chilli Sauce

- 1 tsp Thai Sweet Chilli Sauce

- 1 tsp Tomato Ketchup

- 1/4 tsp Soy Sauce

- Salt (to taste)

- 1 tsp Oil

- 5g Cornflour Paste (made from cornflour and water)
nutrition:
- Calories: Around 100 Kcal

- Fat:Around 4 g

- Protein: Around 2 g

- Fiber: Around3 g
method:
- In a Kadhai, warm the oil slightly.

- Add chopped garlic, stir for a few seconds.

- Add the cut red chillies, stir for a few seconds.

- Add ginger julienne and 1-2 slit green chillies. Stir for a few seconds.

- Add sliced onions and stir-fry for a few seconds to reduce rawness.

- Mix tomato sauce, chilli sauce, Thai sweet chilli sauce, and soya sauce. Stir well for a few seconds.

- Add red chilli powder (as per taste). Mix well for a few seconds.

- Add capsicum, stir for a few seconds.

- Add carrots, stir for a few seconds.

- Add more slit green chillies and chopped coriander leaves. Mix well for a few seconds.

- Maintain the crunchiness of the vegetables.

- Add salt, sugar, and mix.

- Put the cornflour paste to coat the vegetables with the sauce.

name: Paneer Schezwan
ingredients:
- 100g Onion, sliced

- 100g Capsicum, sliced

- 50g Carrots, sliced into strips

- 1/2 tsp Chopped Garlic

- 1 Whole Red Chilli, cut into bits

- 1/8 tsp Ginger Julienne

- Few Slit Green Chillies

- 1/2 tsp Chopped Coriander Leaves

- 1/4 tsp Sugar

- 1/4 tsp Red Chilli Powder

- 1/2 tsp Red Chilli Sauce

- 1 tsp Thai Sweet Chilli Sauce

- 1 tsp Tomato Ketchup

- 1/4 tsp Soy Sauce

- Salt (to taste)

- 1 tsp Oil

Paneer:

- 50g Paneer (cut into thick strips)

- 1/4 tsp Flour

- 1 tsp Corn Flour

- Pinch of Pepper

- Little Salt
nutrition:
- Calories: Around 300 Kcal

- Fat: Around 12 grams

- Protein: Around 10 grams

- Fiber: Around 3 grams
method:
For Vegetables:

- In a Kadhai, warm the oil slightly.

- Add chopped garlic, stir for a few seconds.

- Add the cut red chillies, stir for a few seconds.

- Add ginger julienne and 1-2 slit green chillies. Stir for a few seconds.

- Add sliced onions, stir-fry briefly to reduce rawness.

- Mix tomato sauce, chilli sauce, Thai sweet chilli sauce, and soya sauce. Stir well for a few seconds.

- Add red chilli powder (as per taste), mix well.

- Add capsicum, stir for a few seconds.

- Add carrots, stir for a few seconds.

- Add more slit green chillies and chopped coriander leaves. Mix well.

- Maintain the crunchiness of the vegetables.

- Add salt and sugar, mix well.

For Paneer :

- Make a paste of corn flour, pepper, salt, and a little water.

- In a pan, rub a little oil and warm it.

- Dip paneer strips (or chicken strips) in the corn flour paste and lightly brown both sides in the pan.

- Once done, add to the vegetables and gently mix.

name: Chilli Garlic Chickpea'S
ingredients:
- 30g Chickpeas

- Pinch of Baking Soda (optional)

- 50g Spring Onions

- 1 tsp Chopped Garlic

- 1 tsp Tomato Sauce

- 1/2 tsp Chilli Sauce

- 1/2 tsp Chilli Flakes (optional)

- 1/2 tsp Soya Sauce

- 1/2 tsp Sugar

- Salt (to taste)

- 1 tsp Oil
nutrition:
- Calories: Around 170 Kcal

- Fat: Around 7 g

- Protein: Around 6 g

- Fiber: Around 4 g
method:
- Wash and soak chickpeas overnight or for 7-8 hours.

- Cook chickpeas in a pressure cooker for 30-35 minutes on low flame after the first whistle. Add a little salt and a pinch of baking soda. Let the cooker release pressure naturally.

- Drain the cooked chickpeas in a strainer and keep aside. Preserve the water separately.

- In a pan, heat 1/2 tsp oil and spread it. Roast the boiled chickpeas on low flame till they become crisp. It's helpful to cool the chickpeas in the refrigerator for an hour before roasting.

- Once done, set aside the chickpeas.

- In another pan, warm 1/2 tsp of oil. Add chopped garlic and stir-fry until slightly beige.

- In a bowl, mix tomato sauce, chilli sauce, chilli flakes (if using), soya sauce, and sugar.

- Add the above mixture to the garlic, stir for a few seconds.

- Add chopped spring onions and mix well. Then, add 2 tbsp of the liquid from the chickpeas to create a semi-gravy.

- Quickly mix it and add the chickpeas.

- Mix well and top with a few more spring onions.

- If you want more gravy, add all the liquid, leaving it a bit liquid as it will thicken.

name: Garlic Rice With Chilli Flakes
ingredients:
- 30g Rice

- 100g Chicken

- 50g Chopped Spring Onion

- 1/2 tsp Chopped Garlic

- 1/2 tsp Chilli Flakes

- Salt (to taste)

- Pepper (to taste)

- 1 tsp Oil

- Sugar (to taste)
nutrition:
- Calories: Around 280 Kcal

- Fat: Around 7 g

- Protein: Around 20 g

- Fiber: Around 2 g
method:
- In a Kadhai, heat the oil over medium heat.

- Add chopped garlic and stir-fry for 30-40 seconds.

- Then, add the chilli flakes and chopped spring onions. Stir-fry for a few seconds.

- Mix in the boiled rice gently over medium flame.

- Once the rice is mixed, add the chicken.

- Season with salt, pepper, and sugar according to taste.

- Continue to stir-fry until all ingredients are well combined and heated through.

- Serve hot.

name: Lemon Chicken
ingredients:
- 100g Chicken

- 1/2 Egg

- 1/8 tsp Pepper

- 1/4 tsp Sugar

- 1 tsp Lemon Juice

- 2-3 slices of Lemon (thinly sliced)

- Jaggery (to taste)

- 2 tsp Chopped Spring Onions

Marination for Chicken:

- 1/2 kg Chicken

- 1 tsp Corn Flour

- Salt and Pepper (to taste)

- 1 tsp Oil
nutrition:
- Calories: Around 300 Kcal

- Fat: Around 12 g

- Protein: Around 20 g

- Fiber: negligible
method:
- In a bowl, mix egg, corn flour, and chicken. Allow it to marinate for some time.

- Heat a non-stick pan, add a little oil, and sauté the marinated chicken. Set aside.

For the Gravy:

- In a pan, add the chicken stock. Bring it to a boil.

- Season with salt and pepper.

- Add jaggery and let it dissolve completely. Adjust sweetness to taste.

- Add lemon slices and cook for a few minutes. Remove slices if overcooked to avoid bitterness.

- Stir in lemon juice.

- Mix corn flour with water and add it to the gravy to thicken.

- Add the sautéed chicken to the gravy.

- Stir in chopped spring onions and sugar.

- Once done, the dish is ready to serve.

name: Moong Dal Jaggery Kheer
ingredients:
- 1 tbsp Moong Dal

- 1 tsp Rice

- 50ml Skimmed Milk

- 2 Almonds

- 4-5 Raisins

- Pinch of Cardamom Powder

- 1 tbsp Jaggery

- 1/2 tsp Ghee/Oil
nutrition:
- Calories: Around 180 Kcal

- Fat: Around 5 g

- Protein: Around 6 g

- Fiber: Around 2 g
method:
- Wash the moong dal and rice, then set aside.

- Thinly chop the almonds and raisins.

- In a Kadhai, heat ghee/oil. Once warm, add the chopped dry fruits and roast for about a minute.

- Add the washed dal and rice to the Kadhai. Stir-fry for 1-2 minutes.

- Add water and let it cook. Mix in the jaggery thoroughly.

- When the dal and rice are 3/4 cooked, pour in the milk.

- Cook until done, slightly mashing the rice and dal.

- Allow it to cook on a low flame until it thickens.

- Add the cardamom powder and mix well. Adjust consistency as needed.

- Serve in a bowl, garnished with roasted dry fruits.

name: Coconut Chicken
ingredients:
- 100g Chicken

- 100g Onions, grated

- 100g Tomatoes, grated

- 1/4 tsp Ginger Paste

- 1/4 tsp Garlic Paste

- 1 Green Cardamom

- 1 Cinnamon Stick

- Chilli Powder (to taste)

- 1/8 tsp Turmeric Powder

- 1-2 Green Chillies

- 1 tbsp Coconut Milk

- Salt (to taste)

- 1 tsp Oil
nutrition:
- Calories: Around 250 Kcal

- Fat: Around 10 g

- Protein: Around 20 g

- Fiber: Around 10 g
method:
- Heat oil in a kadhai until slightly warm.

- Add the green cardamom and cinnamon stick to the oil.

- Quickly add the grated onions to the kadhai.

- Sauté the onions until they turn golden brown.

- Add the grated tomatoes to the sautéed onions and continue cooking until the tomato water evaporates.

- Incorporate the dry spices: salt, red chilli powder, and turmeric powder into the masala. Add a few teaspoons of water to infuse the spices and continue sautéing.

- After 5-7 minutes, add the chicken and sauté for 7-10 minutes.

- Pour water into the chicken mixture. Once it starts bubbling, cover and cook on low flame until the chicken is thoroughly cooked.

- Add the coconut milk (prepared from packet coconut powder soaked in warm water, or as instructed on the packet).

- Introduce a few whole green chillies to the mixture according to your taste.

- Continue cooking on low flame for 5-7 minutes until oil surfaces on top.

- Your dish is ready to serve.

name: Tomato Chicken
ingredients:
- 100g Chicken

- 100g Tomatoes, grated

- 100g Onions, grated

- 1/4 tsp Garlic Paste

- 1/4 tsp Ginger Paste

- 1 tsp Tomato Sauce

- 1/4 tsp Vinegar

- Red Chilli Powder (to taste)

- 1/2 tsp Chopped Green Chillies

- 2 tsp Chopped Coriander Leaves

- Salt (to taste)

- 1 tsp Oil
nutrition:
- Calories: Around 200 Kcal

- Fat: Around 8 g

- Protein: Around 20 g

- Fiber: minimal
method:
- Heat oil in a kadhai until slightly warm.

- Add the grated onions to the oil and sauté for 5-7 minutes until they soften.

- Add the ginger-garlic paste to the sautéed onions and continue cooking until the onions turn golden brown.

- Mix in the chicken and sauté for 10 minutes over low flame.

- Add salt and red chilli powder according to taste.

- Incorporate the grated tomatoes and tomato sauce into the mixture. Cook for an additional 5-7 minutes.

- Add the chopped green chillies and cover, allowing the chicken to cook in the released juices.

- When most of the water evaporates, continue sautéing on low flame.

- Pour vinegar into the mixture and mix well.

- Cook for another 5-10 minutes until the chicken is thoroughly done.

- Before removing from heat, add the chopped coriander leaves, ensuring they infuse into the gravy. Let it cook on low flame for a few minutes.

- Serve hot.

name: Patal Bharta Salad
ingredients:
- 100g Patal (Snake Gourd)

- 2 tsp Chopped Coriander Leaves

- Few Chopped Green Chillies

- Salt (to taste)

- 1 tsp Mustard Oil / Olive Oil

- Pinch of Mustard Powder or Paste (if using olive oil)
nutrition:
The exact nutritional content may vary based on the specific ingredients used and their quantities. Here's an estimated nutritional value for the recipe per serving:

- Calories: Around 45 Kcal

- Fat: Around 4 g

- Protein: Around 2 g

- Fiber: Around 2 g
method:
- Wash the patal, trim both ends, and scrape off the skin.

- Place the patal in a steamer or a cooker without the weight and steam for 5-10 minutes until tender.

- Once cooked, remove the patal and transfer it to a plate.

- Mash the steamed patal thoroughly.

- Add the chopped coriander leaves, chopped green chillies, and salt to taste to the mashed patal.

- Mix in 1 teaspoon of mustard oil (or olive oil with a pinch of mustard powder/paste) and combine well.

- Serve the prepared steamed patal.

name: Vegetable Moong Dal Khichdi
ingredients:
- 1 tbsp Moong Dal

- 30g Rice

- 50g Tomatoes

- 20g Pumpkin

- 20g Ridge Gourd

- 20g Carrots

- 20g Potatoes (optional)

- 20g Peas (optional)

- 20g Cauliflower

- 1 Whole Red Chilli

- 1 Bay Leaf

- 1 Green Cardamom

- 1 Clove

- 1 Cinnamon Stick (of 2 each)

- ½ tsp Whole Jeera (Cumin Seeds)

Paste Ingredients:

- 5-6 Green Chillies

- 2 pieces Ginger

- 2 tsp Sugar

- 1 tsp Garam Masala

- Turmeric Powder

- Salt (according to taste)

- 1 tsp Oil
nutrition:
The nutritional values can vary based on specific ingredient quantities and their types. Here's an approximate estimation per serving:

- Calories: Around 250 kcal

- Protein: Around 7 g

- Fat: Around 3 g

- Fiber: Around 7 g
method:
- Roast the moong dal in a Kadhai on low flame until it becomes aromatic. Wash the roasted dal and keep it aside.

- Wash and soak the dal and rice, then set them aside.

- In a Kadhai, add oil/ghee and warm it.

- Add bay leaves, cinnamon stick, cloves, and cardamom. Stir for a few seconds, then add whole red chillies and cumin seeds.

- Once the cumin seeds start spluttering and emit fragrance, add the ginger-green chilli paste. Sauté until the raw smell diminishes.

- Add the tomatoes and stir for a few seconds.

- Add all the vegetables one by one, stirring and mixing in between. Cauliflower can be semi-cooked separately before adding it to the Kadhai.

- Put the washed dal and rice in the Kadhai, add turmeric powder, and mix well.

- Add peas, salt, sugar, and garam masala. Mix gently and pour in some water.

- Add semi-cooked cauliflower, mix gently, cover, and cook.

- Stir occasionally to prevent the vegetables from becoming overly mushy.

- Once cooked, the dish is ready to serve.

name: Raw Mango Chutney/Aam Chutney
ingredients:
- 2 slices of Raw Mango

- 1 piece Whole Red Chilli

- ¼ tsp Panch Phoran (blend of five whole spices)

- Black Salt (to taste)

- Red Chilli Flakes (to taste, or Red Chilli Powder as a substitute)

- Pinch of Turmeric

- ⅛ tsp Jeera (Cumin) Powder

- ⅛ tsp Dhaniya (Coriander) Powder

- Pinch of Garam Masala (optional)

- ½ tsp Oil
nutrition:
- Calories: Around 60 kcal

- Fat: Around 4 g

- Fiber: Around 2 g

- Protein: Around 2 g
method:
- Cut the raw mango into cubes with the skin on and set aside.

- In a Kadhai, heat the oil over low heat.

- Add the whole red chillies followed by the panch phoran. Stir for a few seconds.

- Add the cut mango cubes.

- Stir and roast the mango cubes for 5-10 minutes.

- Add the dry spices (black salt, red chilli flakes or powder, turmeric, jeera powder, dhaniya powder, and garam masala if using) and mix well.

- Pour in ½ cup of water to aid in cooking the mango and to soften it.

- Add jaggery to the mango and continue stirring. Adjust the quantity of jaggery based on desired sweetness.

- Cook on low flame until the mango is soft and cooked.

- Just before removing from heat, taste and adjust the spices if needed.

name: Poha Tikiya
ingredients:
- 2 tbsp Raw Poha (flattened rice)

- 20g Carrots, grated

- 20g Potatoes, boiled and mashed

- 20g Peas, blanched and roughly mashed

- ½ tsp Chopped Dhaniya Patta (Coriander Leaves)

- 20g Onions, chopped

- ¼ tsp Grated Ginger

- Few Green Chillies, chopped (to taste)

- ⅛ tsp Dhaniya (Coriander) Powder

- ½ tsp Jeera (Cumin) Powder

- Pinch of Turmeric Powder

- ¼ tsp Chilli Flakes

- ¼ tsp Garam Masala

- ½ tsp Sugar

- ½ tsp Lemon Juice

- Salt (to taste)

- ½ tsp Oil (for cooking)
nutrition:
- Calories: Around 110 kcal

- Fat: Around 2 g

- Fiber: Around 3 g

- Protein: Around 3 g
method:
- Wash the poha, soak it for 15-20 minutes, then drain and set it aside.

- Roughly mash the blanched peas, boil and mash the potatoes, grate the carrots, and chop the dhaniya patta, onions, ginger, and green chillies.

- Take the soaked poha in a large bowl and mash it well.

- Add all the prepared ingredients mentioned above to the mashed poha and mix thoroughly.

- Add salt, dhaniya powder, jeera powder, turmeric, garam masala, and red chilli flakes to the mixture and mix well.

- Finally, add sugar and lemon juice, adjust salt to taste, and mix thoroughly.

- Take small portions of the mixture, shape them into tikkis.

- Heat 1/2 tsp oil in a pan over medium flame. Place the tikkis on the pan and cook until both sides turn golden brown.

- Once cooked, remove from heat.

name: Curd Brinjal
ingredients:
- 100g Small Brinjal

- 50ml Yogurt

- 100g Chopped Onion

- ¼ tsp Turmeric Powder

- ¼ tsp Jeera (Cumin) Powder

- ¼ tsp Dhaniya (Coriander) Powder

- Red Chilli Powder (to taste)

- Salt (to taste)

- ¼ tsp Garam Masala

- ½ tsp Tomato Sauce

- Oil (approximately 1.5 tbsp total)
nutrition:
- Calories: Around 120 kcal

- Fat: Around 8 g

- Fiber: Around 3 g

- Protein: Around 3 g
method:
- Cut the heads of the brinjal, slit them into 4 parts without reaching the bottom.

- Heat 1.5 tbsp oil in a kadhai. Add the brinjals and cook until they're about ¾ done. Remove them and set aside.

- In the same kadhai, add the remaining oil. Sauté chopped onions until translucent and slightly brown.

- In a bowl, mix turmeric, jeera, coriander, and red chilli powder with a little water to make a paste.

- Add this spice paste to the onions and sauté until it softens. You can add 1-2 tsp water intermittently to prevent the spices from sticking.

- Add yogurt to the sautéed masala and cook well on low flame until the moisture evaporates.

- Mix in tomato sauce and then add the partially cooked brinjal. Sauté gently.

- Season with salt, cover, and cook. Stir occasionally.

- Add garam masala. Mix well and add 2-3 tbsp of water to infuse the spices into the curry.

- Let the water dry on low flame for a few minutes. Once done, it's ready to serve.

name: Spiny Gourd-Kakrul Sabzi
ingredients:
- 100g Kakrul (Spiny Gourd), cut into thin circles

- 1 medium-sized Onion, sliced

- 2-3 Whole Green Chillies

- Salt, to taste

- 1 tsp Sugar

- 1 tsp Oil (preferably Mustard Oil)

For the Paste:

- 1 tsp Poppy Seeds

- 1 Green Chilli
nutrition:
- Calories: Around 100 kcal

- Fat: Around 6 g

- Fiber: Around 3 g

- Protein: Around 3 g
method:
Prepare the Paste:

- Soak poppy seeds in water until they become soft.

- Grind the soaked poppy seeds with a few green chillies to form a paste. Set aside.

Cooking the Kakrul:

- Heat oil in a kadhai. Warm the oil until the raw smell dissipates.

- Add the cut kakrul and stir-fry for 5-7 minutes on medium flame, stirring occasionally.

- Add the sliced onion and whole green chillies according to taste.

- Sauté for a few seconds until the onions turn translucent.

- Add turmeric powder to the kakrul and continue sautéing until onions are soft.

- Once the onions are translucent and kakrul is ¾ cooked, add salt and sugar. Sauté for a few more minutes.

- Add the prepared paste to the kadhai. Gently mix it with the kakrul.

- Cover and cook on low flame until the kakrul is done.

name: Mushroom Peas Masala
ingredients:
- 1 packet of fresh mushrooms (cut each mushroom into 4 pieces)

- ½ cup peas

- 3 tbsp oil

- 1 bay leaf

- 1 ½ medium-sized onions (grated)

- 2 medium-sized tomatoes (pureed)

- ½ tsp ginger paste

- ½ tsp garlic paste

- Salt, to taste

- Red chilli powder, to taste

- ¼ tsp turmeric powder

- ½ tsp jeera powder (cumin powder)

- ½ tsp dhaniya powder (coriander powder)

- Few chopped green chillies (optional)

- 1 tbsp tomato sauce

- 2 tsp curd (yogurt)

- 2-3 tbsp milk

- ¼ tsp garam masala
nutrition:
- Calories: Around 200 kcal

- Fat: Around 15 g

- Fiber: Around 4 g

- Protein: Around 7 g
method:
- Heat oil in a pan.

- Add bay leaf and grated onions. Sauté for a few minutes until onions turn golden brown.

- Add ginger-garlic paste and sauté until the raw aroma disappears.

- Add salt, red chilli powder, turmeric powder, jeera powder, and dhaniya powder. Sauté until aromatic.

- Optionally, add chopped green chillies.

- Pour in tomato puree and cook until the moisture evaporates.

- Add tomato sauce and cook for a few minutes. Then add the curd and sauté for a few more minutes.

- If using fresh peas, cook them partially (50%) and then add to the masala. If using packeted peas, directly add to the masala.

- Add the cut mushrooms, mix well, and sauté on low heat until mushrooms are cooked.

- Pour in the milk and sauté for a few more minutes.

- Sprinkle garam masala, mix thoroughly, and the dish is ready to be served.

name: Hing Torai (Ridge Gourd)
ingredients:
- 2 tbsp oil or ghee

- ¼ tsp hing (asafoetida)

- 1 tsp whole jeera (cumin seeds)

- 1 tsp ginger paste

- Few chopped green chillies (to taste)

- Generous pinch of turmeric powder

- Red chilli powder, to taste

- 1 chopped tomato

- ½ kg torai (ridge gourd), cut in 1-2” pieces lengthwise

- Salt, to taste

- 2 tbsp chopped coriander leaves
nutrition:
- Calories: Around 120 kcal

- Fat: Around 9 g

- Fiber: Around 3 g

- Protein: Around 2 g
method:
- Heat oil or ghee in a pan.

- Add hing and whole jeera (cumin seeds). Let the cumin seeds splutter.

- Add ginger paste and chopped green chillies. Saute for a few minutes.

- Sprinkle turmeric powder and sauté for a few seconds.

- Add red chilli powder according to taste. Saute until the raw smell of ginger dissipates.

- Add the chopped tomato and sauté until it softens.

- Mix in the cut torai (ridge gourd) pieces and stir well.

- Season with salt according to taste.

- Cover and cook on low flame until the torai is cooked (stirring occasionally; torai releases its own water, so no need to add extra water).

- Once the torai is cooked, add chopped coriander leaves and mix well.

- The dish is ready to serve.

name: Kofta Curry(Chicken/Mutton Mince)
ingredients:
- 1/2 kg mince

- 3-4 tbsp finely chopped coriander leaves

- Few chopped green chillies

- 2-3 slices of bread

- 1 egg

- Salt to taste

- 1/2 tsp garam masala

- 1 grated onion
nutrition:
- Calories: Around 350 kcal

- Fat: Around 25 g

- Fiber: Around 3 g

- Protein: Around 30 g
method:
- Mix all kofta ingredients together and shape them into small balls according to preference.

Ingredients for Gravy:

- 3 tbsp oil/ghee or a mixture of both

- 1½ tbsp onion paste

- 1 tomato puréed or 1/2 cup curd

- 4 green cardamom

- 4 cloves

- 1 cinnamon stick

- 3 whole red chillies

- Salt to taste

- Red chilli powder to taste

- 3-4 cups of stock for the gravy (or water if stock is unavailable)

Method for Gravy:

- Prepare stock by boiling chicken/mutton bones in a pressure cooker for 30 minutes on low flame after the first whistle. Let it release pressure naturally.

- In a kadhai, warm 3 tbsp oil/ghee.

- Add cardamom, cloves, cinnamon stick, and whole red chillies. Sauté briefly.

- Add onion paste and sauté until it becomes a beige brown color.

- Add tomato purée/curd and sauté until it becomes a brown color.

- Pour in stock/water to the masala and let it start bubbling.

- Gently add the mince balls to the bubbling gravy without stirring.

- Reduce flame, cover, and cook until the mince balls are cooked through.

- Remove from heat.

Note:

- If you have an air fryer, you can air fry the kofta balls brushed with oil before adding them to the gravy.

name: Patal(Pointed Gourd) And Sweet Potato Sabzi
ingredients:
- 1-2 pieces of patal (scrape the skin lightly and cut into thin vertical pieces)

- 1/4 of a sweet potato (peeled and sliced like potato chips)

- Salt to taste

- Red chili powder to taste

- 1/4 teaspoon turmeric powder

- 1-2 whole red chilies

- 1/4 teaspoon panch phoron (whole spice)

- 1/2 tablespoon of oil (preferably mustard oil)
nutrition:
- Calories: Around 120 Kcal

- Protein: Around 2 g

- Fiber: Around 5 g

- Fat: Around 6 g
method:
- Heat oil in a kadhai.

- Add whole red chilies and panch phoron, sauté for a few seconds.

- Add the sliced patal and sweet potato, stir-fry briefly.

- Season with salt and turmeric, continue stir-frying on low heat.

- You can cover and cook, stirring occasionally for a softer texture or leave uncovered for a crisper finish.

- Sprinkle red chili powder, mix thoroughly.

- Once patal is cooked to your preference, remove from heat.

name: Kheera(Cucumber) Ki Sabzi And Masala Salad
ingredients:
For Sabzi:

- 1 cucumber (cut vertically/lengthwise in 8 pieces, remove the centre part, then chop into ½” pieces)

- 1/8 teaspoon hing (asafoetida)

- 1/8 teaspoon whole jeera (cumin seeds)

- 1/2 tablespoon ghee

- Pinch of turmeric (optional)

- Pinch of red chili powder

- Salt to taste

For Salad:

- 1/4 onion, sliced

- 1/4 tomato, sliced

- 1/2 green chili, chopped

- Pinch of ginger, finely chopped

- 1/2 tablespoon sprouts (optional)

- Dash of lime
nutrition:
- Calories: Around 110 Kcal

- Protein: Around 2 g

- Fiber: Around 3 g

- Fat: Around 8 g
method:
- In a pan, heat the ghee.

- Once warm, add asafoetida and cumin seeds. Let the cumin seeds splutter.
