- Add the chopped cucumber to the pan. Sauté for a few minutes, then cover and cook on low heat, stirring occasionally. The cucumber should remain slightly crunchy.

- Remove the cooked cucumber and place it in a bowl without removing the remaining masala from the pan.

- In the same pan, add the ingredients for the salad (onion, tomato, green chili, ginger, sprouts). Stir-fry for a minute or two.

- Serve the stir-fried salad with the cucumber sabzi.

name: Karela(Bitter Gourd) Bharta
ingredients:
- 1 karela (bitter gourd), about 4-5 pieces

- 1 medium-sized onion, chopped

- 1-2 green chilies, chopped

- 1 tablespoon chopped coriander leaves

- 1/2 boiled potato or sweet potato

- 1 teaspoon mustard oil
nutrition:
- Calories: Around 80 Kcal

- Protein: Around 3 g

- Fiber: Around 6 g

- Fat: Around 2 g
method:
- Steam the karela or boil it with very little water.

- Once steamed, mash the karela.

- Add the boiled potato or sweet potato and mash it into the karela.

- Mix in the chopped onions, green chilies, chopped coriander, salt, and mustard oil.

- Combine all the ingredients thoroughly.

- Serve with dal and rice.

name: Omelette Strips With Vegetables
categories: Breakfast, Sim's Family Recipes, Ramzan Specials
ingredients:
- 2-3 eggs

- 2 tablespoons of oil

- 1 teaspoon chopped garlic

- 1 medium-sized onion, chopped in big pieces

- 1 cup carrots, cut into thin sticks

- 1 cup thinly sliced bell peppers

- 1/2 cup spring onions, cut into 1-2” pieces

- Few chopped green chilies

- 1 tablespoon chopped garlic leeks (chives)

- 1 teaspoon soy sauce

- 1 teaspoon tomato sauce

- Salt to taste

- Pepper to taste
nutrition:
- Calories: Around 300 Kcal

- Protein: Around 12 g

- Fiber: Around 5 g

- Fat: Around 20 g
method:
- Heat 1 tablespoon of oil in a pan.

- Beat the eggs with salt and pepper, pour onto the pan to make a big omelette (or 3 smaller ones). Once cooked, remove to a plate, roll, and cut thin strips. Set aside.

- In the same pan, add the remaining oil and let it warm.

- Add the chopped garlic, stir-fry for about 30 seconds.

- Stir in the chopped onion and fry for a few seconds.

- Add the sliced carrots and stir-fry for about half a minute.

- Introduce the sliced bell peppers and stir-fry for a few minutes.

- Add the chopped garlic leeks, salt, and pepper. Stir-fry briefly.

- Toss in the chopped green chilies and stir-fry for a few seconds.

- Add the soy sauce and tomato sauce, stir-fry for a few seconds.

- Mix in the omelette strips with the vegetables.

- Finally, add the chopped spring onions, stir-fry for a few seconds.

- Serve and enjoy!

- This can be a the sandwich filling too

name: Baigan(Brinjal) Ka Bhurji
ingredients:
- 1 ½ tablespoons ghee

- 1 tablespoon oil

- 1 big brinjal (cut into thick round pieces)

- 1 medium to big size onion, chopped

- 1 teaspoon chopped or grated ginger

- 1 teaspoon chopped green chilies

- ¼ teaspoon asafoetida

- 1 teaspoon whole jeera (cumin)

- ½ teaspoon dhaniya powder (coriander powder)

- 1 teaspoon jeera powder (cumin powder)

- ½ teaspoon amchur powder (dry mango powder)

- 1 teaspoon dry Kasturi methi (fenugreek leaves)

- Salt to taste

- Pinch of red chili powder
nutrition:
- Calories: Around 230 Kcal

- Protein: Around 4 g

- Fiber: Around 8 g

- Fat: Around 18 g
method:
- In a pan, heat the oil and let it warm slightly.

- Rub the cut brinjal with a little salt, turmeric, and red chili powder.

- Add the brinjal to the pan and let it cook. When one side is done, flip to cook the other side.

- Once the brinjal is cooked, remove it to a plate and cut each piece into 4 pieces.

- In the same pan, add the ghee and let it warm slightly.

- Add the asafoetida and stir for a few seconds.

- Add the whole jeera and let it splutter.

- Stir in the chopped ginger and green chilies, sauté for a minute.

- Add the chopped onions and sauté until they become translucent.

- Mix in the salt.

- Add the dhaniya and jeera powder, stir for a minute (if it's sticking, add 1 tablespoon of water and stir).

- Add the cooked cut brinjal and combine it with the onion masala.

- Sprinkle a pinch of red chili powder and amchur, mix well.

- Add the Kasturi methi and stir for a minute to infuse all the flavors.

- Serve and enjoy!

name: Corn Dal
ingredients:
- 1/4 cup raw masoor dal

- 1+1/4 teaspoon mustard seeds

- 2 whole corn cobs, cut into pieces

- 6-10 whole red chilies

- Tamarind (golf ball size)

- 4 cups of water

- Red chili powder to taste

- 1 teaspoon turmeric powder

- Salt to taste

- 1 tablespoon oil
nutrition:
- Calories: Around 220 Kcal

- Protein: Around 8 g

- Fiber: Around 6 g

- Fat: Around 6 g
method:
- Wash and soak the masoor dal to enhance digestibility by reducing phytic acid.

- Create a liquid from the tamarind pulp by adding 1/2 cup warm water. Strain to remove tamarind seeds and strings.

- In a pressure cooker, combine 4 cups of water, salt, and corn pieces. Cook on a slow flame for 25 minutes after the whistle blows.

- Open the pressure cooker and add the washed and drained masoor dal.

- Mix in red chili powder and turmeric.

- Close the pressure cooker lid and allow it to cook until just before the first whistle, then turn off the flame.

- Heat 1 tablespoon of oil in a small pan. Once warm, add mustard seeds.

- Add dry whole red chilies and stir for about a minute.

- Pour this tadka (tempering) into the cooked dal and mix.

- Gradually add the tamarind pulp water to adjust the taste.

- Check and adjust the salt as needed since the tamarind liquid might alter the saltiness.

name: Aam Panna
categories: Evening Snack, Sim's Family Recipes, Ramzan Specials
ingredients:
- 125g raw mango

- Salt (to taste)

- Black salt (to taste)

- Roasted cumin powder (1 teaspoon)

- 1/4 cup sugar/honey/jaggery (as per preference)

- Water (for cooking and dilution)

- Few sprigs of mint leaves (for serving)
nutrition:
- Calories: 200 Kcal

- Protein: 0 g

- Fiber: 0 g

- Fat: 0 g
method:
Prepare Raw Mango:

- Cut 125g of raw mango into pieces.

- In a pressure cooker, add the raw mango pieces, 1 cup of water, and a little salt.

- Pressure cook for 1 whistle.

- Allow the pressure to release naturally.

Sweetening and Straining:

- Once the cooked raw mango cools down, add sugar/honey/jaggery (as per taste preference). Allow it to sit until the sweetener melts.

- Strain the liquid through a strainer into a bottle.

Flavoring and Storing:

- Add black salt and 1 teaspoon roasted cumin powder to the strained liquid. Mix well.

- Store the prepared liquid in a bottle.

Serving:

- When serving, dilute the concentrated mixture with water as per taste preference.

- Optionally, add a few sprigs of mint leaves for enhanced flavor.

name: Orange Chilli Chicken
ingredients:
Chicken:

- 1 tablespoon cornflour / arrowroot

- 4 egg whites

- 4 boneless chicken thighs, cut into bite-sized pieces

- Salt and pepper to taste

- Dash of finely chopped garlic

Sauce:

- 1/2 cup fresh orange juice

- Half an orange rind (optional)

- 1 tablespoon soy sauce

- 1 tablespoon honey

- 1 tablespoon vinegar

- 1/4 teaspoon sesame oil / olive oil / cooking oil

- Salt to taste

- Chilli flakes / plain chilli sauce / red chilli paste to taste

- 1 clove garlic, chopped small

- A little grated or minced ginger

- Handful of spring onions
nutrition:
- Calories: 300 Kcal

- Protein: 30 g

- Fiber: 1 g

- Fat: 12 g
method:
For the Chicken:

- In a large bowl, whisk together cornflour/arrowroot and egg whites with a fork until almost frothy.

- Add the chicken pieces to the mixture and allow them to marinate for 5 to 10 minutes.

For the Sauce:

- Add oil to a non-stick pan.

- Add chopped garlic to the cold oil and allow it to brown slightly.

- Put orange juice, orange rind (if using), soy sauce, vinegar, salt, chilli paste, spring onions, and ginger into the pan and mix.

- Cook the mixture until it starts to bubble and thicken, about 5 minutes.

- Whisk together cornflour and 1/4 cup water in a small bowl. Add 1 to 2 tablespoons of the cornflour mixture to the sauce to thicken it for about a minute.

- In another non-stick pan, add a little oil and cook the marinated chicken pieces on high heat until they brown, which takes about 5 minutes. (Alternatively, use an air fryer or oven for cooking)

- Add the cooked chicken and honey to the sauce, tossing until the chicken is evenly coated.

- Top with spring onions and serve hot.

name: Lemon Basil Garlic Fried Rice
ingredients:
- 1 cup raw rice

- 3 tbsp oil

- 2 tbsp garlic, finely chopped

- 10-12 basil leaves, hand torn

- 1/2 tsp white pepper

- Juice and finely grated zest of 1 lime/lemon

- 1 tbsp fresh lime/lemon juice

- Salt to taste
nutrition:
- Fat: 300 Kcal

- Protein: 5 g

- Fiber: 1 g

- Calories: 20 g
method:
- Boil the rice and set it aside to cool.

- Heat 3 tbsp of oil in a kadhai or wok until slightly warm. Add the chopped garlic and cook on low flame until the edges start to brown.

- Add the torn basil leaves and stir-fry for a few seconds until wilted. Avoid overcooking them to retain their fragrance.

- Add the boiled and cooled rice, gently stir-frying to prevent breaking. Continue cooking on low flame.

- Season with salt to taste and the grated zest of 1 lime/lemon.

- Add 1 tbsp of lemon juice, ½ tsp of white pepper, and gently stir-fry the rice until well mixed.

- Serve hot.

name: Kasuri Methi Dal
ingredients:
- 1/4 cup black gram dal (urad dal)

- 1/4 cup split chickpeas (chana dal)

- 1/4 cup split green gram dal (moong dal)

Wet Masala:

- 1 large tomato

- 1 large onion

- 3-4 cloves of garlic

- 3-4 green chillies

- 1-inch piece ginger

Dry Masala:

- 1 tsp turmeric powder

- 1 tsp chilli powder

- 1 tsp garam masala powder

- 1 tsp roasted cumin powder (bhujia jeera powder)

- Handful of dried fenugreek leaves (kasuri methi)

- Salt to taste
nutrition:
- Calories: 150 Kcal

- Protein: 8 g

- Fiber: 4 g

- Fat: 2 g
method:
- Wash and soak the dals for about 6 hours; a minimum of 1 hour soaking is required.

- Grind the wet masala ingredients (tomato, onion, garlic, green chillies, ginger) into a paste. Add water if needed.

- In a pressure cooker, add the soaked dals, wet masala paste, and all dry masala.

- Pour in 2 cups of water and pressure cook on low flame for 2 - 3 whistles.

- Allow the pressure cooker to release pressure naturally. If the dals are not fully cooked, continue cooking until done.

- Serve hot, garnished with fresh sliced onions, lime, and fresh green garnish.

name: Daadima'S Paneer & Vegetable Recipe
ingredients:
Paneer Vegetable Stew:

- Homemade paneer (cut into cubes)

- Water used for making paneer

- 4-5 tomatoes

- 300-400g pumpkin (cut into small cubes)

- 500g carrots (cut into small cubes)

- 4 capsicums (cut into large squares)

- Handful of chopped parsley leaves (optional)

- 4-5 slit green chillies (adjust according to spice preference)

- 2 onions (ground to a paste)

- 1 1/2 tsp ginger-garlic paste

- 1 1/2 tsp whole cumin seeds (jeera)

- 1/2 tsp turmeric powder (haldi)

- 1 tsp ghee

Homemade Paneer:

- 1.5 liters whole milk

- 2 tbsp lime juice

- Cheesecloth or muslin cloth
nutrition:
- Calories: 250 Kcal

- Protein: 15 g

- Fiber: 8 g

- Fat: 10 g
method:
Paneer Vegetable Stew:

- Place all the ingredients (except jeera and ghee) into the paneer water and set it aside.

- Heat a little ghee in a pressure cooker and add the cumin seeds (jeera). Let them splutter and release their aroma.

- Add the paneer water mixture into the pressure cooker. Pressure cook for one whistle only on high flame.

- Open and serve hot with white rice.

How to Make Paneer:

- Bring whole milk to a boil in a pan.

- Once boiling, add lime juice. If the milk doesn't curdle, add more lime juice as needed.

- As soon as the milk curdles, switch off the heat. Add ice cubes to halt the cooking process.

- Pour the contents through a cheesecloth, separating the whey or paneer water.

- Gather the cloth with the paneer, gently squeeze out excess water, and shape the paneer into a block.

- Place the paneer with the cloth on a plate and place a weight on top for 30 minutes to 1 hour.

- Remove the cloth and cut the paneer into cubes.

name: High Protein Vegetable Pulao
ingredients:
- 1 onion, thinly sliced

- 1 bay leaf (tejpatha)

- 2 cloves (lavang)

- 1 small stick cinnamon (dalchini)

- 1 big black cardamom (black elaichi)

- 1 heaped tsp cumin (jeera)

- Salt to taste

- 1/4 cup brown rice

- 1/2 cup boiled and drained chickpeas (chola)

- 1 cup sliced mushrooms

- 1/4 cup green peas

- 1/4 cup chopped carrots

- 1/2 cup chopped spinach

- 1/2 cup broccoli

- 1/4 cup chickpea water (from boiling chickpeas)

- 1/2 tsp coconut or olive oil
nutrition:
- Calories: 180 Kcal

- Protein: 7 g

- Fiber: 5 g

- Fat: 4 g
method:
- Soak chickpeas (chola) overnight and then boil in water as you would for any chola recipe. Reserve the water used to boil the chickpeas.

- Slice onions lengthwise.

- Heat oil in a pressure cooker. Add onions and sauté until translucent.

- Add bay leaf, cloves, cinnamon, black cardamom, and cumin together. Sauté for a couple of minutes.

- Add all the vegetables and sauté for a couple of minutes.

- Add the brown rice, salt, and chickpea water (should be slightly salty).

- Pressure cook on high for one whistle. Then turn down the flame to medium for another whistle. Switch off the gas and allow the steam to escape on its own. If the rice isn’t cooked, cook it for a bit on the gas.

- Serve with a bowl of yogurt and a cucumber and tomato salad.

Notes:

- This recipe aims to provide a balanced meal of proteins, carbs, and good fats.

- Adjust the quantity of rice to your preference but note that the suggested amount is ideal for a meal.

- Use any whole grain, red rice, black rice, barley, bajra, millets, or white rice, adjusting water accordingly.

- Maintain mushrooms and peas if possible, but feel free to add or change other vegetables.

- Ensure all vegetables are washed properly.

- To reach nearly 20 grams of protein, it is recommended to have this recipe with a bowl of yogurt.

- Adding a spoon of ghee is suggested for children.

name: Baked Oat Meal With Apple And Raisins
ingredients:
- 1/4 cup quick cooking oats

- 1/4 cup milk (of choice)

- 1 egg

- 1/2 tsp baking powder

- 1/2 tsp cinnamon powder

- 1 ripe large banana, sliced

- 1 apple, chopped

- 6-7 walnuts, chopped

- 10 raisins

- 1 tbsp honey (optional)

- Vanilla extract (optional)

- Pinch of salt
nutrition:
- Calories: 200 Kcal

- Protein: 6 g

- Fiber: 5 g

- Fat: 9 g
method:
- Preheat oven to 180°C (356°F). Lightly grease an ovenproof dish and set it aside.

- Arrange banana slices at the bottom of the dish. Place half of the chopped apples over the bananas.

- Sprinkle half of the cinnamon powder and half of the honey over the fruits. Cover the dish with foil and bake for 15 minutes or until the bananas are soft.

- Combine the dry ingredients - oats, half of the nuts, baking powder, remaining cinnamon, and salt; stir together.

- In a separate bowl, whisk together the wet ingredients - egg, milk, remaining honey, and vanilla extract.

- Remove the fruits from the oven and spread the dry oats mixture evenly over them.

- Pour the milk mixture over the oats and sprinkle the remaining fruits and nuts on top.

- Bake the oatmeal for 30 minutes or until the top is golden brown.

- Serve warm from the oven.

Notes:

- Regular Quaker Oats were used, but you can use any plain oats, including rolled oats (not tested with steel-cut oats).

- Choose any combination of nuts and fruits; banana is recommended for a natural sweetness.

- To make it gluten-free, use gluten-free oats.

- For a dairy-free version, use a milk alternative.

- Adjust honey quantity according to personal preference.

- Baking time may vary based on the oven.

name: Baked Apple Crisps
ingredients:
- Apples of choice

- Cinnamon powder

- Brown or coconut palm sugar (optional)
nutrition:
- Calories: 100 Kcal

- Protein: 0 g

- Fiber: 3 g

- Fat: 0 g
method:
- Slice the apples as thinly as possible, preferably using a slicer or mandolin.

- Preheat the oven to 100 degrees Celsius.

- Place the sliced apples on a paper towel and pat to remove excess water.

- Arrange the apple slices on a baking tray lined with aluminum foil or parchment paper.

- Put the baking tray with apple slices into the preheated oven.

- Mix the cinnamon powder and sugar together and set it aside.

- As the slices begin to curl up around the edges, sprinkle the cinnamon and sugar mixture over them.

- Increase the oven temperature to 110 degrees Celsius and continue baking until the edges start to brown.

- Remove from the oven and let cool for at least 10 minutes.

Notes:

- The apple crisps will remain crisp for about 6 hours after preparation and are best enjoyed immediately.

- The low oven temperature dehydrates the apples, giving them a crispy texture.

- Keep an eye on them while baking as they can quickly burn.

- Place the baking tray in the center rack of the oven. If available, use the convection mode; otherwise, it might take longer.

name: Baked Oat Meal With Strawberries And Banana
ingredients:
- 1/4 cup quick-cooking oats

- 1/4 cup milk

- 1 egg

- 1/2 tsp baking powder

- 1/2 tsp cinnamon powder

- 1 ripe banana, sliced

- Handful of blueberries (frozen or fresh)

- Handful of strawberries, sliced

- 6-7 walnuts, chopped

- 6-7 raisins (optional)

- 1 tbsp honey (optional)

- Vanilla extract (optional)

- Pinch of salt
nutrition:
- Calories: Around 350 Kcal

- Protein: Around 8 g

- Fiber: Around 6 g

- Fat: Around 10 g
method:
- Preheat the oven to 180°C. Lightly grease an oven-proof dish with oil and set it aside.

- Arrange the banana slices at the bottom of the dish. Place half of the blueberries and strawberries over the bananas.

- Sprinkle half of the cinnamon powder and half of the honey over the fruits.

- Cover the dish with foil and bake for 15 minutes or until the bananas are soft.

- In a separate bowl, combine the oats, half of the chopped nuts, baking powder, remaining cinnamon, and salt. Stir the dry ingredients together.

- In another bowl, whisk together the egg, milk, remaining honey, and vanilla extract.

- Remove the fruits from the oven and evenly spread the dry oats mixture over the fruits.

- Pour the milk mixture over the oats and sprinkle the remaining fruits and nuts over the top.

- Bake the oatmeal for 30 minutes or until the top turns golden brown.

- Serve warm straight from the oven.

name: Breakfast Egg Muffins
ingredients:
- 6 eggs

- 1 small, finely chopped onion

- little garlic chopped small

- salt and pepper, to taste

- 1/4 tsp baking soda (optional)

Topping options
Tomato spinach mozzarella

- 1/4 cup fresh spinach, roughly chopped

- 10 cherry tomatoes, halved

- 1/4 cup shredded mozzarella cheese

Broccoli and mushrooms

- 1/2 cup broccoli cut small ( soaked in hot water and salt for 10 mins)

- 1/2 cup chopped mushrooms

Garlic mushroom pepper

- 1/2 cup sliced mushrooms

- 1/2 cup bell pepper, (capsicum), diced

- 1 tablespoon fresh chopped basil

- 1/2 teaspoon minced garlic
method:
- Preheat oven to 180°C. Lightly grease a muffin tray with oil.

- In a large bowl, whisk together eggs, garlic and onion. Season with salt and pepper, to taste.

- Add egg mixture halfway up into each tin of a greased muffin tin.

- Top with toppings of choice .

- Bake for 20 minutes.

- Serve or store in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 4 days and reheat when ready to serve.

Notes

- First, you’re going to beat your eggs together with salt and pepper and some finely chopped onion. Pour the egg mixture into your pan and fill with whatever you like!

- Broccoli - when using broccoli soak it in hot water and salt for at least 10 minutes and take out. This softens the broccoli and cleans it of any worms.

- Alternatively you could cook the garlic, onions and toppings in a pan before adding it to the egg mixture.

- For kids you can also add in a little cooked rice or cooked millets.

- For a higher protein option use half the number of yolks to egg whites. So 3 egg yolks and 6 whites. Adjust topping quantity as per egg quantity.

name: 1 Cup Seasonal Fruit
ingredients:
Choose any seasonal fruit of choice according to the following measures:

- Mango / Chickoo: 3/4 cup

- Ice Apple: 3 pieces

- Jackfruit: 4 pieces

- Chickoo: 3/4 cup

- Avocado: 1/2 cup
nutrition:
Calories: Around 465 kcal
Fat: Around 16.5 g
Protein: Around 7.8 g
Fiber: Around 23.1 g
method:
- Select your preferred seasonal fruit from the given options.

- Measure the specified quantity using a standard baking cup.

- If necessary, chop the fruit into smaller pieces to fit the cup measurement accurately.

name: Mustard And Poppy Seed Brinjal
ingredients:
- 300g small brinjal (6-7 pieces)

- 3 tablespoons oil (preferably mustard oil)

- 1 teaspoon onion seeds

- Few whole green chilies

- Salt to taste

- Pinch of turmeric powder

- 1 tablespoon chopped coriander leaves

- 1/2 teaspoon sugar

For the Paste:

- 1 tablespoon mustard seeds (1/2 black and 1/2 yellow mustard seeds if possible)

- 1 tablespoon poppy seeds (khus khus)

- 2-4 whole green chilies
nutrition:
- Calories: 290 Kcal

- Protein: 6 g

- Fiber: 8 g

- Fat: 25 g
method:
- Cut the brinjal into two pieces horizontally. Sprinkle a little salt and turmeric on the cut brinjal.

- In a pan, heat 2 teaspoons of oil. When the oil is warm, place the brinjal flat in the pan and let it cook. Flip the pieces once they turn slightly brown. Set aside once all are done.

- In the same pan, add the remaining oil. When warm, add onion seeds and when they start spluttering, add the whole green chilies (slit from the top).

- Add the paste and a pinch of turmeric. Sauté for 5-7 minutes.

- Pour in 1 cup of water and add sugar. Allow the gravy to bubble.

- Add the cooked brinjal. Cook until the gravy reduces to 3/4 of its original volume.

- Stir in 1 tablespoon of chopped coriander leaves.

- Remove from heat. Serve.

name: Jaggery Vermicelli
ingredients:
- 1-1 ½ tablespoons ghee

- 200g raw vermicelli (not roasted)

- 3 cups water

- 1 cup jaggery

- 1/2 teaspoon cardamom powder

- 6-8 almonds, thinly sliced
nutrition:
- Calories: 250 Kcal

- Protein: 3g

- Fiber: 1g

- Fat: 10 g
method:
- In a pan, bring the water to a boil. Add the jaggery and stir until it completely melts. Remove from heat and set aside.

- In a kadhai (wok) or pan, heat the ghee over low heat. Add the vermicelli and roast until it turns light brown.

- Pour the prepared jaggery water into the kadhai with the roasted vermicelli. Stir well.

- Once the liquid starts bubbling, reduce the heat to low, cover, and let it cook. Stir occasionally.

- Check for sweetness and add more jaggery if needed, according to taste.

- When the vermicelli has absorbed most of the liquid and becomes somewhat dry, add the cardamom powder and 3/4 of the sliced almonds. Mix well.

- Once the liquid has evaporated, and the vermicelli is cooked, garnish with the remaining almonds.

- Serve and enjoy!

name: Chicken Malai Curry(No Cream)
ingredients:
For Chicken Marination:

- 150g chicken

- 1/2 teaspoon ginger paste

- 1/2 teaspoon garlic paste

- 1/4 lemon (juice)

For Curry:

- 1 tablespoon oil

- 1 medium-sized onion (grated or ground to paste)

- 1-2 slit green chilies

- 2 bay leaves

- 2 whole red chilies

- 4 cloves

- 1 piece cinnamon

- 3-4 green cardamom pods

- 1 teaspoon whole cumin seeds

- Pinch of turmeric powder

- Red chili powder to taste

- Salt to taste

- 1/2 teaspoon sugar

- 1 tablespoon cashews (kaju)

- 2 tablespoons grated coconut
nutrition:
- Fat: 12g

- Protein: 18g

- Fiber: 2g

- Calories: 220 kcal
method:
- Marinate Chicken: Combine chicken pieces with ginger paste, garlic paste, and lemon juice. Set aside for marination.

- Prepare Curry:
- In a kadhai or pan, heat oil over medium heat.

- Add bay leaves, whole red chilies, cinnamon, cardamom, cloves, and whole cumin seeds. Let them splutter.

- Add grated/ground onions. Sauté until onions turn slightly brown.

- Add the marinated chicken and sauté for 5-10 minutes.

- Stir in turmeric powder, red chili powder, and salt. Sauté until the masala turns brown.

- In a separate grinder, make a paste using cashews and grated coconut. Add this paste to the kadhai and sauté until well combined.

- Introduce slit green chilies and continue cooking until the oil starts separating from the sides.

- Add sugar and mix well. Cook for a few more minutes on low flame.

- If more gravy is desired, add hot water and simmer until the chicken is fully cooked.

- Serve: Once done, the dish is ready to be served.

name: Kadhai Mushrooms
categories: Lunch, Dinner, Sim's Family Recipes, Breakfast
ingredients:
- Vegetables:
- 1 packet fresh mushrooms (cut into quarters)

- 1 capsicum (cut into big cubes)

- 2 onions (cut into cubes)

For Masala:

- 1 tablespoon oil

- 1/2 teaspoon whole cumin

- 2 cardamom pods

- 3-4 cloves

- 1 medium-sized onion (sliced)

- 1 piece ginger (cut into pieces)

- 1 tomato (cut into cubes)

- Few green chilies

- Pinch of salt

- Pinch of turmeric powder

For Cooking:

- 2 tablespoons oil

- 2 bay leaves

- 1 piece cinnamon stick

- 2-3 teaspoons curd (yogurt)

- Pinch of roasted cumin powder
nutrition:
- Calories: 250 Kcal

- Protein: 6 g

- Fiber: 4 g

- Fat: 18 g
method:
Prepare Masala:

- Heat 1 tablespoon oil in a kadhai.

- Add whole cumin, cloves, and cardamom.

- Once the cumin splutters, add sliced onion and ginger. Sauté until onions become translucent.

- Add a pinch of salt and turmeric. Sauté for a few more minutes.

- Introduce cut tomato and green chilies. Sauté for 5-10 minutes on low to medium heat.

- Remove from heat and allow it to cool down. Grind this mixture into a smooth paste.

Cooking:

- In the same kadhai, add 2 tablespoons of oil. Warm the oil.

- Add bay leaves and cinnamon stick.

- Put in the ground masala paste and sauté for 5-10 minutes.

- Add onions and stir for a few minutes.

- Add capsicum and stir for a few more minutes.

- Introduce mushrooms and sauté for a bit.

- Season with red chili powder and salt according to taste (considering some salt and green chilies are already present).

- Pour in the curd and cook for 5-7 minutes.

- Finally, add the tomato and cook for another 5-7 minutes.

- Sprinkle a pinch of roasted cumin.

- Once done, the dish is ready to be served.

name: Papad Ki Kadhi
ingredients:
- 1/2 cup Yogurt (curd)

- 2 tablespoons besan (gram flour)

- 2-3 tablespoons oil/ghee

- 1/4 teaspoon asafoetida

- 1/2 teaspoon whole cumin seeds

- 1/2 teaspoon mustard seeds

- 1 teaspoon whole coriander seeds (dhaniya seeds)

- 3-4 bay leaves

- 4-5 whole red chillies

- 4 cloves

- 1/2 teaspoon turmeric powder

- Red chilli powder according to taste

- Salt according to taste

- 3/4 teaspoon ginger paste

- 1/2 teaspoon garlic paste

- 1/2 teaspoon kasuri methi (dried fenugreek leaves)

- 15-20 curry leaves

- 3-5 papads (roasted and kept aside)

- Water, as needed (approximately 1.5 liters)
nutrition:
- Calories: 150 Kcal

- Protein: 5 g

- Fiber: 3 g

- Fat: 10 g
method:
- Whip together besan and yogurt until well combined. Set aside.

- In a large kadhai, heat oil/ghee.

- Add asafoetida, whole cumin seeds, mustard seeds, and coriander seeds. Stir for a few seconds.

- Add whole red chillies, bay leaves, curry leaves, ginger-garlic paste, and sauté for a few minutes. If the masala sticks, add 3-4 tablespoons of water.

- Mix in turmeric powder and red chilli powder. Add a little water and sauté for a minute.

- Pour in the besan-yogurt mixture and stir well.

- Add approximately 1.5 liters of water (adjust for desired consistency).

- Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce the flame and let it cook.

- Season with salt according to taste.

- When the gravy settles down, check for salt, spice, and consistency.

- Crush kasuri methi and sprinkle it on top.

- Just before serving, break the roasted papads into pieces and add them to the kadhi.

name: Papad Ka Raita
ingredients:
- 250 grams Yogurt/Curd

- 1-2 Roasted Papad (broken into bits, masala papad used here)

- 2 tsp Chopped Coriander Leaves

- Salt (according to taste)

- ¼ tsp Roasted Cumin Powder

- Pinch of Red Chilli Powder

- Pinch of Chat Masala
nutrition:
- Calories: Around 120 Kcal

- Protein: Around 7 g

- Fiber: Around 2 g

- Fat: Around 8 g
method:
- Whip the yogurt and add salt, red chilli powder, chat masala, roasted cumin powder, and chopped coriander leaves.

- Mix well and refrigerate.

- Just before serving, add roasted papad pieces. Gently mix.

- Garnish with coriander leaves and a sprinkle of roasted cumin powder.

- Serve immediately.

name: Aachari Chicken/Lamb
ingredients:
- 500 grams Chicken

- 3-4 tbsp Oil (preferably mustard oil)

- 4 medium-sized Onions, sliced

- 2-inch piece Ginger, julienned

- 2 big Tomatoes, sliced

- 6-7 Whole Red Chillies

- 2 Bay Leaves

- 1 tsp Red Chilli Powder

- ½ tsp Turmeric Powder

- Salt (according to taste)

- 3-6 Whole Green Chillies

- Pinch of Cumin Powder
nutrition:
- Calories: Around 350 Kcal

- Protein: Around 30 g

- Fiber: Around 5 g

- Fat: Around 25 g
method:
- Heat oil in a kadhai.

- Add whole red chillies and bay leaf. Stir for a few minutes.

- Add sliced onions and stir-fry for 5-7 minutes.

- Add ginger julienne and stir-fry until onions become translucent.

- Include sliced tomatoes and sauté for a few minutes.

- Add salt, red chilli powder, and turmeric. Sauté for a few minutes.

- Add the chicken and sauté on medium flame until it releases water.

- Cover and cook until the chicken is done, stirring occasionally.

- Adjust gravy consistency according to preference.

- Sprinkle a pinch of cumin powder.

- Ready to serve.

name: Onion Chicken
ingredients:
- 1 ½ tbsp of Oil

- 500 gms Chicken

- Salt (to taste)

- Red Chilli Powder (according to taste)

- ¼ tsp Coriander Powder

- Pinch of Turmeric Powder

- 3-4 Cloves

- 1 Black Cardamom

- 1 piece Cinnamon Stick (1-inch)

- 2 Onions (cut into 4 pieces)

- ½ tsp Garam Masala

To be sautéed and ground to a paste:

- 2 medium-sized Onions (sliced)

- 1 big Tomato (chopped)

- 1 tsp Ginger Paste

- 1 tsp Garlic Paste

- Few Green Chillies

- ½ tsp Whole Cumin

- 1 ½ tbsp of Oil
nutrition:
- Calories: Around 350 Kcal

- Protein: Around 35 g

- Fiber: Around 5 g

- Fat: Around 25 g
method:
- Heat 1 ½ tbsp of oil in a kadhai.

- Add whole cumin. Once it starts spluttering, add the sliced onions and cook until translucent.

- Add ginger-garlic paste and sauté until the raw smell disappears.

- Include chopped tomato and green chillies. Sauté until onions turn slightly brown and tomatoes become soft. Cook for 5-10 minutes on medium heat, occasionally stirring. Add 1-2 tbsp of water while sautéing. Once golden brown, remove from heat and let it cool down. Then, grind to a smooth paste. Add water if needed. Set aside.

- In the same kadhai, add 1 ½ tbsp of oil. Warm it slightly.

- Add cloves, cinnamon, and cardamom. After a few seconds, add the cooked masala paste.

- Sauté for a few minutes. Add salt, red chilli powder, turmeric powder, and coriander powder. Sauté on low to medium flame until the moisture from the masala dries up.

- Add the chicken and sauté for 5-10 minutes.

- Cover and cook on low flame until the chicken is cooked. Stir occasionally. If needed, add ½ cup water if the chicken doesn't release enough liquid.

- When the chicken is ¾ done, add the cut onions and sauté for a few minutes.

- Add garam masala and cook for a few more minutes.

- Done.

name: Paneer Peas Stuffed Paratha
ingredients:
- Dough kneaded and kept aside

- 1 cup Peas (cooked and mashed)

- 1-1½ cups Crushed Paneer

- 1 large Onion (chopped)

- 1 tbsp Chopped Ginger

- 2-3 tbsp Chopped Coriander Leaves

- Chopped Green Chillies (according to taste)

- Salt (according to taste)

To Prepare the Peas:

- Heat 2 tsp of ghee in a kadhai.

- Add 1/4 tsp of asafoetida and 1/4 tsp of whole cumin. When the cumin splutters, add the peas (frozen peas are used here).

- Stir for a few seconds, then add a pinch of turmeric powder, a pinch of red chilli powder, 1/4 tsp of coriander powder, 1/2 tsp of roasted cumin powder, salt to taste, and optional ¼-½ tsp of chilli flakes.

- Stir the spices and cook until the peas are done. Mash and set aside to mix with other ingredients.
nutrition:
- Calories: Around 300 Kcal

- Protein: Around 15 g

- Fiber: Around 5 g

- Fat: Around 15 g
method:
- Mix all the ingredients including the cooked peas together.

- Combine well to allow the flavors to infuse.

- Make balls from the prepared dough.

- Roll out a dough ball into a small circle and place the peas and paneer mixture in the center.

- Bring all the edges to the center and seal the top. Gently press and roll out the dough.

- Heat a tawa and place the stuffed roti on it. Cook slightly, then flip the side.

- Spread a little ghee on the top using a brush. Flip again and cook until brown spots appear on top. Repeat on the other side.

- Done. Serve with curd and chutney.

name: Manchoorian Mince Balls With Bell Pepper And Onions
ingredients:
For the Mince Balls:

- 500g Chicken Mince

- Salt (to taste)

- Juice of ½ Lime

- ½ tsp Pepper

- ¼ cup Small Chopped Chives/Spring Onions

- 2 slices of Bread (grated)

- ½ Egg

For the Sauce:

- 4 tbsp Tomato Ketchup

- 2 tbsp Vinegar

- 1 ½ tbsp Soy Sauce

- 2-3 tbsp Honey

- 2 tsp Corn Flour mixed in ¼ cup Water

For the Vegetables:

- 1 Yellow Bell Pepper (cut into cubes)

- 1 Red Bell Pepper (cut into cubes)

- 2 Onions (cut into cubes)

- 1 cup Spring Onions (1" cut)

- 3 tsp Chopped Garlic

- Salt and Pepper (to taste)

- 2 tbsp Oil

For Gravy (Optional):

- 2 cups Boiling Water/Stock
nutrition:
- Calories: Around 350 Kcal

- Protein: Around 25 g

- Fiber: Around 4 g

- Fat: Around 15 g
method:
To Cook the Mince Balls:

- Mix all the chicken mince ball ingredients together.

- Shape them into balls and set aside.

- Heat 1 tbsp oil in a pan, add the balls, and cook on low flame until done. Alternatively, use an air fryer to cook them.

For the Sauce:

- Mix tomato ketchup, vinegar, soy sauce, and honey together. Set aside.

- Mix cornflour with water separately and keep aside.

For Vegetables and Gravy:

- Heat oil in a kadhai and warm it slightly.

- Stir-fry chopped garlic until light brown.

- Add bell peppers, stir-fry for a minute, then add onions.

- Season with salt and pepper.

- Pour in the mixed sauces, stir well.

- Add the cornflour paste, stir until it thickens.

- Gently add the cooked mince balls, coat them with the sauce.

- Add chopped spring onions, mix briefly, and keep on flame for a few seconds. Then, it's ready.

Optional Gravy:

- If desired, for a gravy consistency, add 2 cups of boiling water/stock to the kadhai.

- Once the gravy thickens, remove from heat.

name: Coffee Hung Curd Chia Pudding
ingredients:
- 2 tbsp Chia Seeds

- ½ cup Black Coffee

- 1 tbsp Cocoa Powder

- ½ tsp Honey

- 3 tbsp Hung Curd/Yogurt

- Favourite Fruits (to serve, optional)
nutrition:
- Calories: Around 300 Kcal

- Protein: Around 10 g

- Fiber: Around 12 g

- Fat: Around 15 g
method:
- In a container, combine 2 tbsp chia seeds with ½ cup black coffee, 1 tbsp cocoa powder, and ½ tsp honey. Mix well.

- Refrigerate the mixture overnight to allow the chia seeds to soak and thicken.

- In the morning, layer the soaked chia mixture with 3 tbsp of hung curd.

- Optionally, add your favorite fruits on top to balance the bitterness of the coffee.

Notes:

- The recommended ratio of hung curd to the chia mixture is 3:2.

- Adjust the ratio to suit your preference for the taste of black coffee.

name: Chicken Pulao
ingredients:
- 500 gms Chicken

- 2 large Onions (sliced)

- 1 large Tomato (chopped)

- 1 tsp Ginger Paste

- 1 tsp Garlic Paste

- 2-3 tbsp Peas

- 1 Potato (cut into 8 pieces, optional)

- Few Slit Green Chillies (to taste)

- Salt (to taste)

- Red Chilli Powder (to taste)

- ½ tsp Turmeric Powder

- ¼ tsp Cumin Powder

- ¼ tsp Coriander Powder (Dhaniya Powder)

- ½ tsp Garam Masala

- 2-3 Bay Leaves

- 1 tsp Whole Cumin Seeds

- 4 Cloves

- 1 piece of Cinnamon Stick

- 3 Green Cardamom Pods

- 3 tbsp Oil/Ghee

- 1 ½ cups Rice (washed and soaked for 30 minutes)
nutrition:
- Calories: Around 400 Kcal

- Protein: Around 25 g

- Fiber: Around 5 g

- Fat: Around 15 g
method:
- Heat oil/ghee in a kadhai or pan over medium heat.

- Add cloves, cinnamon stick, cardamom pods, bay leaves, and whole cumin seeds to the warm oil/ghee.

- Once the cumin seeds start spluttering, add the sliced onions. Cook until the onions turn translucent and light brown.

- Stir in ginger-garlic paste and sauté until the raw smell fades.

- Add chopped tomatoes and whole green chillies. Cook until the tomatoes become mushy.

- Add chicken pieces and sauté for a few minutes.

- Season with salt, red chilli powder, turmeric powder, coriander powder, cumin powder, and garam masala. Sauté until the chicken is ¾ cooked and turns golden brown.

- Add the potato pieces and sauté for a few minutes.

- Pour in 3 cups of water and add peas. Stir well.

- Add the soaked rice, adjust salt if needed, and mix thoroughly.

- Once the water starts bubbling, cover the pan and cook on low flame until the rice is fully cooked.

- Turn off the flame and let it rest for some time.

- Serve the Chicken Pulao with salad and raita.

name: Paneer Ki Sabzi
categories: Dinner, Lunch, Sim's Family Recipes, Breakfast
ingredients:
- 250 gms Paneer (cut into thick strips)

- 2 ½ Bell Peppers (colors of your choice), thinly sliced

- 1 large Onion, sliced

Paste to be ground and kept aside:

- 2 large Tomatoes

- 3-5 Whole Green Chillies

For Cooking:

- 1 tsp Whole Cumin

- 1/4 tsp Turmeric Powder

- Salt (to taste)

- Red Chilli Powder (to taste, considering green chillies in the paste)

- 1 tsp Ginger Paste

- 2-3 tbsp Oil/Ghee
nutrition:
- Calories: Around 350 Kcal

- Protein: Around 20 g

- Fiber: Around 5 g

- Fat: Around 15 g
method:
- Heat oil/ghee in a pan.

- Add whole cumin seeds to the warmed oil/ghee.

- Once the cumin seeds start spluttering, add ginger paste and sauté for a minute.

- If the ginger starts sticking to the pan, add 1-2 tbsp of water.

- Add turmeric powder.

- Put the tomato-green chilli paste in the pan and sauté for a few minutes.

- Add red chilli powder and continue sautéing until the water from the tomatoes evaporates, and oil begins to separate from the sides.

- Incorporate the sliced onions and sauté for a few minutes.

- Add bell peppers and mix well with the onions and masala.

- Season with salt.

- Cover and cook for a few minutes until the onions and bell peppers are ¾ cooked.

- Gently add the paneer, ensuring it doesn't break. Mix gently.

- Cover and cook for a few more minutes.

- Stir in 1-2 tbsp of chopped coriander leaves, then remove from heat. Done.

name: Channa Dal And Peas Pulao
ingredients:
- 1 cup raw Rice (soaked for 30 minutes to 1 hour)

- 1 cup Chana Dal (soaked for 1 to 1 1/2 hours)

- 1 cup Peas

- 2-3 tablespoons Oil/Ghee

- 2 Bay Leaves

- 4 Whole Red Chillies

- 4 Green Cardamom Pods

- 4-5 Cloves

- 1 teaspoon Whole Cumin Seeds

- 1 sliced Onion

- 1 teaspoon Ginger Paste

- 1/2 teaspoon Turmeric Powder

- Salt to taste

- Red Chilli Powder to taste

- 1/2 teaspoon Garam Masala

- Water (approximately 3 1/2 cups)
nutrition:
- Calories: Around 400 Kcal

- Protein: Around 15 g

- Fiber: Around 7 g

- Fat: Around 40 g
method:
- Heat oil/ghee in a kadhai or deep pan.

- Add bay leaves, whole red chillies, cloves, cinnamon stick, and cardamom. After a few seconds, add the whole cumin seeds.

- When the cumin seeds start to splutter, add the sliced onion. Sauté until it turns a light golden brown.

- Add ginger paste and sauté until the raw smell fades. If the masala sticks to the bottom of the kadhai, add 2-3 tablespoons of water.

- Drain the water from the soaked Chana dal and add it to the masala. Mix well.

- Add turmeric powder and red chilli powder according to taste. Sauté for a few minutes.

- Drain the water from the soaked rice and add it to the kadhai. Mix well.

- Add salt and garam masala powder. Sauté for a few minutes.

- Add peas and mix well.

- Pour water into the mixture (use a ratio of 1:2 for rice and dal, slightly less water if desired for separate grains, approximately 3 1/2 cups). Cover and cook until done.

name: Tava Keema (Mince)
ingredients:
- 250 grams Mince

- 1 ½ tablespoons Oil

- 1 large Onion, chopped

- 1 Tomato, chopped

- Few Whole Green Chillies

- Few Chopped Green Chillies

- 1 tablespoon Ginger Juliennes

- 1 Onion, cut into rings

- 1-2 tablespoons Chopped Coriander Leaves

- 1/2 teaspoon Garlic Paste

- 1/2 teaspoon Ginger Paste

- Salt, to taste

- Red Chilli Powder, to taste

- 1/4 teaspoon Turmeric Powder

- 1/4 teaspoon Dhaniya (Coriander) Powder

- 1/4 teaspoon Cumin Powder

- 1/4 teaspoon Garam Masala Powder
nutrition:
- Calories: Around 300 kcal

- Protein: Around 25 g

- Fat: Around 20 g

- Fiber: Around 4 g
method:
- Place a flat pan or tava on the stove and heat it.

- Spread the mince immediately onto the heated tava.

- Add chopped onions, ginger-garlic paste, chopped tomato, and chopped green chillies on top of the mince.

- Sprinkle turmeric powder, red chilli powder, salt, garam masala, dhaniya powder, and cumin powder. Gently mix the spices into the mince.

- Stir gently for a minute. The mince will release its natural juices. Reduce the flame to low, cover, and cook, stirring occasionally.

- Once the water evaporates, add 1 ½ tablespoons of oil. Saute on low flame until the mince turns a nice brown color.

- When the mince is ¾ cooked, add whole green chillies and ginger juliennes. Allow it to cook on low flame.

- After a few minutes, add the chopped coriander leaves. You can add 2-3 tablespoons of water for sautéing.

- Place the onion rings on top, cover, and cook for a few minutes. Gently mix the onion rings into the mince.

- Once the onions are ¾ done, remove from heat.

name: Tangy Bhindi Masala(Lady'S Finger)
ingredients:
- 500 grams Bhindi (Okra), dried and cut into 1-inch pieces

- 1 big Onion, chopped

- 1 big Tomato, chopped

- 10-12 Garlic Pods, whole

- 2 Onions, cut into quarters

- 10-15 Curry Leaves

- 2-3 teaspoons Tamarind Pulp

- 1/4 teaspoon Methi (Fenugreek) Seeds

- 1/2 teaspoon Mustard Seeds

- 1/2 teaspoon Whole Cumin

- 2-3 Whole Red Chillies

- 2-3 tablespoons Oil

- Salt, to taste

- Red Chilli Powder, to taste

- 1/4 teaspoon Dhaniya (Coriander) Powder

- 1/4 teaspoon Turmeric Powder
nutrition:
- Calories: Around 200 kcal

- Fat: Around 12 g

- Protein: Around 4 g

- Fiber: Around 7 g
method:
- Heat oil in a pan and add mustard seeds, whole cumin, methi seeds, and whole red chillies.

- Once the seeds start spluttering, add chopped onions and sauté till translucent.

- Add whole garlic pods and continue sautéing till the onions turn golden.

- Add chopped tomatoes and sauté until they soften.

- Add salt, turmeric powder, red chilli powder, and coriander powder. Stir for a few seconds.

- Cook the masala until it turns soft and gains a reddish hue, approximately 5-10 minutes.

- Add curry leaves and sauté for a few more minutes.

- Add the cut bhindi (okra) and mix well. Sauté for a few minutes.

- Lower the flame, cover, and cook until the bhindi is half done.

- Add the quartered onions and continue cooking on low flame until the bhindi is completely cooked, stirring occasionally.

- Finally, add the tamarind pulp and mix thoroughly. Cook for a few more minutes and remove from heat.

name: Oats Flour Dimsums And Tomato Chutney
ingredients:
For Oats Flour Dimsums:

- 25 grams Oats Flour

- 10 grams Cabbage, finely chopped

- 10 grams Onion, finely chopped

- 1-inch Ginger, grated

- 10 grams Minced Soya

- Salt, to taste

For Tomato Chutney:

- 20 grams Tomato

- 1 Garlic Clove

- 2 Dry Red Chillies

- Salt, to taste

- Pinch of Black Pepper Powder
nutrition:
- Calories: Around 250 kcal

- Fat: Around 6 g

- Protein: Around 10 g

- Fiber: Around 8 g
method:
For Oats Flour Dimsums:

- Roast the oats flour on a pan until it turns slightly golden. Make a dough by gradually adding a small quantity of water. Set aside.

For Filling:

- Boil soya chunks in water for 2 minutes. Once cooled, drain the water and mince in a grinder.

- In a bowl, mix finely chopped cabbage, onion, minced soya, grated ginger, and salt.

- Sauté the mixed vegetables in a pan until slightly cooked. Add minced soya and a pinch of black pepper.

- Roll out thin small rounds of dough.

- Wet the edges with water, place ¾ tsp of filling, and fold them into a half-moon shape.

- Steam for 15 minutes.

For Tomato Chutney:

- Blanch tomatoes in water for 5 minutes, remove the skin.

- In a grinder, add tomatoes, garlic clove, dry red chilies, and salt. Grind into a smooth texture.

- Remove the chutney from the grinder and serve.

name: Nimbu Pani Popsicles
ingredients:
- 15 ml Lemon Juice

- 1 tsp Honey

- 1 pinch Salt

- 1 pinch Black Salt

- Water (quantity not specified)
nutrition:
- Calories: Around 20 kcal

- Fat: 0 g

- Protein: 0 g

- Fiber: 0 g
method:
- In a cup of water, add 1 tsp of honey and stir well until the honey dissolves.

- Squeeze the juice from the lemon using a handheld squeezer into the water-honey mixture.

- Add a pinch of black salt and regular salt into the mixture and mix well.

- Fill up popsicle moulds with the prepared mixture.

- Freeze the popsicles for approximately 4-5 hours until they solidify.

name: Raita
ingredients:

- 10g onion

- 30g cucumber

- 1 green chilli (de-seeded and chopped )

- 1 tsp coriander leaves

- ¼ tsp cumin powder

- salt to taste
nutrition:
- Calories: Around 65 kcal

- Fat: Around 3.5 g

- Protein: Around 3 g

- Fiber: Around 1.5 g
method:
- Chill curd, wash and chop onion, cucumber and green chillies, coriander leaves.

- Add curd and salt to a mixing bowl and whisk them until smooth.

- Add cucumber , onion, green chilli, coriander leaves and stir.

- Sprinkle cumin powder on top.

name: Tomato Raita
ingredients:

- 1 green chili (de-seeded and chopped)

- 1 tsp coriander leaves

- Salt to taste
nutrition:

- Fat: Around 2 g

- Protein: Around 2 g

- Fiber: Around 1.5 g
method:
- Chill the curd. Wash and chop the onion, tomato, green chili, and coriander leaves.

- Add curd and salt to a mixing bowl. Whisk until smooth.

- Stir in the chopped tomato, onion, green chili, and coriander leaves.

- Sprinkle cumin powder on top.

name: Coconut Chutney
ingredients:
- 50 grams raw coconut

- 5 grams green coriander

- 5 grams green chillies

- 5 grams tamarind pulp

- Salt to taste

For Tadka:

- ½ tsp oil

- ¼ tsp mustard seeds

- ¼ tsp whole cumin seeds

- Few curry leaves

- ¼ tsp urad dal
nutrition:
- Calories: Around 90 kcal

- Fat: Around 6 g

- Protein: Around 1 g

- Fiber: Around 2 g
method:
- Peel the hard skin of the coconut, wash, and cut it into small pieces.

- In a mixer, combine coconut, green coriander, green chilies, tamarind pulp, and 2 tbsp water. Blend to make a fine paste.

- Transfer the chutney into a bowl. Adjust the consistency by adding water to your desired thickness.

- Heat oil in a small frying pan. Add mustard and whole cumin seeds. Once they splutter, turn off the heat. Add a few curry leaves and mix in the oil.

- Pour this tadka (tempering) into the chutney and mix properly.

name: Oats Egg White Omelette
ingredients:
- 10g oats

- 50g egg whites

- 10g onions, chopped

- 10g tomato, chopped

- 10g capsicum, chopped

- 2 garlic cloves, crushed

- 1 green chili, chopped

- ½ tsp coriander leaves

- Pinch of black pepper powder

- Pinch of turmeric powder

- ½ tsp oregano powder

- Salt to taste

- ½ tsp oil
nutrition:
- Calories: Around 95 kcal

- Fat: Around 3 g

- Protein: Around 8 g

- Fiber: Around 2 g
method:
- Grind oats in a blender until a powder is attained.

- In a large bowl, combine oats flour, salt, turmeric, oregano, pepper, and chopped vegetables.

- Add egg whites to the mixture and whisk thoroughly.

- Heat a pan, apply oil, and preheat the pan.

- Pour the omelette batter onto the pan, spreading it evenly.

- Cook on both sides until it turns golden brown. Then, turn off the flame.

- Divide the cooked omelette into equal pieces and serve with mint chutney.

name: Besan Capsicum Chilla
ingredients:
- 25g Gram flour

- 15g capsicum

- 10g chopped onions

- 10g chopped tomatoes

- ½ tsp chopped ginger

- ½ tsp chopped coriander leaves

- 1 chopped green chili

- ½ tsp carom seeds

- 5g curd

- 1 tsp oil

- Salt to taste
nutrition:
- Calories: Around 135 kcal

- Fat: Around 5 g

- Protein: Around 6 g

- Fiber: Around 4 g
method:
Making the Batter:

- In a large bowl, combine gram flour, carom seeds, all the vegetables, chopped ginger, chopped coriander leaves, chopped green chili, and mix thoroughly until the flour coats the vegetables.

- Add curd to the mixture. Gradually add water while stirring to make a lump-free, runny batter. Adjust the water to achieve the right consistency. Perform a taste test to check for salt.

Cooking the Cheela:

- Heat a pan or tawa over medium heat. Once hot, drizzle about a teaspoon of oil and let it heat up.

- Pour a ladleful of batter onto the pan, spreading it to form a round pancake shape.

- Allow the cheela to cook on one side for about 2 minutes or until it turns golden brown.

- Optionally, drizzle some oil on the top surface, then flip it using a spatula.

- Cook the other side for 1-2 minutes until both sides are cooked evenly.

- Once cooked, transfer the cheela to a plate and serve.

name: Hung Curd Open Sandwich With Cabbage
ingredients:
For Sandwich Spread:

- 10g thick curd / hung curd / yogurt

- Pinch of pepper powder

- 10g Cabbage

- 3g Corn

- 3g Carrot

- Salt to taste

For Sandwich:

- 2 slices whole grain bread

- Sesame seeds (til)
nutrition:
- Calories: Around 140 kcal

- Fat: Around 2 g

- Protein: Around 5 g

- Fiber: Around 4 g
method:
Sandwich Spread:

- In a large mixing bowl, take thick curd (preferably hung curd).

- Add crushed or powdered pepper according to your spice preference.

- Sprinkle salt to taste and mix well.

- Add finely chopped vegetables like carrot, cabbage, and corn. Mix thoroughly and set aside.

Sandwich Recipe:

- Cut the edges of the whole grain bread slices.

- Generously spread the prepared sandwich spread over one side of a bread slice.

- Cover it with another bread slice, creating a sandwich.

- Heat a tawa or use a sandwich maker. Sprinkle sesame seeds over it.

- Place the prepared sandwich on the tawa or sandwich maker.

- Once one side of the bread turns golden brown, flip it and repeat the step of adding sesame seeds.

- Toast the other side of the bread by gently pressing it.

- To serve, cut the sandwich in half or serve it whole.

- Enjoy the curd sandwich with mint chutney.

name: Vermicelli Upma With Vegetables
ingredients:
- 30g vermicelli

- Water (as needed for cooking)

- 1 tsp oil

- ½ tsp mustard seeds

- ½ tsp urad dal (split black gram)

- 1 tsp chana dal (split chickpeas)

- 1 green chili

- Few curry leaves

- 5g peanuts

- 1-inch ginger

- Pinch of turmeric powder

- 10g onion (chopped)

- 10g beans (chopped)

- 5g carrot (chopped)

- ½ tsp chopped coriander leaves

- Salt to taste

- Few drops of lemon juice
nutrition:
- Calories: Around 200 kcal

- Fat: Around 8 g

- Protein: Around 6 g

- Fiber: Around 4 g
method:
- Cook the vermicelli according to package instructions using water. Drain and set aside.

- In a kadai or pan, heat 1 tsp of oil. Add mustard seeds, urad dal, chana dal, 1 chopped green chili, and a few curry leaves. Allow them to splutter.

- Add peanuts and roast them until they turn crunchy on a low flame.

- Add 1-inch grated ginger and sauté.

- Add chopped onion and sauté until translucent.

- Now, add chopped carrot and beans. Sauté for a minute.

- Sprinkle a pinch of turmeric powder and salt. Sauté for another minute.

- Cover and cook for about 2 minutes or until the vegetables become soft.

- Add the cooked vermicelli to the kadai and mix gently to combine. Avoid over-mixing to prevent the vermicelli from getting mashed.

- Add 2 tbsp chopped coriander leaves and squeeze in the juice of half a lemon. Mix well.

- Serve the vermicelli upma hot, paired with hot masala chai for a delightful morning breakfast.

name: Ginger Chutney
ingredients:
- 1 tsp oil

- 25g chopped ginger

- 20g Onion

- 6 green chillies

- 1 red chilli

- Few tamarind pieces

- 1 tsp grated coconut

- Coriander leaves

- ¼ tsp salt

- Water (as needed)

- 2 tsp jaggery

- ¼ tsp urad dal (split black gram)

- ¼ tsp whole cumin seeds

- ¼ tsp mustard seeds

- Curry leaves

- Pinch of asafoetida powder
nutrition:
- Calories: Around 70 kcal

- Fat: Around 3 g

- Protein: Around 1 g

- Fiber: Around 1 g
method:
- In a pan, add oil, chopped ginger, onion, green chillies, and red chilli. Sauté for 5 minutes. Then, add grated coconut, coriander leaves, and salt to taste. Sauté again and let it cool.

- Once cooled, grind all the sautéed ingredients with a little water. Then add jaggery and grind it again to form a paste.

- In another pan, heat oil and add urad dal, whole cumin seeds, mustard seeds, curry leaves, 1 red chilli, and a pinch of asafoetida.

- Add this tempering to the ground chutney.

name: Curd Rice
ingredients:
- 25g rice

- 25 ml curd

- 3-4 red chillies

- 2 tsp mustard seeds

- 10g onion

- Salt to taste

- Curry leaves

- Oil (amount not specified)

- Garlic (amount not specified)

- Coriander leaves (amount not specified)
nutrition:
- Calories: Around 120 kcal

- Fat: Around 2 g

- Protein: Around 2 g

- Fiber: Around 1 g
method:
- Cook the rice according to usual method and keep it aside.

- In a pan, heat oil. Add mustard seeds, curry leaves, garlic, chopped onion, and red chillies. Sauté until fragrant and onions turn translucent.

- Add curd and salt to the sautéed mixture. Mix well.

- Combine this mixture with the cooked rice and mix thoroughly.

- Garnish the prepared rice with coriander leaves.

name: Apple Chips
ingredients:
- 10 grams sliced apple

- ½ tsp black pepper powder

- ½ tsp chili powder

- Cinnamon powder

- Salt to taste
nutrition:
- Calories: Around 15 kcal

- Fat: Around 0.1 g

- Protein: Around 0.1 g

- Fiber: Around 0.5 g
method:
- Slice the apple and place it in a bowl.

- Add chili powder, black pepper powder, a sprinkle of cinnamon powder, and salt. Mix the spices well with the sliced apple.

- Air fry the seasoned apple slices.

- Serve the air-fried apple slices with a yogurt dip.

name: Mint Chutney
ingredients:
- 15g mint leaves

- 10g coconut

- 3 green chilies

- 5g onion

- 2 garlic cloves

- ¼ tsp mustard seeds

- 5g tamarind

- 1 tsp oil

- Salt to taste
nutrition:
- Calories: Around 60 kcal

- Fat: Around 4 g

- Protein: Around 1 g

- Fiber: Around 2 g
method:
- Wash the mint leaves thoroughly and place them into a blender jar.

- Add coconut, green chilies, onion, garlic, and tamarind into the blender with the mint leaves.

- Blend all the ingredients into a smooth paste.

- Season the chutney with salt according to taste preference.

- Heat oil in a kadhai (pan) and add mustard seeds. Let them splutter.

- Garnish the mint chutney with the spluttered mustard seeds along with the oil and some mint leaves.

- Serve the mint chutney.

name: Curry Leaves Chutney
ingredients:
- 15g curry leaves

- 10g coconut

- 5g tamarind

- ¼ tsp jeera (cumin seeds)

- 3 green chilies

- 3 garlic cloves

- 5g onion

- Salt to taste
nutrition:
- Calories: Around 50 kcal

- Fat: Around 2 g

- Protein: Around 1 g

- Fiber: Around 1 g
method:
- Wash the curry leaves thoroughly and place them in a blender jar.

- Add coconut, green chilies, garlic, onion, tamarind, and jeera to the blender with the curry leaves.

- Blend all the ingredients into a smooth paste.

- Season the chutney with salt according to taste preference.

- Garnish the chutney with additional curry leaves.

- Serve the chutney.

name: Onion Ragi Chilla
ingredients:
- 30g ragi flour (finger millet flour)

- 30g curd

- 10g onion

- 2 green chilies

- 2 tsp oil

- Salt to taste

- Water (as needed)

- Coriander leaves for garnish
nutrition:
- Calories: Around 180 kcal

- Fat: Around 8 g

- Protein: Around 5 g

- Fiber: Around 4 g
method:
- Sieve the ragi flour into a container and mix it with curd until well combined.

- Chop the onion and green chilies into small pieces, then add them to the batter.

- Season the batter with salt according to taste.

- Gradually add water and mix well until the batter reaches a watery consistency.

- Heat a pan and add a little oil.

- Pour the batter onto the pan to make small chilla (pancakes).

- Garnish the chilla with coriander leaves.

- Serve hot.

name: Chickpea Pulao
ingredients:
- 30g chickpeas

- 60g rice

- ¼ tsp whole cumin

- ¼ tsp asafoetida (hing)

- 1 piece clove (laung)

- ¼ cardamom

- ¼ small stick cinnamon

- 1 small onion

- ¼ tsp ginger garlic paste

- 10g chopped tomatoes

- ⅛ tsp turmeric powder

- ⅛ tsp chili powder

- ¼ tsp coriander cumin powder

- ½ tsp oil

- ½ tsp ghee

- Salt to taste
nutrition:
- Calories: Around 300 kcal

- Fat: Around 5 g

- Protein: Around 8 g

- Fiber: Around 6 g
method:
- Soak the chickpeas in enough water in a bowl for 8 hours. Drain well and set aside.

- Heat oil and ghee in a pressure cooker. Add whole cumin, clove, cardamom, cinnamon, and hing. Saute on a medium flame for a few seconds.

- Add onions and ginger-garlic paste. Saute on a medium flame for 2 to 3 minutes.

- Add tomatoes, turmeric powder, chili powder, coriander cumin seed powder, and salt. Mix well and cook on a medium flame for 1 to 2 minutes, stirring occasionally.

- Add the soaked chickpeas and 1 cup water. Mix well and pressure cook for 3 whistles.

- Allow the steam to escape before opening the lid.

- Add the rice, mix gently, and cook on a medium flame for 2 whistles.

- Allow the steam to escape before opening the lid.

- Serve the pulao hot.

name: Vegetable Poha
ingredients:
- 30g poha (beaten rice)

- 10g tomatoes

- 5g onions

- 10g carrots

- 10g beans

- 10g capsicum

- 1 green chili (finely chopped)

- ½ tsp oil

- ¼ tsp mustard seeds

- ¼ tsp asafoetida

- 1 piece curry leaves

- ⅛ tsp turmeric powder

- ¼ tsp lemon juice

- ¼ tsp sugar

- Salt to taste
nutrition:
- Calories: Around 90 kcal

- Fat: Around 1 g

- Protein: Around 2 g

- Fiber: Around 2 g
method:
- Cut all the vegetables into small pieces.

- Heat oil in a deep non-stick pan. Add mustard seeds and sauté on a medium flame for a few seconds.

- Add the chopped vegetables and turmeric powder. Mix well and cook on a medium flame for a few minutes, stirring occasionally.

- Meanwhile, place the beaten rice in a sieve and hold it under running water for a few seconds. Toss well to drain out excess water.

- Add the washed and drained beaten rice, lemon juice, sugar, and salt. Mix well and cook on a medium flame for 3 minutes, stirring occasionally.

- Switch off the flame and serve the vegetable poha hot.

name: Soya Curry
ingredients:
- 30g soya chunks

- ⅛ tsp whole cumin

- Pinch of asafoetida

- ¼ tsp ginger-green chili paste

- ⅛ tsp garlic paste

- ⅛ cup chopped onions

- ⅛ cup freshly chopped tomatoes

- ¼ tsp turmeric powder

- ⅛ tsp chili powder

- ⅛ tsp coriander powder

- 1 tbsp fresh curd

- 1 tsp gram flour

- 1 tsp oil

- Salt to taste

- Sugar to taste (optional)
nutrition:
- Calories: Around 150 kcal

- Fat: Around 5 g

- Protein: Around 12 g

- Fiber: Around 4 g
method:
- Soak the soya nuggets in hot salted water for about 20 minutes. Squeeze out the water and keep aside.

- Heat oil in a non-stick pan and add whole cumin. When they crackle, add the asafoetida, ginger-green chili paste, garlic paste, and onions. Sauté till the onions turn translucent.

- Add the tomatoes, turmeric powder, chili powder, and coriander powder. Cook on a slow flame for about 5 to 10 minutes.

- Mix the curd, gram flour, and ¾ cup water. Add this mixture to the onion-tomato gravy.

- Add the soya nuggets, sugar (if using), and salt. Simmer for 2 more minutes.

- Serve hot.

name: Lemon Rice
ingredients:
- 30g Rice

- 15g Urad dal

- 4 Curry leaves

- 2 Green chillies

- 1 tsp Coriander

- ½ tsp Turmeric

- 1 tsp Lemon juice

- 1 tsp Oil

- Salt to taste
nutrition:
- Calories: Around 150 kcal

- Fat: Around 2 g

- Protein: Around 4 g

- Fiber: Around 2 g
method:
- Take a pan, add 1 tsp of oil, curry leaves, urad dal, turmeric, and green chillies.

- Fry until browned, then add boiled rice.

- Add lemon juice and mix well.

- Season with salt to taste.

- Garnish with coriander leaves.

- Serve hot.

name: Ragi Porridge With Cucumber
ingredients:
- 30g Ragi Flour

- 15g Curd

- 10g Cucumber

- Salt as per taste

- Water as required
nutrition:
- Calories: Around 80 kcal

- Fat: Around 1 g

- Protein: Around 3 g

- Fiber: Around 2 g
method:
- Mix ragi flour in hot boiling water, cook for 5 minutes, allow it to cool, and then add curd.

- Add water gradually, mix well, and check for the desired consistency.

- Cut cucumber into small pieces and add them to the mixture.

- Season with salt as per taste.

- Serve.

name: Knol Khol Sambar
ingredients:
- 15g Toor Dal

- 5g Tomato

- 10g Onion

- 10g Knol Khol

- 1 tsp Tamarind Pulp

- ½ tsp Turmeric

- ½ tsp Coriander Leaves

- ½ tsp Sambar Masala

- 4 Curry Leaves

- ¼ tsp Mustard Seeds

- ½ tsp Red Chilli Powder

- Salt to taste

- 1 tsp Oil
nutrition:
- Calories: Around 80 kcal

- Fat: Around 2 g

- Protein: Around 4 g

- Fiber: Around 4 g
method:
- Precook the toor dal.

- Heat oil in a pan.

- Add mustard seeds, curry leaves, chopped onions, tomato, turmeric, sambar powder, coriander leaves, tamarind pulp, and red chilly powder.

- Add the precooked dal and salt as per taste.

- Cook for 5 minutes until the water has reduced by half of its quantity.

- Garnish with mint leaves.

- Serve hot.

name: Knol Khol Dal
ingredients:
- 15g Masoor Dal

- 5g Tomato

- 5g Onion

- 10g Knol Khol

- 1 tsp Oil

- 2 Garlic Cloves

- ½ tsp Red Chilly Powder

- ½ tsp Turmeric

- ¼ tsp Jeera (Cumin Seeds)

- ½ tsp Tamarind Pulp

- ½ tsp Coriander Leaves

- 4 Curry Leaves

- Salt as per taste
nutrition:
- Calories: Around 100 kcal

- Fat: Around 3 g

- Protein: Around 5 g

- Fiber: Around 4 g
method:
- Take a pressure cooker, wash the masoor dal, and add it to the cooker.

- Cut tomato, onion into small pieces and add them to the cooker.

- Add tamarind, jeera, garlic cloves, red chilly powder, turmeric.

- Pour 1 glass of water, close the lid, and pressure cook:
- After 2 whistles, remove from heat.

- Cut knol khol into round shapes, add into the cooker, and pressure cook for 1 more whistle.

- Remove water and knol khol from the cooker into a separate vessel.

- Blend all the ingredients into a smooth paste.

- In a separate vessel, add 1 tsp of oil, curry leaves, and chopped onions. Fry until brown.

- Add the paste along with the removed water to the vessel.

- Add knol khol and salt as per taste.

- Garnish with coriander leaves.

- Serve hot.

name: Onion Chutney
ingredients:
- 50g Onion or Shallots

- 1 Garlic Clove

- ½ tsp Tamarind

- ½ tsp Urad Dal

- 1 Red Chilli

- ½ tsp Red Chilli Powder

- ½ tsp Oil

- Salt to taste
nutrition:
- Calories: Around 60 kcal

- Fat: Around 2 g

- Protein: Around 1 g

- Fiber: Around 1 g
method:
- Heat ½ teaspoon of oil in a pan.

- Add ½ teaspoon of urad dal and fry, stirring often, until the lentils turn golden.

- Then add red chillies, chopped onions, and sauté on a low to medium flame until they turn golden brown.

- Transfer the entire mixture into a blender jar, add tamarind, salt, and blend it into a smooth mixture.

name: Garlic Chutney
ingredients:
- 30g Garlic Cloves

- 1 tsp Red Chilli Powder

- ½ tsp Whole Cumin

- 1 tsp Coriander Powder

- 1 tsp Lemon Juice

- Salt to taste
nutrition:
- Calories: Around 30 kcal

- Fat: Around 0 g

- Protein: Around 1 g

- Fiber: Around 1 g
method:
- Roast garlic cloves on a non-stick pan until golden brown.

- Take the roasted garlic, lemon juice, whole cumin, coriander powder, and salt in a blender jar.

- Blend the ingredients into a smooth paste.

- Remove the chutney from the blender and serve it.

name: Cabbage Chutney
ingredients:
- 100g Cabbage

- 1 tsp Urad Dal

- 2 Green Chillies

- 10g Chopped Onions

- Pinch of Asafoetida

- ½ tsp Tamarind

- 1 tsp Oil

- Salt to taste
nutrition:
- Calories: Around 50 kcal

- Fat: Around 2 g

- Protein: Around 2 g

- Fiber: Around 4 g
method:
- Heat oil in a pan, add urad dal, and sauté until it changes color to golden brown.

- Add red chillies and asafoetida, sauté briefly, then add chopped cabbage, mix well, and cook for 3 minutes.

- Transfer the cooked mixture into a blender jar and blend into a smooth paste.

- Heat oil in a pan, add mustard seeds, let them crackle, then add a pinch of asafoetida.

- Add the smooth paste to the pan, mix thoroughly, and transfer to a serving bowl. Serve.

name: Besan Chilla
ingredients:
- 30 grams Gram Flour (Besan)

- ¼ teaspoon Ajwain (Carom Seeds)

- Salt to taste

- 30 grams Onion, finely chopped

- Chopped Coriander

- 30 grams Green Capsicum, finely chopped

- ½ teaspoon Ginger, finely chopped

- 1 Green Chilli, chopped (to taste)

- Water as needed

- 1 teaspoon Oil (for cooking the chilla)
nutrition:
- Calories: Around 130 kcal

- Fat: Around 4 g

- Protein: Around 6 g

- Fiber: Around 3 g
method:
- In a large bowl, mix besan, ajwain, and salt.

- Add chopped onion, coriander, green capsicum, ginger, and green chilli.

- Gradually add water while whisking continuously to form a thick batter with pouring consistency.

- Heat an iron skillet/tawa on medium heat. Once hot, pour a ladle full of batter onto the skillet.

- Spread the batter in a circular motion with the ladle on the tawa.

- Pour around ½ teaspoon oil around the edges of the chilla and a few drops on top.

- Cook for 1 to 2 minutes, then flip the chilla.

- Press with a spatula and cook the other side for around 2 minutes until light brown spots appear.

- Once both sides are cooked, remove the chilla from the pan.

- Serve hot with mint chutney.

name: Tamarind Chutney
ingredients:
- 12.5 grams tamarind

- 12.5 grams jaggery

- Approximately 3/8 cup water

For the Masala Blend:

- Coriander (Dhania) Seeds

- ½ tablespoon Whole Cumin (Jeera)

- ½ tablespoon Fennel Seeds (Saunf)

- 1-2 whole Dry Kashmiri Red Chilies

- Pinch of Asafoetida (Hing)

- ½ teaspoon Chili Powder

- ½ tablespoon Dried Ginger (Sonth) Powder

- ¼ teaspoon Black Salt

- Salt to taste
nutrition:
- Calories: Around 60 kcal

- Fat: Around 0.3 g

- Protein: Around 0.6 g

- Fiber: Around 1.7 g
method:
- Soak tamarind in water for an hour.

- Boil 1 cup of water, mix tamarind into it, and let it sit. Remove from heat and mash the tamarind in water.

- Drain the water and take out the tamarind pulp. Keep this water aside for later use.

- Blend the tamarind pulp to make a smooth paste.

- In a pan, add the strained water along with another cup of water. Bring it to a boil, then add jaggery and let it melt.

- Add the grinded tamarind paste into the pan.

- Mix in the roasted masala powder, chili powder, dry ginger powder, black salt, and salt. Let the mixture boil for 5-7 minutes.

- Taste and adjust sugar or salt if needed.

- Cool and store for later use. Serve.

name: Oats Chilla
ingredients:
- 30 grams quick cooking rolled oats

- 10 grams besan (Bengal gram flour)

- 1/4 cup onion, finely chopped

- Finely chopped coriander (dhania)

- 1 green chili, finely chopped

- Salt to taste

- Oil for cooking
nutrition:
- Calories: Around 160 kcal

- Fat: Around 4.5 g

- Protein: Around 6 g

- Fiber: Around 3 g
method:
- Combine all the ingredients in a bowl.

- Add a little water and mix well to create a smooth batter.

- Heat a non-stick tawa and lightly grease it with oil.

- Pour 1/4th portion of the mixture onto the tawa and spread it evenly with a ladle to make a thin chilla.

- Cook over medium heat until the chilla turns golden brown on one side.

- Flip and cook on a medium flame for another minute, folding it over with a spatula to make a semi-circle.

- Serve hot with green or tamarind chutney.

name: Mushroom Kathi Roll
ingredients:
- 30 grams wheat flour

- 50 grams mushrooms, finely chopped

- 2 cloves garlic, finely chopped

- 1/2 teaspoon grated ginger

- 1/2 large onion, finely chopped

- 1/2 tomatoes, finely chopped

- 1 teaspoon coriander-cumin (dhania-jeera) powder

- 1 teaspoon dried fenugreek leaves (kasuri methi)

- 1/4 cup tomato puree

- 1/2 tablespoons curd

- Pinch of sugar

- 1 tablespoon chopped coriander

- 1/2 tablespoon oil

- Salt to taste

- Water for kneading
nutrition:
- Calories: Around 190 kcal

- Fat: Around 5 g

- Protein: Around 6 g

- Fiber: Around 4 g
method:
- Knead the wheat flour with water to make a chapati dough. Prepare chapatis and keep them aside.

- Heat oil in a pan. Add garlic, ginger, and onion. Sauté until the onion turns translucent.

- Add the tomatoes and cook until the oil separates.

- Mix in the coriander-cumin seed powder, kasuri methi. Add the tomato puree and cook for a few more minutes.

- Add mushrooms and salt. Stir until the mushrooms are cooked.

- Add curd, sugar, and coriander. Mix well and set aside.

- Divide the mushroom filling into equal portions, spread onto chapatis, roll.

- Serve.

name: Palak Raita
ingredients:
- 100ml curd (dahi / yogurt)

- 50g Spinach Leaves (Palak), finely chopped

- 1/4 teaspoon red Chilli powder

- 1/2 teaspoon cumin powder (Jeera)

- 1/2 teaspoon whole black peppercorns, coarsely pounded

- Salt, to taste

- Ingredients for seasoning (alternative Flavor)
- 1/4 teaspoon oil

- 1/4 teaspoon mustard seeds (Rai)

- 1/2 teaspoon white urad Dal (Split)

- 1 teaspoon curry leaves
nutrition:
- Calories: Around 65 kcal

- Fat: Around 3 g

- Protein: Around 4 g

- Fiber: Around 3 g
method:
- Heat oil in a heavy-bottomed pan; add the whole cumin and allow it to crackle. Add chopped spinach and sauté on high heat until tender and most of the water is evaporated.

- Set aside and allow the spinach to cool completely.

- Whisk together the yogurt, cumin powder, red chilli powder, black pepper, and salt. Fold the cooled spinach mixture into the whisked yogurt.

- Transfer to a serving dish and refrigerate for 2 hours before serving.

- For seasoning, heat oil in a tadka pan; add the seasoning ingredients and allow it to roast and crackle. Once it roasts and crackles, turn off the heat.

- Pour the seasoning onto the Palak Raita and serve it with Parathas or as a side dish along with your main course meal.

name: Palak Stuffed Idli
ingredients:
- 30 grams rawa (semolina)

- 1 tablespoon curd

- 2 tablespoons water

- Salt to taste

- 1/4 teaspoon baking soda

- 1/2 teaspoon oil

- 1/2 teaspoon rai (mustard seeds)

- 4-5 curry leaves

- 5 grams urad dal

- 1/2 green chilli (finely chopped)

Stuffing for Stuffed Idli:

- 30 grams finely chopped palak (spinach)

- 1/2 finely chopped green chilli

- 1/2 teaspoon ginger paste

- 1/2 teaspoon salt

- 5 ml oil
nutrition:
- Calories: Around 350 kcal

- Fat: Around 10 g

- Protein: Around 10 g

- Fiber: Around 5 g
method:
Beat curd. Filter suji in a utensil, mix it with curd, and blend properly. Add water and salt and blend rigorously to make a smooth batter.

Heat oil in a small pan; add mustard seeds. Once they crackle, add curry leaves, urad dal, and fry till dal turns light brown. Add green chilli and fry some more. Cover the mixture and keep aside for 15 minutes allowing the suji grains to get puffed.

Heat oil in a pan, add green chilli and ginger paste, followed by palak. Cook until palak turns soft. Put in salt; stuffing required to prepare idli is ready.

Add baking soda to the batter and blend well. Do not overmix after adding soda.

Apply oil to the idli stand. Pour mixture into each idli mold halfway using a spoon. Place stuffing on the idli mixture in all the molds and cover it. Fill all the levels of the idli stand this way.

Place the stand in a cooker with water in it (steam emitting). Cook for 10 minutes on high flame. Check if idlis are cooked using a knife.

Remove idli stand from the cooker, take idlis out using a knife, and place them on a plate.

name: Spicy Garlic Tofu
ingredients:
- 100 grams tofu

- 3-4 cloves garlic (unpeeled)

- 1-inch ginger

- 4-5 dry red chillies

- 1 teaspoon white sesame seeds

- Salt (according to taste)

- 1 teaspoon soy sauce

- 1 teaspoon oil

- 50 grams onion

- 30 grams spring onion

- 20 grams green capsicum

- 1 teaspoon black pepper powder (or crushed pepper)

- Chopped green onions (for garnish)
nutrition:
- Calories: Around 300 kcal

- Fat: Around 15 g

- Protein: Around 20 g

- Fiber: Around 5 g
method:
Place the dry red chillies, ginger, sesame seeds, salt, and unpeeled garlic in a blender. Pulse 3-4 times until it forms a coarse paste.

Heat oil in a pan over medium-low heat. Add the spice paste and onion. Fry for 30 seconds, then add the soy sauce, black pepper powder, tofu cubes, spring onion, and capsicum.

Toss well to coat the tofu with the spices and soy sauce. Fry for approximately 2 minutes until the tofu turns slightly golden and crispy on the outside.

Garnish with chopped green onions or sesame seeds before serving.

name: Grilled Vegetables
ingredients:
- 20 grams green capsicum

- 20 grams yellow capsicum

- 20 grams red capsicum

- 25 grams broccoli

- 15 grams baby corn

- Pinch of salt and pepper

- 5 ml lemon juice
nutrition:
- Calories: Around 50 kcal

- Fat: Around 1 g

- Protein: Around 2 g

- Fiber: Around 3 g
method:
Finely chop the capsicums, baby corn, and broccoli.

Heat a grill pan and add 1 teaspoon of oil. Saute all the vegetables in the pan until they turn golden brown.

Season with salt and pepper according to taste.

Once cooled, add the lemon juice to the vegetables.

name: Vegetable Fried Rice
ingredients:
- 5 ml oil

- 50 grams paneer

- 30 grams chopped spring onions

- 30 grams capsicum

- 10 grams carrot

- 30 grams shredded cabbage

- 3/4th cup cooked rice

- Pinch of freshly ground white pepper powder

- Salt to taste
nutrition:
- Calories: Around 300 kcal

- Fat: Around 12 g

- Protein: Around 9 g

- Fiber: Around 3 g
method:
Heat the oil in a wok or kadhai. Add paneer and sauté for a few minutes.

Add chopped spring onions, capsicum, carrots, and cabbage. Sauté on high flame for 3 to 4 minutes.

Add the cooked rice, freshly ground white pepper powder, spring onion, and salt. Toss well and sauté on high flame for an additional 2 minutes.

Serve immediately.

name: Chole Poha
ingredients:
- 20g poha (beaten rice)

- 10g chana dal (soaked and boiled)

- 10g onion, finely chopped

- 10g tomato, finely chopped

- 1 green chilli

- 1/2 tsp mustard seeds

- 1/2 tsp whole cumin seeds

- 1 tsp oil

- 1/2 tsp coriander leaves, chopped

- Pinch of turmeric powder

- Salt to taste

- Lemon juice to taste
nutrition:
- Calories: Around 150 kcal

- Fat: Around 4 g

- Protein: Around 5 g

- Fiber: Around 3 g
method:
Place the poha in a sieve and rinse it under running water for a few seconds. Let it drain for 2 minutes to remove excess water.

Heat oil in a broad non-stick pan. Add mustard seeds and cumin seeds. When they crackle, add chopped onions. Sauté for 1-2 minutes on medium flame.

Add turmeric powder, chopped tomatoes, and boiled chana dal. Mix well and cook for 2-3 minutes on medium flame, stirring occasionally.

Add green chilli paste, chilli powder, salt, and 2 tbsp water. Mix and cook for 1 minute on medium flame.

Add the soaked poha, lemon juice, and chopped coriander leaves. Mix well and cook for 2-3 minutes on medium flame, stirring occasionally.

Serve the chole poha hot.

name: Mushroom Toast
ingredients:
- 20g mushrooms

- 25g tomatoes

- 20g onions

- 1/2 tsp red chilli powder

- 2 slices whole wheat bread

- 1 tsp oil

- 1/2 tsp coriander leaves

- Salt to taste
nutrition:
- Calories: Around 150 kcal

- Fat: Around 4 g

- Protein: Around 5 g

- Fiber: Around 5 g
method:
Begin by chopping the mushrooms, tomatoes, onions, and coriander leaves. Toast the bread slices in a toaster.

Heat 1 tsp oil in a pan over medium flame. Add chopped mushrooms, onions, and tomatoes. Stir-fry the vegetables for 3-4 minutes.

Add red chilli powder and salt to the pan. Cook the mixture for an additional 5-10 minutes, stirring occasionally.

Spread this cooked vegetable mixture on the toasted bread slices. Top with chopped coriander leaves and serve hot with your preferred chutney.

name: Palak Sprouts Pancake
ingredients:
- 20g finely chopped spinach (palak)

- 20g sprouted green gram

- 1 green chilli

- 1-inch ginger

- 1/2 tsp whole cumin

- Pinch of turmeric powder

- 1 tsp oil

- Salt to taste
nutrition:
- Calories: Around 120 kcal

- Fat: Around 3 g

- Protein: Around 5 g

- Fiber: Around 4 g
method:
Preparation:

- Soak and sprout green gram. Blend it into a smooth mixture.

For Pancakes:

In a bowl, combine the green gram mixture, chopped spinach, green chilli paste, ginger, whole cumin, turmeric powder, salt, and water. Mix well to form a batter-like consistency.

Heat oil on a pan. Spread a portion of the mixture onto the pan once the oil is heated.

Cover and cook one side until it's done, then flip and cook the other side until it's cooked through.

Serve the pancakes hot.

name: Healthy Veg Stew
ingredients:
- 1 tsp oil

- 1-inch cinnamon

- 1 pod cardamom

- 10g onion

- 10g beans

- 10g carrot

- 10g peas

- 10g cauliflower

- 1 green chilli

- 1-inch ginger

- Salt to taste

- Few curry leaves

- Thin coconut milk

- Thick coconut milk
nutrition:
- Calories: Around 200 kcal

- Fat: Around 15 g

- Protein: Around 5 g

- Fiber: Around 6 g
method:
- In a large pan, heat oil and sauté cloves, add cinnamon and cardamom pods.

- Add onions and sauté until they shrink slightly without browning.

- Add beans, carrots, potatoes, peas, cauliflower, green chilli, and ginger. Sauté for a minute.

- Add water if needed, salt to taste, and a few curry leaves. Mix well. Cover and boil for about 5 minutes or until the vegetables are half-cooked.

- Pour in thin coconut milk, mix well, and continue boiling for approximately 7 minutes or until the vegetables are completely cooked.

- Turn off the flame and add thick coconut milk. Mix well.

- Serve the healthy vegetable stew.

name: Veg Appe
ingredients:
- 15g semolina/rava

- 10g curd to make batter

- 10g onion (chopped)

- 5g carrot (chopped)

- 1 green chilli

- ½ tsp coriander leaves (chopped)

- Few curry leaves

- 1 inch ginger

- Pinch of black pepper

- 1 tsp oil

- Salt to taste
nutrition:
- Calories: Around 120 kcal

- Fat: Around 4 g

- Protein: Around 3 g

- Fiber: Around 2 g
method:
- Take the semolina/rava in a pan, slightly roast it, and then put it in a mixing bowl. Add curd to it and mix well to form a batter.

- Add chopped onion, carrot, green chilli, coriander leaves, curry leaves, grated ginger, black pepper, and salt to the batter. Mix thoroughly. If the batter seems too thick, adjust the consistency by adding water.

- Close the lid and let the batter rest for 15 minutes.

- Heat the appe pan and grease it with some oil.

- Pour 1-2 tablespoons of batter into each of the appe moulds in the pan. Cover the pan with a lid and let the appes cook on medium flame.

- Once the base turns golden brown, optionally brush some oil on top of the appes, then flip them over and cook the other side until golden brown.

- The healthy mixed veg appes are now ready to be served.

- Enjoy them hot with coconut chutney and peanut-tomato chutney.

name: White Sauce Pasta
ingredients:
- 20g wheat pasta
