- 1 tsp oil

- 2 tsp milk

- 1 tsp atta

- 5g onion

- 5g carrot

- 5g tomato

- 5g capsicum

- 5g sweet corn kernels

- 5g peas

- ½ tsp garlic

- 1 small green chilli (optional)

- Freshly ground pepper to taste

- Herbs as required

- Salt to taste
nutrition:
- Calories: Around 180 kcal

- Fat: Around 4 g

- Protein: Around 6 g

- Fiber: Around 4 g
method:
Boiling Pasta:

- Pour a required amount of water into a large pot and add ¼ tsp salt.

- Bring the water to a rapid boil and add wheat-based pasta.

- Cook on medium-high flame until the pasta is tender, firm, and chewy but not mushy. Check a minute earlier than mentioned on the package.

- Drain the pasta in a colander, reserving some water/stock. Set the cooked pasta aside.

Making White Sauce Pasta:

- In a bowl, mix atta with a little milk to get a smooth paste.

- Add the paste to a pan. Slowly add the remaining milk, mixing to ensure there are no lumps.

- Add salt, pepper, and herbs. Cook on low flame, stirring continuously until the sauce slightly thickens.

- Cut all vegetables in similar shapes and sizes, then set them aside.

- Heat a little oil in a pan. Add chopped garlic and sauté for 1 minute.

- Add the vegetables and cook for 5 minutes.

- Once cooked, add the cooked pasta and vegetables to the white sauce. Stir well.

- Garnish with red chilli flakes and crushed black pepper if desired. Serve immediately.

name: Rava Idli
ingredients:
- 50g rava (semolina)

- 20ml curd (yogurt)

- ½ tsp salt

- ¼ cup water

- ¼ tsp soda
nutrition:
- Calories: Around 180 kcal

- Fat: Around 1 g

- Protein: Around 4 g

- Fiber: Around 1 g
method:
For Rava Idli Preparation:

- In a pan, roast rava until it turns aromatic. Allow it to cool.

- In a bowl, mix the roasted rava, curd, and salt, ensuring no lumps. Let it rest for 20 minutes.

- After 20 minutes, add water and soda to the mixture. Gently mix until it reaches the desired consistency.

- Fill an idli plate with this batter and cook for 15 minutes.

name: Millets Uttapam With Grated Vegetables
ingredients:
- 30g foxtail millet

- 1 tsp ghee

- 1 tsp urad dal

- ½ tsp mustard seeds

- ½ tsp whole cumin seeds

- 10g onion

- 2 green chillies

- Chopped ginger

- Few curry leaves

- 5g grated green beans

- Salt to taste

- ½ tsp turmeric powder

- 1 ½ cups water

- 10g tomato
nutrition:
- Calories: Around 130 kcal

- Fat: Around 3 g

- Protein: Around 4 g

- Fiber: Around 3 g
method:
- In a pan, heat ghee. Add urad dal, chana dal, mustard seeds, whole cumin seeds, onion, green chilli, ginger, curry leaves. Sauté until the onion turns transparent.

- Add carrot, beans, peas, tomatoes, salt to taste, turmeric powder. Sauté well and add water and foxtail millets.

- Cook for 15 minutes until the foxtail millets are cooked.

name: Green Loaded Chilla
ingredients:
- 50g spinach

- 1 cup water

- 25g gram flour

- 10g onion

- 1 green chilli

- ¼ tsp carom seeds

- Coriander leaves

- Salt to taste
nutrition:
- Calories: Around 130 kcal

- Fat: Around 4 g

- Protein: Around 7 g

- Fiber: Around 5 g
method:
- In a grinder, add spinach and water, then grind it into a smooth paste.

- In a bowl, combine gram flour, the ground spinach paste, additional water, and mix well to form a batter.

- Add chopped onion, green chilli, coriander leaves, carom seeds, and salt to taste into the batter and mix thoroughly.

- In a pan, add oil, spread the batter, and cook for 2-3 minutes until it forms a chilla.

- Chilla is now ready to serve.

name: Chilla With Grated Onion And Zucchini
ingredients:
- 25g gram flour

- Salt to taste

- ¼ tsp turmeric powder

- ¼ tsp black pepper powder

- ½ tsp whole cumin seeds

- 25g grated zucchini

- 10g grated onion

- Water
nutrition:
- Calories: Around 80 kcal

- Fat: Around 2 g

- Protein: Around 3 g

- Fiber: Around 2 g
method:
- In a bowl, combine gram flour, turmeric powder, salt, black pepper powder, whole cumin seeds, and water to form a batter.

- Add grated zucchini and onion into the batter and mix well.

- In a pan, add oil, spread the batter, and cook to make the chilla.

name: Mix Veg Sandwich
ingredients:
- 1 tsp oil

- 1 tsp red chili flakes

- ½ tsp ginger-garlic paste

- 2 green chilies

- 1 onion, chopped

- 1 capsicum, chopped

- Salt, to taste

- 10 grm cabbage

- 10 grm grated carrot

- ¼ tsp black pepper powder

- Wheat bread slices
nutrition:
- Calories: Around 200 kcal

- Fat: Around 7 g

- Protein: Around 5 g

- Fiber: Around 5 g
method:
- Heat oil in a pan, add red chili flakes and ginger-garlic paste. Roast for 1 minute.

- Add green chilies, chopped onion, capsicum, cabbage, grated carrot, and salt to taste. Cook for 1 minute.

- Transfer the cooked vegetables to a bowl. Allow them to cool for 5 minutes, then add black pepper powder and mix well.

- Spread this vegetable mixture on wheat bread slices.

- Cook the prepared sandwich in a pan.

name: Egg Lettuce Toast
ingredients:
- 2 boiled eggs

- 10 grm sliced lettuce

- 10 grm sliced tomatoes

- Curd

- Wheat bread slices
nutrition:
- Calories: Around 300 kcal

- Fat: Around 15 g

- Protein: Around 20 g

- Fiber: Around 5 g
method:
- In a bowl, smash the boiled eggs, add curd, and mix well.

- On one bread slice, spread the lettuce, egg and curd mixture, sliced tomatoes, and another layer of lettuce.

- Cover with another bread slice to make a sandwich.

- Toast the assembled sandwich on a pan until golden brown.

name: Appe With Veg Sambar
ingredients:
- 1 cup rice flour

- ½ cup rava (semolina)

- ¾ cup curd

- Water

- ½ onion, chopped

- 1 carrot, grated

- 2 green chillies, chopped

- Curry leaves

- Coriander leaves

- ¼ tsp baking soda
nutrition:
- Calories: Around 200 kcal

- Fat: Around 2 g

- Protein: Around 6 g

- Fiber: Around 3 g
method:
- In a mixing bowl, combine rice flour, rava, curd, and enough water to make a smooth batter with a medium consistency.

- Add chopped onion, grated carrot, chopped green chillies, curry leaves, and coriander leaves to the batter. Mix well to incorporate all the ingredients evenly.

- Grease the appe moulds with oil and pour the batter into each mould.

- Cook the appe on both sides until golden brown.

name: Mango Overnight Oats
ingredients:
- 20g quick oats

- 30g homemade/store-bought curd (yogurt)

- 20g chopped mango

- ½ tsp cinnamon powder or vanilla essence (optional)

- 1 tsp seed powder (optional)

- 5g thin slices of coconut (optional)
nutrition:
- Calories: Around 150 kcal

- Fat: Around 5 g

- Protein: Around 5 g

- Fiber: Around 5 g
method:
- Mix all the ingredients together in a container.

- Ensure that the yogurt/curd mixture is runny, similar to a milkshake or dosa batter consistency.

- Store the mixture overnight in the fridge.

- Before serving, top with chopped mangoes and coconut slices.

name: Cabbage Tahini
ingredients:
- 10 grams chopped cabbage

- 10 ml curd

- Salt to taste

- 1 teaspoon olive oil

- 1 piece garlic
nutrition:
- Calories: Around 40 kcal

- Fat: Around 3 g

- Protein: Around 2 g

- Fiber: Around 1 g
method:
- In a grinder, add cabbage, olive oil, salt, and garlic. Grind the ingredients into a paste.

- In a bowl, add curd and the ground paste. Mix well.

name: Oats Warm Water Porridge
ingredients:
- 30 grams rolled oats

- 5 grams chopped beans

- 5 grams chopped carrot

- 5 grams peas

- 1/2 teaspoon oil

- Salt to taste

- 2 cups water
nutrition:
- Calories: Around 120 kcal

- Fat: Around 3 g

- Protein: Around 5 g

- Fiber: Around 4 g
method:
- In a pan, lightly roast the rolled oats. Set aside.

- Heat 1/2 teaspoon oil in the pan, add chopped vegetables (beans, carrots, peas), and sauté for 2-3 minutes.

- Pour 2 cups of water and bring it to a boil.

- Add the roasted oats and salt according to taste. Stir well and cook the porridge on low to medium flame.

- Stir occasionally and allow the porridge to simmer and thicken. Cook for approximately 5 to 6 minutes.

- Serve the oats porridge hot, warm, or at room temperature. Note: The porridge thickens as it cools.

name: Ragi Wheat Oats
ingredients:
- 10 grams ragi flour

- 10 grams oats

- 10 grams wheat flour

- 15 ml water

- Salt, to taste
nutrition:
- Calories: Around 70 kcal

- Fat: Around 2 g

- Protein: Around 3 g
Fiber: Around 2 g
method:
- In a pan, add water and salt. Bring it to a boil.

- Add oats and cook for 2 minutes.

- Then add ragi flour and wheat flour. Cook for a few more minutes.

- Allow the mixture to cool.

name: Parval Dal
ingredients:
- 15 grams toor dal (pigeon peas)

- 25 grams parval (pointed gourd)

- 5 grams onion

- 5 grams tomato

- ¼ teaspoon turmeric powder

- 1 dried red chili

- ½ teaspoon mustard seeds

- Few curry leaves

- A pinch of hing (asafoetida)

- 2 garlic cloves

- 1 teaspoon oil

- Salt, to taste
nutrition:
- Calories: Around 100 kcal

- Fat: Around 3 g

- Protein: Around 5 g

- Fiber: Around 3 g
method:
- (Optional) Soak the toor dal in water for half an hour.

- Scrape the parval gently and cut it into half-inch-thick circles.

- Heat oil in a pressure cooker. Add mustard seeds, curry leaves, red chili, garlic, and hing. Sauté for a few seconds.

- Add onion and tomato. Sauté for 2 minutes, then add parval and sauté until it turns light golden brown.

- Add dal, salt, and mix gently. Cook on medium heat for 2 minutes. Add turmeric powder and more salt if needed.

- Lower the heat, add the required amount of water, and pressure cook for 2-3 whistles.

- Serve the dal curry with plain rice.

name: Dal Roti
ingredients:
Dal Filling:

- 10 grams Bengal gram dal (chana dal)

- 1 teaspoon oil

- Pinch of turmeric

- ½ teaspoon coarsely ground cumin

- 10 grams spring onion, finely chopped

- ½ teaspoon chopped coriander

- Salt to taste

Roti:

- 30 grams wheat flour

- Freshly boiled water as required

- Pinch of salt (optional)
nutrition:
- Calories: Around 250 kcal

- Fat: Around 5 g

- Protein: Around 9 g

- Fiber: Around 6 g
method:
For Stuffing:

- Boil the Bengal gram dal until tender but still firm. It should be soft yet retain its shape when pressed between your fingers. Pulse the boiled dal in a food processor until it resembles fine breadcrumbs. Avoid over-processing to prevent it from becoming mushy.

- Heat oil in a pan over medium heat. Add the spring onion and sauté for a few seconds.

- Add the coarsely ground cumin and boiled dal. Season with salt and mix well. Cook for another minute, then remove from heat.

- Once the dal mixture cools down, add chopped coriander and combine well.

For Roti:

- In a large bowl, add wheat flour and salt (if using). Pour in the freshly boiled water gradually.

- Combine all the ingredients with a spoon initially (as the mixture will be hot). Once it cools slightly, knead the dough for about 5 minutes until it forms a soft, silky dough.

- Divide the dough into 2 balls. Fill each ball with about 1½ tablespoons of the prepared dal stuffing. Bring the edges together to form a ball.

- Gently roll the filled dough balls into circles. Toast each roti on a non-stick pan over medium heat. Toast one side for a few seconds, then flip and toast the other side for a few seconds. Repeat this process until both sides are cooked, taking around a minute per roti.

- Serve the hot dal stuffed rotis with curd and pickle (optional).

name: Coriander Roti
ingredients:
- Whole Wheat Flour Dough:
- 30 grams Whole Wheat Flour

- ½ teaspoon Cumin Powder

- ¼ teaspoon Turmeric Powder

- 10 grams finely chopped Coriander Leaves

- 1 Green Chilli, finely chopped

- 10 grams Spring Onion

- 1-inch piece of Ginger, grated

- Salt and Pepper to taste

- 1 teaspoon Oil
nutrition:
- Calories: Around 150 kcal

- Fat: Around 3 g

- Protein: Around 5 g

- Fiber: Around 4 g
method:
- In a large mixing bowl, combine the whole wheat flour, cumin powder, turmeric powder, finely chopped coriander leaves, green chillies, spring onion, grated ginger, salt, and pepper.

- Gradually add a little water at a time to knead the ingredients into a firm and smooth dough. Drizzle ½ teaspoon of oil over the dough and knead for a few minutes until the dough becomes smooth and soft.

- Cover the dough and let it rest in the bowl for at least 10 minutes.

- Divide the dough into 2 equal portions. Take each portion, dust it with flour, and roll it out into round circles.

- Heat a flat iron skillet or tawa on medium heat for a few minutes.

- Place the rolled roti dough on the heated skillet and cook the roti on medium heat until you notice spots appearing on the top surface. Flip the roti and cook the other side. Repeat the process, flipping as needed, until both sides have golden brown spots and are fully cooked.

- Repeat the same process to cook the remaining coriander rotis.

name: Paneer Roll
ingredients:
For Filling:

- ½ teaspoon powdered Red Chilli

- ¼ teaspoon whole Cumin Seeds

- ½ teaspoon chopped Coriander Leaves

- 1 teaspoon Oil

- Pinch of Fennel Seeds

- 20 grams Paneer Cubes

- ½ teaspoon powdered Garam Masala

- ¼ teaspoon powdered Curry Powder

- Salt to taste

- ½ teaspoon Garlic Paste

For Filling Ingredients:

- 5 grams finely grated Carrot

- 1 small finely chopped Green Chilli

- 5 grams finely chopped Capsicum

- 5 grams chopped Onion

- 5 grams finely chopped Tomato

For Roti:

- 30 grams Wheat Flour

- Freshly boiled Water as required

- Pinch of Salt (optional)
nutrition:
- Calories: Around 220 kcal

- Fat: Around 10 g

- Protein: Around 8 g

- Fiber: Around 4 g
method:
For Filling:

- Heat oil in a pan over medium flame. Add fennel seeds and whole cumin seeds, sauté for 30 seconds.

- Add chopped onions, green chillies, capsicum, and carrots. Sauté for a minute.

- Add tomatoes and cook for another minute. Stir in red chilli powder and salt, mix well.

- Add grated paneer and garam masala powder. Cook for a minute or two on low-medium flame. Garnish with coriander leaves, then turn off the flame.

For Roti:

- In a large bowl, add wheat flour and salt. Pour in the boiling water. Mix the ingredients with a spoon initially as it will be hot.

- Once it cools slightly, knead the dough for about 5 minutes until it forms a soft, silky dough.

- Divide the dough into 2 equal portions. Roll each portion into a circle gently.

- Toast the rolled dough on a non-stick pan over medium heat. Toast one side for a few seconds, then flip and repeat until both sides have brown spots. This should take about a minute for each roti.

- Spread some of the prepared paneer-vegetable mixture on the chapati and roll it tightly.

name: Mixed Veg Paratha
ingredients:
For Dough:

- 30g Wheat Flour

- Salt (optional)

- Water as required

For Pressure Cooking Vegetables:

- 5g Carrot

- 5g Cauliflower

- 10g Beans

- 5g Peas

For Stuffing:

- 1 tsp Oil

- ½ tsp Ginger Paste

- 1 Green Chilli

- ½ tsp Garam Masala

- ½ tsp Whole Cumin Powder

- ½ tsp Dry Mango Powder

- ½ tsp Coriander Powder

- ¼ tsp Carom Seeds

- Pinch of Hing

- 10g Paneer

- ½ tsp Coriander Leaves
nutrition:
- Calories: Around 280 kcal

- Fat: Around 10 g

- Protein: Around 10 g

- Fiber: Around 5 g
method:
Dough Preparation:

- In a large bowl, mix wheat flour and salt (if using).

- Knead the mixture to form a smooth and soft dough, adding water as needed. Cover the dough and let it rest for 20 minutes.

Vegetable Stuffing Preparation:

- Pressure cook carrot, cauliflower, beans, and peas without adding any water for 4 whistles.

- Drain off any excess water from the cooked vegetables and mash them into a smooth mix.

- Heat oil in a kadai, add ginger paste, and chopped green chilli. Sauté.

- On low flame, add garam masala, cumin powder, dry mango powder, coriander powder, carom seeds, and a pinch of hing. Sauté until the spices turn aromatic.

- Add grated paneer, sauté for 2 minutes.

- Further, add the mashed vegetables, salt, and sauté for 5 minutes until the mixture loses moisture and separates oil.

- Turn off the flame, add coriander leaves, mix well, and let the stuffing cool completely.

Making Vegetable Paratha:

- Take a portion of wheat dough, dust it with wheat flour, and roll it into a circle.

- Place a ball-sized prepared vegetable stuffing in the center of the rolled dough.

- Bring the edges together, pleat them towards the center, and secure tightly, pinching off any excess dough.

- Sprinkle some wheat flour and gently roll the stuffed dough slightly thick.

- On a hot tawa (griddle), roast both sides of the rolled paratha until cooked and golden brown.

- Serve the hot mixed vegetable paratha with raita and pickle (optional).

name: Coriander Raita
ingredients:
- 30ml Curd

- 15g Finely Chopped Coriander Leaves

- 1 Green Chilli

- ½ tsp Cumin Powder

- Salt to Taste
nutrition:
- Calories: Around 25 kcal

- Fat: Around 1 g

- Protein: Around 2 g

- Fiber: Around 1 g
method:
- In a bowl, combine water and curd, whisk thoroughly.

- In a blender, add coriander leaves, green chilli, salt, whole cumin powder, and blend into a smooth paste.

- Add the blended paste into the curd-water mixture. Mix well to combine.

- Serve the Coriander Raita with vegetable biryani or other preferred dishes.

name: Mint Rice
ingredients:
For Cooking Rice:

- 30g Basmati Rice (washed)

- Water (double the quantity of rice)

- Salt (to taste)

For Mint Paste:

- 20g Mint Leaves

- 2 Green Chillies (chopped)

- 3 Garlic Cloves (chopped)

- Salt (to taste)

For Mint Rice:

- 1 tsp Oil

- ½ tsp Whole Cumin Seeds

- 1 Dried Red Chilli

- 15g Onion (chopped)

- Blended Mint Paste

- Salt (if required)

- Cooked Basmati Rice
nutrition:
- Calories: Around 130 kcal

- Fat: Around 3 g

- Protein: Around 3 g

- Fiber: Around 3 g
method:
Cooking Basmati Rice:

- In a cooking vessel, combine washed Basmati rice, water, and salt to taste. Cook until the rice is completely done. Set aside for later use.

Preparing Mint Paste:

- Blend fresh mint leaves, chopped green chillies, garlic cloves, and salt in a blending jar until it forms a fine paste.

Making Mint Rice:

- Heat oil in a pan or wok. Add whole cumin seeds and allow them to splutter.

- Add dried red chillies and sauté for a few seconds over low flame.

- Add chopped onions and cook until they turn slightly golden.

- Mix in the prepared mint paste. Add salt if required. Cook on low flame until the oil separates from the sides.

- Add the cooked Basmati rice to the mint gravy and mix thoroughly.

- Cook the mint rice for 2-3 minutes on low flame.

- Mint rice is ready to be served. Enjoy it with chutney or curd.

name: Thai Cauliflower Fried Rice
ingredients:
- 1 tsp Oil

- ½ tsp Chopped Garlic

- ½ tsp Fresh Grated Ginger

- ½ tsp Red Chilli Paste

- ½ tsp Lime Juice

- 20g Cauliflower

- 10g Spring Onion

- 20g Rice

- 10ml Curd
nutrition:
- Calories: Around 170 kcal

- Fat: Around 7 g

- Protein: Around 4 g

- Fiber: Around 3 g
method:
- Heat oil in a large pan over medium-high heat.

- Add spring onions, stir and cook for 1-2 minutes until they begin to soften.

- Add chopped garlic and fresh grated ginger.

- Once onions have softened, add red chilli paste. Stir, then add cauliflower and sauté for 2 minutes.

- Add coconut milk and let it boil for 1 minute.

- Add rice and required amount of water.

- Pressure cook for 2-3 whistles.

- Season with lime juice and stir to combine.

- Serve hot.

name: Bisibelebath
ingredients:
- 1 tsp Oil

- ½ tsp Mustard Seeds

- Few Curry Leaves

- Pinch of Hing (Asafoetida)

- 20g Rice

- 10g Toor Dal

- 5g Peas

- 5g Carrot

- 10g Beans

- 5g Tomato

- 5g Onion

- 1 tbsp Bisibelebath Powder

- Salt to Taste
nutrition:
- Calories: Around 200 kcal

- Fat: Around 4 g

- Protein: Around 8 g

- Fiber: Around 5 g
method:
- Wash or rinse the dal and rice separately. Soak them for 20 minutes (optional).

- Prepare the vegetables; chop them finely.

- Discard the soaking water from the dal and rice. Transfer both to a pressure cooker, adding required water, a pinch of turmeric powder, and a drop of oil to cook them softly.

- Pressure cook for 3-4 whistles until done. If using an instant pot, cook on manual (high pressure) for 10 minutes.

- Heat oil in a pan on medium heat. Once hot, add mustard seeds and let them splutter. Add dried red chilies, curry leaves, and hing. Sauté for a few seconds.

- Add onion and cook until soft and translucent.

- Add the rest of the veggies. Mix and sauté for 3-4 minutes until slightly tender.

- Add water, cover, and cook until the veggies are fully cooked and tender.

- Stir in the bisibelebath powder and cook on simmer for 2-3 minutes.

- Add the boiled dal and rice mix. Adjust the consistency by adding water if necessary.

- Let it cook for another 4-5 minutes, stirring occasionally.

- Serve hot with chutney or curd.

name: Cabbage Stir Fry
ingredients:
- 30g Cabbage (julienne or shredded)

- 10g Onion (julienne)

- 1 Green Chilli

- 2 Garlic Cloves (finely chopped)

- ½ tsp Coarsely Crushed Black Pepper

- 1 tsp Oil

- Salt to taste
nutrition:
- Calories: Around 50 kcal

- Fat: Around 4 g

- Protein: Around 2 g

- Fiber: Around 2 g
method:
Preparation:

- Cut the cabbage into 4 quarters and soak them in warm water (not hot) for 2 minutes.

- Rinse the cabbage thoroughly in a pot filled with cold water. Ensure it's drained completely to avoid making it mushy.

Cabbage Stir Fry:

- Heat a pan with oil on high heat.

- Sauté garlic and green chillies until a nice aroma emanates.

- Add onion and stir-fry for 2 to 3 minutes until partially cooked but still crunchy. Maintain high heat throughout to retain crunchiness.

- Add salt, pepper, and sauté for another minute. Avoid overcooking to prevent mushiness.

- Transfer the cabbage stir fry to a serving bowl.

name: Beans Sabzi
ingredients:
- 30g French Beans (stringed and chopped)

- 10g Bengal Gram Dal

- 15g Onion (chopped)

- 1 tsp Oil

- ½ tsp Mustard Seeds

- ½ tsp Whole Cumin

- Pinch of Asafoetida

- 1 Green Chilli (chopped)

- ½ tsp Turmeric Powder

- Salt to taste
nutrition:
- Calories: Around 90 kcal

- Fat: Around 4 g

- Protein: Around 5 g

- Fiber: Around 5 g
method:
Pressure cook the field beans and bengal gram dal for two whistles over medium heat in a pressure cooker. Let the steam release naturally and turn off the heat.

Heat oil in a non-stick pan. Add mustard seeds and let them splutter. Then, add whole cumin seeds, asafoetida, and green chillies. Sauté for about 30 seconds.

Add chopped onions and turmeric powder. Sauté for approximately two minutes until onions are translucent.

Add the boiled field beans and bengal gram dal to the pan. Reduce the heat.

Season with salt and mix well. Cover and cook for about 1 minute. Turn off the heat.

Transfer the prepared dish into a serving bowl, optionally garnish with coconut, and serve hot.

name: Black Bean Masala
ingredients:
- 20g Dried Black Beans

- 10g Onion (chopped)

- 10g Tomato (chopped)

- 2 Garlic Cloves (chopped)

- 1-inch Ginger (grated)

- 1 Green Chili (chopped)

- 10ml Curd

- ½ tsp Garam Masala Powder

- ½ tsp Red Chili Powder

- ¼ tsp Turmeric Powder

- A Pinch of Asafoetida / Hing

- ½ tsp Coriander Powder

- ½ tsp Lemon Juice

- ½ tsp Amchur Powder (optional)

- 1 Bay Leaf

- ½ tsp Whole Cumin

- Salt to taste

- 1 tsp Oil
nutrition:
- Calories: Around 100 kcal

- Fat: Around 3 g

- Protein: Around 6 g

- Fiber: Around 5 g
method:
Cook the black beans in a pan with boiling water and salt or pressure cook for one whistle. Drain and set aside.

Heat oil in a pan. Add bay leaf and whole cumin. Sauté for about 30 seconds.

Add chopped onion, garlic cloves, green chilies, ginger, and sauté until the onions turn translucent.

Stir in yogurt, garam masala, chili powder, turmeric powder, asafoetida, coriander powder, and water. Mix well and cook for about 2 minutes.

Add the cooked black beans and bring it to a boil. Simmer for approximately 10 minutes to allow the flavors to combine.

Optionally, mash a portion of the black beans for a thicker gravy consistency.

Black Bean Masala is now ready. Serve it hot and enjoy.

name: Horsegram Curry With Brinjal
ingredients:
- 20g Horse Gram Dal (soaked for at least 4-5 hours or overnight)

- 5g Onion (roughly chopped)

- 5g Tomato (roughly chopped)

- 10g Brinjal (roughly chopped)

- ½ tsp Tamarind Water

For the Curry Masala:

- 5g Onion

- 5g Tomato

- 5g Fresh Coconut (grated)

- 1 Clove

- 1-inch Cinnamon Stick

- 1-inch Ginger

- 4 Cloves of Garlic

- 1 tsp Sambar Powder

For Seasoning:

- ½ tsp Mustard Seeds

- 1 Dry Red Chili

- Few Curry Leaves

- A Pinch of Asafoetida (Hing)

- 1 tsp Oil
nutrition:
- Calories: Around 90 kcal

- Fat: Around 4 g

- Protein: Around 3 g

- Fiber: Around 4 g
method:
Pressure cook the soaked horse gram with chopped onion, tomato, and brinjal for two whistles over medium heat. Allow the steam to release naturally from the pressure cooker.

In a mixer, grind all the curry masala ingredients into a smooth paste using a little water. Transfer the paste to a bowl.

Once the pressure cooker is ready, open the lid and add the prepared curry masala. Close the lid again and pressure cook for two more whistles.

Open the pressure cooker, add tamarind extract and salt to taste. Let the curry simmer for a few minutes until all the flavors are combined well.

For tempering, heat oil in a tadka pan over medium heat. Add mustard seeds and sauté gently on low heat. Next, add curry leaves, asafoetida, and red chilies. Once it splutters, pour it over the curry and stir to combine.

Serve the horse gram curry with steamed rice or Phulka.

name: Cabbage Dal Sabji
ingredients:
- 30g Cabbage, chopped

- 10g Bengal Gram Dal

- 15g Onion, chopped

- 1 tsp Oil

- ½ tsp Mustard Seeds

- ½ tsp Whole Cumin Seeds

- Pinch of Asafoetida

- 1 Green Chilli, chopped

- ½ tsp Turmeric Powder

- Salt to taste
nutrition:
- Calories: Around 90 kcal

- Fat: Around 4 g

- Protein: Around 3 g

- Fiber: Around 4 g
method:
Pressure cook the chopped cabbage and bengal gram dal for two whistles over medium heat. Allow the steam to release naturally from the pressure cooker.

Heat oil in a non-stick pan. Add mustard seeds and let them splutter. Add whole cumin seeds, asafoetida, and chopped green chillies. Sauté for about 30 seconds.

Add chopped onion and turmeric powder. Sauté for about two minutes until onions turn translucent.

Then add the boiled cabbage and bengal gram dal into the pan. Reduce the heat.

Add salt and mix well. Cover and cook for about 1 minute. Turn off the heat.

Transfer the prepared dish into a serving bowl. Optionally garnish with coconut and serve hot.

name: Paneer Veg Kebab
ingredients:
- 30g Paneer

- 10g Onion

- 5g Capsicum

- Cooking Spray

For Marination:

- 10ml Curd

- ½ tsp Ginger-Garlic Paste

- ½ tsp Paprika Powder

- ¼ tsp Turmeric Powder

- ½ tsp Chat Masala

- ½ tsp Garam Masala

- ½ tsp Lemon Juice

- Salt to taste
nutrition:
- Calories: Around 150 kcal

- Fat: Around 9 g

- Protein: Around 8 g

- Fiber: Around 2 g
method:
- Cut the paneer into cubes.

- Cut the onion and capsicum into squares.

- In a bowl, whisk together all the marination ingredients to form a smooth paste.

- Add paneer pieces into the marinade, cover with plastic wrap, and marinate in a cool place for 30 minutes.

- Preheat the oven to 525°F (280°C) using the broil mode.

- Skewer the marinated paneer and vegetables onto wooden skewers, alternating between paneer and vegetables. Shake off excess marinade.

- Generously spray the kebabs with cooking spray. Place the skewers in a deep bowl to prevent them from touching the bottom.

- Put the bowl in the preheated oven and set the timer for 5-8 minutes.

- Once done, remove the bowl with skewers from the oven and arrange them on a plate. Serve hot with green chutney.

name: Oats Blend Idli
ingredients:
For Idli:

- 30g oats

- 1 tbsp semolina

- 2 tbsp curd

- 1 garlic clove, finely chopped

- 1 tsp coriander leaves, finely chopped

- 1 green chili, finely chopped

- Salt to taste

- Pinch of turmeric

- Pinch of baking soda

- Water (as needed for blending)

- Oil for greasing

For Peanut Chutney:

- 15g roasted and dehulled peanuts

- 1 inch dry red chili

- 2 garlic cloves

- 2 tbsp finely chopped onion

- Salt to taste

- Water (as needed for blending)
nutrition:
- Calories: Around 225 kcal

- Fat: Around 10 g

- Protein: Around 7 g

- Fiber: Around 5 g
method:
For Idli:

- Grind oats into a fine powder and mix with semolina, curd, chopped garlic, coriander leaves, green chili, turmeric, baking soda, and salt.

- Add 50ml water, mix well, and let it rest for 45 minutes.

- After 45 minutes, add another 50ml water to make a thick batter.

- Grease the idli tray with oil and pour the batter into it.

- Steam the oats idli for 10-12 minutes, then turn off the stove and allow them to cool down.

For Peanut Chutney:

- Dry roast peanuts, remove their seed coat, and transfer to a blender jar.

- Add garlic, chopped onion, dry red chili, and salt to the blender.

- Blend all the ingredients, adding a little water to achieve a thick chutney consistency.

name: Veg Rava Uttapam With Tomato Chutney
ingredients:
For Uttapam:

- 30g semolina (rava)

- 1 tbsp curd

- 1 finely chopped green chili

- 1 finely chopped garlic clove

- 1 tsp finely chopped coriander leaves

- 50g finely chopped onion

- 50g finely chopped tomato

- Pinch of baking soda

- Salt to taste

- 3 tbsp water

- 1 tsp oil (for cooking)

For Tomato Chutney:

- 50g tomato

- 50g onion

- Half dry red chili

- Pinch of cumin seeds (jeera)

- ¼ tsp red chili powder

- ¼ tsp coriander powder

- ¼ tsp turmeric powder

- Pinch of sugar

- Salt to taste

- Water for cooking
nutrition:
- Calories: Around 210 kcal

- Fat: Around 5 g

- Protein: Around 6 g

- Fiber: Around 4 g
method:
For Uttapam:

- In a bowl, mix semolina with finely chopped green chilies, garlic, and 2 tbsp water. Allow it to rest for 30 minutes.

- After resting, add 2 tbsp of water, salt, and mix well.

- Heat a pan on medium flame, grease with oil, and pour half the batter.

- Once the batter settles, top it with chopped tomatoes, onions, and coriander leaves.

- Cook for 2 minutes, then flip and cook the other side for an additional 2 minutes.

- Repeat the same process for the remaining batter. Once both uttapams are cooked, place them on a serving plate.

For Tomato Chutney:

- Heat ½ tsp oil in a pan, add cumin seeds, and sauté for a minute.

- Add tomatoes, onions, dry red chili, and cook with some water for 2 minutes.

- Add red chili powder, coriander powder, turmeric powder, salt, sugar, and cook for a while.

- Turn off the flame and let it cool to room temperature. Transfer the mixture to a blender and blend into a chutney.

name: Paneer Veg Stuffed Dosa
ingredients:
For Dosa:

- 1 tbsp urad dal

- 1 tsp chana dal

- ¼ tsp methi seeds (fenugreek seeds)

- 1 tbsp rice

- Salt to taste

- Pinch of baking soda

- Water (for blending)

- 1 tsp oil (for cooking)

For Paneer Stuffing:

- 20g paneer

- 50g tomato

- 1 finely chopped green bean

- ¼ tsp red chili powder

- ¼ tsp garam masala

- ¼ tsp turmeric powder

- ¼ tsp coriander powder

- Pinch of chat masala

- Salt to taste
nutrition:
- Calories: Around 250 kcal

- Fat: Around 8 g

- Protein: Around 10 g

- Fiber: Around 4 g
method:
For Dosa:

- Soak urad dal, chana dal, methi seeds, and rice in water for 2 hours. Drain the water.

- Transfer soaked ingredients to a blender jar, add some water, and blend into a smooth mixture.

- Pour the blended mixture into a bowl, add water to make a runny texture, and allow it to ferment overnight.

- After fermentation, add a pinch of baking soda and salt to the mixture and mix well.

- Heat a griddle or tava, grease with oil, and pour half the batter onto it using a ladle.

- Cook the dosa until it is well-done on one side, then flip and cook on both sides.

- Repeat the same process for the remaining batter. Transfer the cooked dosas to a serving plate.

For Paneer Stuffing:

- Mash paneer in a bowl and add finely chopped tomatoes, green beans, red chili powder, turmeric powder, coriander powder, garam masala, chat masala, and salt. Mix all the ingredients well.

- Transfer the mixture to a pan and sauté for two minutes.

- Place the pre-prepared dosa on a plate, fill it with the paneer vegetable stuffing, and wrap the dosa.

- Cut the paneer-stuffed dosa into 2 halves and serve.

name: Methi Paneer
ingredients:
- 1 tsp oil

- ½ tsp chopped ginger or ½ tsp ginger paste

- ½ tsp chopped garlic or ½ tsp garlic paste

- 30 grams onions, cubed

- 30 grams tomatoes, chopped (not very sour)

- Salt (as needed)

- ¼ tsp red chili powder

- Garam masala (to taste)

- 50 grams fenugreek leaves (methi)

- 50 grams paneer

- ¼ tsp whole cumin seeds (jeera)

- ¼ tsp green cardamoms (elaichi)
nutrition:
- Calories: Around 220 kcal

- Fat: Around 14 g

- Protein: Around 10 g

- Fiber: Around 4 g
method:
- Pluck methi leaves and soak them in a large utensil filled with water. Drain and set aside.

- In a hot pan, add oil and fry chopped ginger and garlic till aromatic.

- Add cubed onions and fry till they turn lightly golden.

- Add chopped tomatoes and a sprinkle of salt. Fry till tomatoes turn mushy.

- Add red chili powder and garam masala. Fry for 2 to 3 minutes till the masala releases a good aroma.

- Turn off the stove and let the mixture cool. Blend it with a little water to make a smooth puree.

- In the same pan, sauté methi leaves for 2 minutes. Add paneer and sauté for another 2 minutes. Set this mixture aside.

- Add a little more oil to the same pan. Add whole cumin seeds and cardamom. When they start to sizzle, add the onion-tomato puree. Adjust water to reach a gravy consistency.

- Bring it to a boil and let it cook until the gravy thickens, and traces of oil appear on the surface.

- Add the methi-paneer mixture that was set aside. Cook for about 3 minutes on medium flame. Be cautious not to overcook as it can make the paneer rubbery.

- Transfer the Methi Paneer to a serving bowl.

name: Palak Soup
ingredients:
- 1 cup cleaned and chopped spinach

- 1 tsp my super seed powder or my nut powder (optional)

- ¼ cup milk

- Salt & pepper to taste
nutrition:
- Calories: Around 70 kcal

- Fat: Around 3 g

- Protein: Around 5 g

- Fiber: Around 3g
method:
- Place the spinach in a deep pan with 1/4 cup of water and bring it to a boil.

- Boil for approximately 10 minutes or until the spinach is soft enough to squash the stems with your fingers.

- Allow it to cool down.

- Blend the boiled spinach in a mixer grinder with milk and the optional seed or nut powder until you achieve a smooth consistency.

- Transfer the blended mixture back into the pan.

- Add salt and pepper to taste. Adjust the consistency by adding more milk if you desire a thinner and creamier soup.

- Serve the soup with toasted bread and toasted sesame seeds on top.

name: Baingan Bharta
ingredients:
- 50 grams brinjal/eggplant

- 2 garlic cloves (halved)

- 5 ml Oil

- 1 tsp nigella seeds (Kalonji)

- 3 garlic cloves, minced

- 1 tsp grated ginger

- 1 green chili, finely chopped

- 50 grams onion, finely chopped

- 50 grams tomatoes, finely chopped

- 1 tbsp red chili powder

- 1 tbsp coriander powder

- ½ tsp turmeric powder

- Salt to taste

- 1 tsp chopped coriander
nutrition:
- Calories: Around 110 kcal

- Fat: Around 4 g

- Protein: Around 3 g

- Fiber: Around 5 g
method:
- Cut each garlic clove in half. Make 6 small slits in the brinjal and stuff the slits with the halved garlic cloves.

- Roast the brinjal on an open flame for 8-10 minutes, turning it every 1-2 minutes to ensure even roasting. The skin should blister, and the brinjal should become soft. Check by pricking with a fork or knife; if needed, roast for a few more minutes.

- Once roasted, cover the brinjal with foil and set it aside to cool for a few minutes.

- Heat oil in a pan and add nigella seeds. After 30 seconds, add minced garlic, grated ginger, chopped chili, and onions. Stir-fry until the onions are soft.

- Add tomatoes, ground coriander paste, red chili powder, coriander powder, turmeric, and salt. Mix well, cover, and cook until the tomatoes are soft and pulpy.

- Add the roasted brinjal, mix well, cover, and cook for another 3-4 minutes while stirring occasionally.

- Garnish with chopped coriander and serve hot.

name: Lemon, Garlic And Herbs Prawns
ingredients:
- 100g raw king prawns

- 0.5 tbsp olive oil

- 1 tbsp Lemon (juice and zest)

- 1 garlic clove

- Handful of fresh parsley, finely chopped
nutrition:
- Calories: Around 160 kcal

- Fat: Around 6 g

- Protein: Around 20 g

- Fiber: Around 1 g
method:
- Put the olive oil in a frying pan and add the prawns, lemon juice and zest, and garlic.

- Cook for 3-4 minutes or until the prawns turn pink.

- Pour the cooked prawns into a bowl and scatter them with the fresh chopped parsley before serving.

name: Stuffed Veg Mushroom With Paneer
ingredients:
For the Stuffing:

- 75 grams finely chopped mixed vegetables (French beans, carrot, and capsicum)

- 25 grams finely chopped onions

- ¼ tsp finely chopped garlic

- ¼ tsp finely chopped green chillies

- ¼ tsp garam masala

- 100 grams crumbled paneer (cottage cheese)

- Negligible cup finely chopped coriander (dhania)

- Salt to taste

For Mushrooms:

- 4 pieces/50 grams whole large mushrooms (khumbh), cleaned and washed
nutrition:
- Calories: Around 40 kcal

- Fat: Around 2 g

- Protein: Around 3 g

- Fiber: Around 1 g
method:
For the Stuffing:

- Heat butter in a broad pan, add onions and garlic, sauté on a medium flame for 1 minute.

- Add green chilies and mixed vegetables, mix well, and cook on medium flame for 2 minutes while stirring continuously.

- Add garam masala, paneer, chopped coriander, and salt. Mix well and keep the stuffing aside.

How to Proceed:

- Divide the prepared stuffing into 4-5 equal portions.

- Remove the stems of each mushroom.

- Stuff each mushroom with a portion of the prepared stuffing and press gently.

- Heat 1 tsp of butter in a broad non-stick pan, place stuffed mushrooms on it, cover with a lid, and cook on a medium flame for 2 minutes.

- Turn them over and cook for an additional 2 minutes on medium flame. Remove and set aside.

- Serve the stuffed mushrooms immediately.

name: Sattu Laddu
ingredients:
- 20g sattu flour

- 10g jaggery powder

- ½ tsp cardamom powder

- ½ tsp oil
nutrition:
- Calories: Around 70 kcal

- Fat: Around 1 g

- Protein: Around 2 g

- Fiber: Around 1 g
method:
- In a dry non-stick tava, add sattu flour and roast for 2-3 minutes until it becomes aromatic. Transfer the roasted sattu flour to a bowl.

- Melt jaggery in a pan.

- Add the roasted sattu flour to the melted jaggery and mix well.

- Grease your hands with a small quantity of oil.

- Take a small portion of the mixture and shape it into a ball or ladoo.

name: Lauki Dhokla
ingredients:
- 15 gms bottle gourd/lauki

- 20 gms besan/gram flour

- 1 green chilli

- ½ tsp chilli powder

- ¼ tsp ginger paste

- ½ tsp lemon juice

- pinch of turmeric powder

- salt to taste

- ½ tsp oil

- pinch of asafoetida/hing

- 10 gms mustard seeds

- fruit salt
method:
- Wash, peel, grate and remove the excess water from the bottle gourd.

- Add gram flour, ginger chilli paste, salt, turmeric powder, juice of lemon, water and mix well.

- Use very less water as the bottle gourd will release water and we want a thick batter.

- Add fruit salt to the batter and mix well untill the batter feels light and fluffy.

- Pour in a greased tray/thali, sprinkle some red chilli powder over it. Put in a steamer, cover and cook on a medium to low flame.

- Steam for 15- 20 minutes depending upon the thickness of the dhokla.

- Insert a knife to check, if it comes out clean it's ready, if the batter clings then it needs to be cooked for few more minutes.

- Heat oil, add mustard seeds, once they splutter add asafoetida, green chilli. Turn off the flame immediately, pour the mustard seeds over the dhokla with a spoon.

- Cut into desired pieces and serve.

name: Broccoli Daliya Khichdi
ingredients:
- 30g daliya (broken wheat)

- 20g moong dal (split mung beans)

- 100g broccoli

- 20g chopped onion

- 25g chopped tomato

- ½ tsp ginger garlic paste

- ½ tsp whole cumin

- 1 green chili

- ¼ tsp turmeric powder

- 1 stick curry leaves

- ¼ tsp mustard seeds

- ½ tsp garam masala

- Salt to taste

- 1 tsp oil
nutrition:
- Calories: Around 180 kcal

- Fat: Around 3 g

- Protein: Around 8 g

- Fiber: Around 7 g
method:
- Heat 1 tsp of oil in a pressure cooker. Add mustard seeds, whole cumin, and curry leaves.

- Add chopped onions and green chilies. Cook for a while. Add chopped tomatoes and mash to a pulp. Stir in the ginger garlic paste.

- Add broccoli, daliya, moong dal, turmeric powder, garam masala, and salt. Stir everything well and add water.

- Close the lid of the pressure cooker and cook for 4 whistles on medium flame.

- Remove from heat and allow the pressure to settle down.

- Serve hot with curd.

name: Spring Onion Poha
ingredients:
- 1 tsp oil

- ½ tsp whole cumin

- ¼ tsp mustard seeds

- 1 green chili

- Salt to taste

- ¼ tsp turmeric powder

- ½ tsp sugar

- 25g spring onion

- 5g green peas

- 30g soaked rice flakes (poha)

- 5g coriander leaves
nutrition:
- Calories: Around 120 kcal

- Fat: Around 3 g

- Protein: Around 2 g

- Fiber: Around 3 g
method:
- In a pan, heat oil and sauté whole cumin, mustard seeds, and green chili for a few minutes.

- Add spring onion bulbs, cooked potatoes, green peas, salt, sugar, and turmeric powder. Sauté well.

- Then add spring onion, soaked poha, and coriander leaves. Cook for a few more minutes.

name: Stir Fry Idli
ingredients:
- 2 medium-sized idlis

- 5g oil

- ½ tsp mustard seeds

- ½ tsp whole cumin

- Few curry leaves

- 5g urad dal

- A pinch of turmeric powder

- ½ tsp red chili powder

- 5g coriander leaves

- Salt to taste

- Lemon juice to taste
nutrition:
- Calories: Around 150 kcal

- Fat: Around 5 g

- Protein: Around 3 g

- Fiber: Around 2 g
method:
- Cut the 2 medium-sized idlis into pieces and set aside.

- In a non-stick pan, heat oil. Add mustard seeds, whole cumin, and urad dal. Let the dal become golden.

- Add the curry leaves and spices.

- Toss in the idli pieces and splash some water if needed.

- Leave it on low heat for some time to crisp up on one side if desired.

- Sprinkle some lemon juice and serve hot.

name: Vegetable Idli
ingredients:
For Idli Batter:

- 30g rice (parboiled)

- 8g urad dal

- ½ tsp fenugreek seeds

For Vegetable Topping:

- 5g oil

- ½ tsp mustard seeds

- ¼ tsp whole cumin

- 5g chana dal

- 5g urad dal

- Pinch of hing (asafoetida)

- Few curry leaves

- 1 green chili

- 1-inch ginger

- 5g carrot

- 5g capsicum

- 5g sweet corn

- 10g beans

- 5g peas

- A pinch of turmeric powder

Additional:

- 40ml curd

- Pinch of baking soda (optional)

Coriander leaves for garnish
nutrition:
- Calories: Around 200 kcal

- Fat: Around 5 g

- Protein: Around 7 g

- Fiber: Around 4 g
method:
For Idli Batter Preparation:

- Soak 30g parboiled rice and 8g urad dal separately in water for 4-5 hours. Include ½ tsp fenugreek seeds while soaking the dal for softer idlis.

- Drain excess water and grind rice finely. Do the same for urad dal and fenugreek seeds separately.

- Mix both ingredients thoroughly and allow the batter to ferment for 12-24 hours.

For Vegetable Topping:

- Finely chop all required vegetables.

- Heat oil in a pan, add mustard seeds, chana dal, whole cumin, urad dal, hing, and curry leaves.

- Add green chili, ginger, and sauté until golden.

- Incorporate grated carrot, capsicum, sweet corn, beans, and peas. Sauté for 2 minutes until slightly reduced.

- Add a pinch of turmeric, sauté briefly, and set aside.

For Instant Vegetable Idli:

- Combine vegetable mixture with idli batter, 60g curd, salt to taste, and mix well to form a smooth batter. Rest for 20 minutes.

- Grease the idli plate with oil and optionally add a pinch of baking soda to the batter.

- Pour the batter into the idli plate, sprinkle coriander leaves, and steam for 15 minutes on medium flame.

- Serve the instant vegetable idli with coconut chutney or sambar.

name: Crispy Rava Dosa
ingredients:
- 3/4 cup rice flour

- 1/4 cup chiroti rava (super fine rava / sooji)

- 1/4 teaspoon jeera (cumin seeds)

- 1/4 teaspoon ajwain (carom seeds)

- Salt to taste

- Water (to reach a thin buttermilk consistency)

- Ghee (for cooking)
nutrition:
- Calories: 210 kcal

- Fat: Around 4 g

- Protein: Around 3 g

- Fiber: Around 1 g
method:
- Prepare Batter: In a bowl, mix rice flour, chiroti rava, jeera, ajwain, and salt. Gradually add water and mix well until you achieve a thin buttermilk-like consistency.

- Heat Pan: Heat a non-stick pan on medium heat.

- Cook Dosa: Pour the batter onto the pan, spreading it thinly in a circular motion. Drizzle a little ghee over the dosa.

- Cover and Cook: Cover the dosa and cook until the edges start leaving the pan.

- Flip and Cook: Once the edges brown and crisp up, free the rava dosa from the pan, flip it, and cook the other side until golden and crispy.

- Serve: Serve the dosa hot and crispy.

name: Vegetable Roll With Yogurt
ingredients:
Vegetable Filling:

- 1/8 tsp whole cumin

- A pinch of fennel seeds

- 1/4 tsp chilli garlic paste

- 1/2 tsp oil

- 1/4 tsp powdered red chilli

- 1/4 tsp powdered garam masala powder

- 5g finely chopped broccoli

- 2.5g finely chopped cabbage

- 2.5g finely grated carrot

- 2.5g finely chopped capsicum

- 2.5g chopped onion

- 2.5g finely chopped tomato

- 2.5g sweet corn kernels

- 1/4 tsp chopped coriander leaves

- 5ml curd (yogurt)

- Salt to taste

For Roti:

- 15g wheat flour

- Boiling water as required

- A pinch of salt (optional)
nutrition:
- Calories: Around 150 kcal

- Fat: Around 3 g

- Protein: Around 4 g

- Fiber: Around 3 g
method:
Prepare Vegetable Filling:

- Heat oil in a pan over medium heat. Fry the fennel seeds and whole cumin for a few seconds.

- Add onions and chilli garlic paste. Saute until onions are translucent.

- Add broccoli, cabbage, carrot, capsicum, tomato (except for a portion for garnish), and sweet corn. Sauté for about a minute.

- Add red chilli powder, salt, and garam masala powder. Mix well and cook for another minute or two on low-medium heat.

- Garnish with coriander leaves. Remove from heat and let it cool slightly. Then mix in the curd (yogurt).

For Roti:

- In a large bowl, add wheat flour and salt. Pour in boiling water gradually while mixing with a spoon.

- Once it cools slightly, knead the dough for about 5 minutes until it becomes soft and smooth.

- Divide the dough into 2 balls. Roll each ball into circles gently.

- Toast each roti on a non-stick pan over medium heat. Cook each side for a few seconds until lightly browned.

Assembly:

- Place some of the prepared vegetable mixture onto a roti and roll the roti tightly to form a roll.

name: Broccoli Pulao
ingredients:
- 20g rice

- 15g finely chopped broccoli

- 5g finely chopped tomato

- 5g finely chopped onion

- 5g peas

- 1/2 tsp ginger garlic paste

- 1 green chilli

- A pinch of turmeric powder

- 1 inch of cinnamon

- 1 clove

- 1 bay leaf

- 1/2 star anise

- 1/2 tsp kasuri methi (dried fenugreek leaves)

- 1 cardamom pod

- 1/2 tsp whole cumin

- 2-3 mint leaves

- 1 tsp oil

- Salt to taste
nutrition:
- Calories: Around 120 kcal

- Fat: Around 2 g

- Protein: Around 3 g

- Fiber: Around 2 g
method:
Preparation:

- Heat the pressure cooker and add oil. Then add cumin seeds, cinnamon, clove, bay leaf, star anise, cardamom pod, and mint leaves. Allow them to splutter.

- Add onions and sauté until translucent. Then add ginger-garlic paste, green chili, and turmeric powder. Cook for a minute.

- Add peas and tomatoes. Cook for another minute, then add broccoli and rice. Mix well.

Cooking:

- Add water as required (enough to cook the rice). Once it starts boiling, add salt according to taste.

- Close the pressure cooker lid and cook for 2-3 whistles or until the rice is fully cooked.

Serving:

- Serve hot with raita or chutney.

name: Choliya Pulao
ingredients:
- 15g choliya (green chickpeas)

- 30g rice

- 50g cauliflower

- 5g peas

- 20g beans

- 10g carrot

- 5g coriander leaves

- 1 tsp Oil

- 1/2 tsp lemon juice

- 1 green chili

- 1/2 tsp ginger

- 1 cardamom

- 1 clove

- 1/2 cinnamon stick

- 1/2 tsp whole cumin

- 1/2 tsp Salt

- 8-10 black peppercorns
nutrition:
- Calories: Around 200 kcal

- Fat: Around 3 g

- Protein: Around 5 g

- Fiber: Around 5 g
method:
Preparation:

- In a pan, heat oil and add choliya (green chickpeas) and carrot. Cook for about 3 minutes.

- Meanwhile, in a pressure cooker, add whole cumin, cinnamon, ginger, green chilies, cardamom, black pepper, and cloves. Stir well.

- Add all the vegetables (cauliflower, peas, beans) to the pressure cooker and cook for a few minutes.

Cooking:

- Add the partially cooked choliya (chickpeas) and rice to the pressure cooker.

- Pour in water, add salt, and lemon juice.

- Pressure cook for 2-3 whistles or until the rice and vegetables are fully cooked.

Serving:

- Garnish with fresh coriander leaves on top.

- Serve hot.

name: Rajma Curry
ingredients:
- 20g soaked rajma (kidney beans)

- 10g tomato and green chili paste

- 1 tsp oil

- 5g coriander leaves

- 1/2 tsp cumin powder

- 1/4 tsp garam masala

- 2 tsp coriander powder

- 1/2 tsp turmeric powder

- A pinch of hing (asafoetida)

- 1/2 tsp red chili powder

- Salt to taste

- A pinch of baking soda
nutrition:
- Calories: Around 150 kcal

- Fat: Around 4 g

- Protein: Around 6 g

- Fiber: Around 4 g
method:
- Preparation:
- In a pressure cooker, add soaked rajma, salt, and baking soda. Add water, close the lid, and cook for 1 whistle. After that, boil it for an additional 6-7 minutes in the same cooker.

- Cooking:
- In a pan, heat oil. Add hing, cumin seeds (jeera), and turmeric. Then add tomato-green chili paste, coriander powder, red chili powder, and cumin powder. Stir well.

- Add the cooked rajma (kidney beans) to the masala. Adjust salt if needed. Sprinkle garam masala and mix well.

- Serving:
- Garnish with fresh coriander leaves on top.

name: Broccoli Salad
ingredients:
- 50g broccoli

- 2 cloves garlic, mashed into a paste

- 1 tsp lemon juice

- 1/2 tsp mustard seeds

- Red chili flakes to taste

- 1/4 tsp black pepper

- 1 tsp oil

- Salt to taste
nutrition:
- Calories: Around 70 kcal

- Fat: Around 3 g

- Protein: Around 3 g

- Fiber: Around 4 g
method:
Prepare Broccoli:

- Trim the bottoms of the broccoli stem and cut off the broccoli heads. Cut the broccoli heads into quarters. Peel the broccoli stems and cut them into quarters crosswise.

- Bring a pot of lightly salted water to a boil. Reduce heat to medium and cook the broccoli until tender but still slightly firm (about 5 to 6 minutes).

- Transfer the cooked broccoli to a large bowl filled with cold water to stop the cooking process. Drain well. Arrange broccoli in a colander with the florets facing down to drain for at least 30 minutes.

Prepare Dressing:

- Whisk together garlic, lemon juice, mustard seeds, salt, black pepper, and red chili flakes in a large serving bowl.

- Slowly drizzle in oil while whisking rapidly until the dressing thickens and becomes creamy. Adjust salt, black pepper, and red chili flakes to taste.

Assemble Salad:

- Toss the drained broccoli with the prepared dressing. Allow it to marinate for 5 to 10 minutes, then toss again.

- If desired, the salad can be refrigerated for up to an hour before serving if you prefer it cold.

name: Amaranth Thepla
ingredients:
- 1 tsp oil

- 20g finely chopped amaranth leaves (green)

- 30g whole wheat flour

- 1/4 tsp carom seeds

- 1/2 tsp whole cumin

- A pinch of roasted cumin powder

- 1/4 tsp turmeric powder

- 1/4 tsp garam masala powder

- 1 green chili, finely chopped

- 1/2 tsp dry raw mango powder (optional)

- Salt to taste
nutrition:
- Calories: Around 120 kcal

- Fat: Around 4 g

- Protein: Around 4 g

- Fiber: Around 3 g
method:
Preparation:

- Sift the whole wheat flour and keep it aside.

- Wash the amaranth leaves and strain excess water using a colander or by placing them between an absorbent cloth before finely chopping them.

Making the Dough:

- In a mixing bowl, combine all the ingredients except oil and water.

- Mix the ingredients using your hand and gradually add water to knead the mixture into a smooth dough. The dough should have a consistency similar to that of chapati dough.

- Finally, add oil and knead the dough for a minute. Let the dough rest for 20 minutes, covered with a damp cloth.

Cooking the Rotis:

- Heat an iron pan over high heat.

- Divide the dough into 1-inch balls and shape them into ovals or desired shapes.

- Roll out each ball into an oval shape and proceed to shallow fry the rotis in the heated pan until dark brown specks appear on both sides.

- Repeat the process with the remaining dough. Keep the cooked rotis covered in a linen cloth or casserole to retain warmth.

Serving:

- Serve the amaranth rotis with curd.

name: Soya Manchow Soup
ingredients:
- 1 tsp oil

- 2 cloves garlic, finely chopped

- 1-inch ginger, grated

- 1 green chili, finely chopped

- 5g onions, finely chopped

- 5g cabbage, finely chopped

- 5g carrots, finely chopped

- 5g sweet corn, finely chopped

- 10g mushrooms, finely chopped

- 10g cooked soya granules

- Salt to taste

- Water
nutrition:
- Calories: Around 90 kcal

- Fat: Around 3 g

- Protein: Around 5 g

- Fiber: Around 3 g
method:
Preparation:

- Heat oil in a pan. Add chopped garlic, green chili, and grated ginger. Sauté for a few seconds until fragrant.

- Add onions, cabbage, carrots, sweet corn, and sauté for about a minute.

- Then add sliced mushrooms and cooked soya granules. Stir and sauté for an additional two minutes on medium flame.

Cooking the Soup:

- Add water to achieve the desired consistency and stir well.

- Simmer the soup for 4 to 5 minutes on a low to medium flame without covering it.

- Afterward, add salt to taste and cover the pan. Simmer the soup on low to medium flame for about 15 minutes until the mushrooms, soya granules, and vegetables are cooked through.

- Occasionally check the soup while it simmers.

Final Touch:

- Once cooked, taste and adjust salt if needed.

- Serve the Soya Manchow Soup hot, with or without any accompaniment.

name: Mushroom Masala Rice
ingredients:
- 25g cooked rice

- 25g mushrooms

- Salt to taste

- 1 tsp oil

- 1 tsp garlic, minced

- 1 green chili, chopped

- 1 onion, chopped

- 10g capsicum (bell pepper), chopped

- Pepper powder, to taste

- Homemade tomato sauce
nutrition:
- Calories: Around 120 kcal

- Fat: Around 3 g

- Protein: Around 2 g

- Fiber: Around 2 g
method:
- Cooking:
- Heat oil in a pan. Add minced garlic, chopped green chili, and chopped onion. Sauté until translucent.

- Add chopped capsicum and mushrooms. Sauté until mushrooms are cooked.

- Season with salt, pepper powder, and homemade tomato sauce.

- Once the mushrooms are cooked well, add the cooked rice to the pan.

- Mixing:
- Mix the rice thoroughly with the mushroom and vegetable mixture until well combined.

name: Mushroom Veg White Sauce Pasta
ingredients:
- 20g mushrooms

- 40g wheat pasta

- 1 tsp oil

- 1 clove garlic, chopped

- 10ml milk

- 5g coriander leaves

- 1/2 tsp black pepper powder

- 5g onion, chopped

- 5g capsicum, chopped
nutrition:
- Calories: Around 200 kcal

- Fat: Around 4 g

- Protein: Around 6 g

- Fiber: Around 4 g
method:
Cooking the Pasta:

- Boil the wheat pasta in a pot of water until it's cooked. Drain the pasta and set it aside.

Preparing the Mushroom Pasta:

- In a pan, heat oil. Add chopped garlic and onion. Sauté until the onions become translucent.

- Add capsicum and mushrooms. Cook until they become soft.

- Pour milk into the pan and mix it well with the cooked vegetables.

- Add coriander leaves and black pepper powder. Stir to combine.

- Add the boiled pasta to the sauce and cook for an additional 2 minutes, allowing the flavors to combine.

Serve:

- Your Mushroom Pasta is now ready to be served.

name: Diced Mushroom Masala With Spring Onions
ingredients:
- 50g diced mushrooms

- 20g spring onion

- 10g chopped tomatoes

- 2 tsp chili powder

- 2 tsp coriander powder

- 1/2 tsp turmeric powder

- 1/2 tsp jeera (cumin) powder

- 1/2 tsp cashew nuts (in paste form)

- Ginger-garlic paste (quantity not specified)
nutrition:
- Calories: Around 120 kcal

- Fat: Around 5 g

- Protein: Around 4 g

- Fiber: Around 2 g
method:
Cooking Mushrooms:

- Heat oil in a pan and sauté ginger-garlic paste with diced mushrooms for about 5 minutes. Transfer the cooked mushrooms to a bowl.

Preparation of Gravy:

- In the same pan, add onions and sauté until golden brown. Add ginger-garlic paste and sauté for a minute.

- Add salt, chili powder, coriander powder, turmeric powder, jeera powder, and chopped tomatoes. Sauté well.

- Add cashew nut paste, mix it well, and add a little water. Allow it to boil.

- Once the mixture is boiling, add the cooked mushrooms and cook for an additional 5 minutes.

- Finally, add spring onions and cook for another minute.

Serving:

- Serve the dish hot.

name: Vegetable Kheema
ingredients:
- 10g cauliflower, grated or minced finely

- 10g mushrooms, finely chopped

- 10g French beans, chopped finely

- 5g carrot, grated or minced finely

- 5g green peas, boiled

- 10g tomatoes, chopped finely

- 10g onion, chopped finely

- 1 green chili

- 1-inch ginger, grated

- 2 garlic cloves, made into paste

- 1/2 cardamom

- 1/2-inch cinnamon

- 1/2 tsp coriander powder

- 1/4 tsp turmeric powder

- 1/4 tsp garam masala powder

- 1/2 tsp coriander leaves

- 1 tsp oil

- Salt, as required

- Water, as required
nutrition:
- Calories: Around 90 kcal

- Fat: Around 3 g

- Protein: Around 3 g

- Fiber: Around 4 g
method:
Cooking the Vegetables:

- Heat oil in a pan. Add whole garam masala spices - black cardamom and cinnamon.

- Add chopped onion and fry until light brown. Then add ginger-garlic paste.

- Add chopped tomatoes and all the spice powders (coriander powder, turmeric powder, garam masala powder). Fry the mixture until the oil separates.

- Add all the finely chopped veggies except the boiled green peas. Add water and salt. Cover and cook until all the veggies are well cooked.

- Ensure the mixture becomes dry without any moisture.

Final Touch:

- Once the vegetables are cooked, add the boiled green peas and stir. Check and adjust the seasonings if required.

- Serve the veg kheema hot, garnished with coriander leaves. This dish can be served with rotis, phulkas, naan, or bread.

name: Mushroom Soup
ingredients:
- 30g white button mushrooms, finely chopped

- 10g spring onion (white part), finely chopped

- 10g spring onion (green part), finely chopped

- 10g celery, finely chopped

- 2 garlic cloves, finely chopped

- 1/2 inch ginger, grated

- 1/2 tsp crushed black pepper

- 1 tsp oil

- Salt, as required
nutrition:
- Calories: Around 45 kcal

- Fat: Around 2 g

- Protein: Around 2 g

- Fiber: Around 2 g
method:
Preparation:

- Rinse, wipe, and finely chop the white button mushrooms. Slice the spring onions (white and green parts). Finely chop garlic cloves and grate the ginger.

Cooking the Soup:

- Heat oil in a pan. Add chopped garlic and ginger. Sauté for a few seconds.

- Then add the sliced spring onion whites and sauté for a minute. Set aside the spring onion greens to be added later.

- Add sliced mushrooms and chopped celery. Stir and sauté for two minutes over medium flame.

- Pour water as needed and stir. Simmer the soup for 4 to 5 minutes on a low to medium flame without covering it.

- Add 1/2 teaspoon crushed black pepper and salt according to taste.

- Cover the pan and continue simmering the soup on a low to medium flame for about 15 minutes or until the mushrooms are cooked.

- Occasionally check the soup while it simmers.

Final Touch:

- Once done, switch off the flame. Adjust seasoning with additional black pepper or salt if required.

- Finally, add the chopped spring onion greens. Rice vinegar can also be added if desired.

- Serve the clear mushroom soup hot, with or without accompaniment.

name: Ginger Tea
ingredients:
- 200ml water

- 1-inch ginger, grated or crushed

- 1 cardamom, crushed

- 5g tea powder

- 50ml milk

- 1 tsp sugar
nutrition:
- Calories: Around 40 kcal

- Fat: Around 1 g

- Protein: Around 1 g

- Fiber: Around 0 g
method:
Preparation:

- Rinse, peel, and crush the ginger roots in a mortar pestle or grate them.

- Crush or powder the green cardamom in a mortar-pestle.

Making Ginger Tea:

- In a saucepan or kettle, add water, grated or crushed ginger, and the crushed green cardamoms (with peels).

- Simmer until the color of the water changes to a mild yellowish hue due to ginger releasing its juices and flavors.

- Add sugar and simmer for an additional 1 to 2 minutes.

- Add tea powder and simmer for about 1 to 2 minutes until the water develops a deep red hue. Simmer for a longer time for a stronger tea, about 3 minutes or to desired strength. Turn off the heat, cover, and let the tea steep for 3 to 4 minutes.

- Then add milk and simmer for another minute or two.

- Strain the tea through a strainer into cups.

- Serve the hot ginger tea.

name: Veg Sticks
ingredients:
- 20g avocado, peeled and stone removed

- 1 clove garlic, crushed

- 1/2 tsp lemon juice

- 5g onion, finely chopped

- 1 small red chili, seeds removed, finely chopped

- 5g carrot, cut into sticks

- 10g cucumber, cut into sticks

- 5g snow peas, ends removed

- 10g cherry tomatoes

- 5g capsicum, cut into sticks

- Salt and pepper, to taste
nutrition:
- Calories: Around 70 kcal

- Fat: Around 5 g

- Protein: Around 1 g

- Fiber: Around 3 g
method:
Chunky Version:

- Place avocados, crushed garlic, lemon juice, chopped onion, and chopped chili in a small bowl.

- Use a fork to mash the avocado until all the ingredients are well-combined. Season with salt and pepper to taste.

Smooth Version:

- Place avocados, crushed garlic, lemon juice, salt, chopped red onion, and chopped chili in a food processor.

- Blend until smooth.

- For serving, place the dip into a small serving bowl and arrange the vegetable sticks and cherry tomatoes around it on a serving platter.

name: Vegetable Coconut Stew
ingredients:
For the Base:

- 2 Carrots, cut into 1" pieces

- 10-15 French beans, cut into 1" pieces

- 1/2 cup peas

- 1/2 cauliflower, cut into florets

- 1 cup water

- Pinch of salt

For the Stew:

- 1 big onion, cut into big cubes

- 3-4 Green Chillies, slit through the center

- 1 cup thick coconut milk

- 1 tsp garlic, finely chopped

- 1 tsp ginger, peeled and finely chopped

- 1-2 bay leaves

- 1 tbsp chopped coriander leaves

- 2 tbsp unflavored or coconut oil

- Salt to taste
nutrition:
- Calories: Around 200 kcal

- Fat: Around 15 g

- Protein: Around 5 g

- Fiber: Around 7 g
method:
Preparing the Vegetables:

- Put carrots, beans, peas, and cauliflower in a pressure cooker with 1 cup of water and a pinch of salt.

- Close the pressure cooker and cook on medium heat for 1 whistle.

- Switch off the heat and allow the pressure cooker to release pressure. Carefully open it once all the pressure has been released.

Preparing the Stew:

- Heat oil in a pan over medium heat. Add bay leaves, chopped garlic, ginger, and slit green chilies. Cook until the raw smell dissipates and ginger-garlic begin to change color.

- Add the chopped onions and stir-fry for a minute or until slightly translucent.

- Add the cooked vegetables along with the remaining water. Gently stir for a few minutes, taking care not to break the vegetables.

- Reduce the heat to low and slowly pour in the coconut milk.

- Taste the curry for salt and adjust as needed.

- Cook the stew on low flame until it starts bubbling.

- Remove from heat and garnish with 1 tbsp chopped coriander (optional).

name: Vegetable Loaded Bhel Puri
ingredients:
- 15g puffed rice

- 10g finely chopped tomatoes

- 10g finely chopped onions

- 5g grated carrot

- 10g finely chopped cucumber

- 1/2 tsp finely chopped coriander (dhania)

- 1/2 tsp chili powder

- 1/2 tsp chaat masala

- 1/2 tsp lemon juice

- Salt to taste
nutrition:
- Calories: Around 40 kcal

- Fat: Around 0.5 g

- Protein: Around 1 g

- Fiber: Around 1.5 g
method:
- Combine all the ingredients in a deep bowl.

- Mix well until all ingredients are thoroughly combined.

- Serve the vegetables loaded bhel immediately.

name: Lettuce And Radish Salad
ingredients:
- 20g romaine lettuce

- 5g cucumbers, thinly sliced

- 20g radishes, trimmed and thinly sliced

- 5g spring onion, finely chopped

- 1 tsp extra virgin olive oil

- 1 tsp freshly squeezed lemon juice

- Salt to taste

- Ground black pepper to taste

- Zest from ½ lemon (optional)
nutrition:
- Calories: Around 45 kcal

- Fat: Around 3 g

- Protein: Around 1 g

- Fiber: Around 2 g
method:
To Make Lemon Vinaigrette:

- In a small bowl, combine and stir together extra virgin olive oil, freshly squeezed lemon juice, salt, and ground black pepper. Set aside.

To Make Lettuce Radish Salad:

- Rinse and pat dry all vegetables.

- In a medium salad bowl, combine thinly sliced cucumbers, thinly sliced radishes, and finely chopped fresh spring onions.

- Chop romaine lettuce into bite-sized pieces and add it to the salad.

- Drizzle with lemon vinaigrette and toss gently until the salad is evenly coated. Alternatively, you can drizzle without tossing and serve.

name: Masala Puffed Rice
ingredients:
- 20g Puffed rice

- 5g Groundnuts

- 5g Bengal gram dal, roasted

- 1/4 tsp Turmeric powder

- 1/2 tsp Chilli powder

- 10g Tomato, finely chopped

- 10g Onion, finely chopped

- 1/2 tsp Coriander leaves, finely chopped

- 1/2 tsp Lemon juice

- Salt to taste
nutrition:
- Calories: Around 70 kcal

- Fat: Around 2 g

- Protein: Around 3 g

- Fiber: Around 2 g
method:
- In a deep bowl, combine all the ingredients thoroughly.

- Mix well to ensure the spices and flavors are evenly distributed.

- Serve the masala bhel immediately.

name: Peri Peri Yogurt Dip
ingredients:
- 1 Kashmiri red chilli

- 2 garlic cloves, finely chopped

- 1/4 tsp red chilli flakes

- 1/2 tsp coriander leaves, finely chopped

- 1 tsp lemon juice

- 40ml yogurt

- 1 tsp virgin olive oil

- 1/2 tsp fresh oregano leaves

- Salt to taste
nutrition:
- Calories: Around 60 kcal

- Fat: Around 4 g

- Protein: Around 2 g

- Fiber: Around 1 g
method:
- Remove the stems of Kashmiri red chilli and soak them in water for 5 minutes.

- Grind all the ingredients (except for chilli flakes and salt) to a smooth paste in a mixer grinder, adding olive oil slowly.

- Transfer the mixture to a bowl, add yogurt, chilli flakes, and salt. Mix well.

- Serve it with some starters.

name: Chicken Coconut Stew
ingredients:
Base:

- 100g Chicken (with bone, without skin)

- 20g Carrots, cut into 1" pieces

- 3-4 French beans, cut into 1" pieces

- 1/4 cup peas

- 1/4 cup cauliflower florets

- 1/4 cup water

Stew:

- 1/4 large onion, cut into big cubes

- 1 Green Chili, slit through the center

- 1/4 cup thick coconut milk

- 1/4 tsp garlic, finely chopped

- 1/4 tsp ginger, peeled and finely chopped

- 1/4 tsp chopped coriander leaves

- 1/2 tbsp unflavored or coconut oil

- 1-2 Bay leaves
nutrition:
- Calories: Around 190 kcal

- Fat: Around 11 g

- Protein: Around 12 g

- Fiber: Around 3 g
method:
Base Preparation:

- Place the chicken, carrots, French beans, peas, and cauliflower in a pressure cooker with 1/4 cup of water and a pinch of salt.

- Pressure cook on medium heat for 1 whistle.

- Allow the pressure cooker to release pressure naturally before opening.

Stew Preparation:

- Heat oil in a pan on medium heat. Add bay leaves, chopped garlic, ginger, and slit green chili. Cook until the raw smell diminishes and the ginger-garlic change color.

- Add chopped onion and stir-fry for a minute.

- Add the cooked chicken and vegetables along with the remaining water. Stir gently for a few minutes.

- Reduce the heat and slowly add in coconut milk. Adjust salt as needed.

- Continue cooking the stew on low heat until it starts to bubble.

- Remove from heat and garnish with chopped coriander (optional).

name: Chinese Spinach
ingredients:
- Spinach Stir-Fry:
- 100g spinach (washed and cut into big pieces)

- 1 tbsp refined oil

- 1/4 medium onion, chopped

- 1 tsp chopped garlic

- 1/8 - 1/4 tsp chili flakes

- Pinch of pepper

- Salt to taste

- 1/2 tsp lemon juice
nutrition:
- Calories: Around 80 kcal

- Fat: Around 7 g

- Protein: Around 1 g

- Fiber: Around 2 g
method:
- Heat oil in a pan on medium flame.

- Add chopped garlic, stir-fry until it starts changing color.

- Add chopped onion, stir-fry for a minute.

- Add spinach to the pan, stir-fry with onion and garlic for a few minutes.

- Add chili flakes, pepper, lemon juice, and salt. Continue stir-frying for a few more minutes.

- Cook until the spinach releases its liquid and the liquid evaporates.

- Once the liquid dries up, the spinach stir-fry is done.

name: Bottle Gourd Kadhi
ingredients:
Curd Mixture:

- 100g homemade curd

- 1/2 tsp besan (chickpea flour)

- Pinch of salt

- Red chilli powder to taste

- 1/4 tsp coriander powder

Bottle Gourd:

- 100g bottle gourd, cut into cubes

- Pinch of salt

Kadhi:

- 1 tbsp refined oil

- 1/4 tsp black mustard seeds

- 1/4 tsp whole cumin

- 1/2 tsp finely chopped ginger

- 2-3 green chillies, slit

- 1/4 medium onion, chopped into cubes

- 1/2 tsp turmeric powder

- 6-10 curry leaves

- Salt to taste

- 1/2 cup water
nutrition:
- Calories: Around 100 kcal

- Fat: Around 6 g

- Protein: Around 4 g

- Fiber: Around 2 g
method:
Prepare Curd Mixture:

- Mix curd, besan, salt, red chilli powder, and coriander powder. Blend until smooth. Set aside.

Cook Bottle Gourd:

- In a pressure cooker, add bottle gourd cubes, a pinch of salt, and 1 cup of water.

- Cook for 1 whistle on medium heat, then simmer for 5 minutes after reducing the flame.

- Allow pressure to release naturally. Reserve the water, do not drain.

Prepare Kadhi:

- Heat oil in a pan. Add mustard seeds and cumin. Allow them to splutter.

- Add ginger, green chillies, and chopped onion. Sauté for a few minutes.

- Lower the heat, slowly pour in the prepared curd mixture, stirring continuously to prevent lumps.

- Add turmeric powder, curry leaves, and 1/2 cup water gradually while stirring.

- Add cooked bottle gourd along with the reserved water from the pressure cooker.

- Adjust salt to taste. Let it simmer for 5 minutes.

- Turn off the heat and serve with rice.

name: Onion Poha
ingredients:
- 30g poha (flattened rice)

- Onion (quantity as per preference)

- 10g roasted peanuts

- 2 green chillies

- 4-5 curry leaves

- 1/2 tsp mustard seeds

- 1/2 tsp oil

- 1/2 tsp turmeric powder

- 3/4 tsp salt

- 1/2 tsp lemon juice
nutrition:
- Calories: Around 180 kcal

- Fat: 6 g

- Protein: 5 g

- Fiber: 3 g
method:
- Rinse the 30g of poha in water until softened, drain all the water, and set aside.

- Add 3/4 tsp salt and 1/2 tsp turmeric powder to the poha, mix gently, and set aside.

- Dry roast 10g peanuts until crunchy.

- Heat oil in a pan, crackle 1/2 tsp mustard seeds.

- Add finely chopped onions (quantity as per preference) and sauté until translucent.

- Add 4-5 curry leaves, 2 chopped green chillies, and sauté briefly.

- Add the roasted peanuts and stir.

- Add the prepared poha, mix gently, cover, and steam for about 2 minutes on low heat.

- Switch off the heat and let it remain covered for 1-2 minutes.

- Remove the lid, sprinkle 1/2 tsp lemon juice, mix gently, and serve.

name: Peas Poha
ingredients:
- 30g poha (flattened rice)

- 30g peas (boiled)

- 15g onion (finely chopped)

- 2 green chillies (chopped)

- 4-5 curry leaves

- 1/2 tsp mustard seeds

- 1/2 tsp whole cumin seeds

- 1/2 tsp oil

- 1/2 tsp turmeric powder

- 3/4 tsp salt

- 1/2 tsp lemon juice
nutrition:
- Calories: Around 110 kcal

- Fat: 1.5 g

- Protein: 4 g

- Fiber: 3 g
method:
- Rinse 30g of thick poha in water until softened, drain, and set aside.

- Add 1/2 tsp turmeric powder and boiled peas to the poha, mix well, and set aside.

- Heat 1/2 tsp oil in a pan. Add mustard seeds and whole cumin seeds; let them crackle.

- Add 15g finely chopped onions, sauté until translucent.

- Add curry leaves and chopped green chillies, sauté for a few seconds.

- Add the poha-peas mixture, mix gently.

- Cover and steam for about 2 minutes on low heat.

- Turn off the heat and let it remain covered for 1-2 minutes.

- Remove the lid, sprinkle 1/2 tsp lemon juice, mix gently, and serve.

name: Cucumber Dosa
ingredients:
- 60g Rice

- 100g Chopped cucumber

- 1/2 tsp Finely chopped ginger

- 2 Chopped green chillies

- 1 tsp Salt
nutrition:
- Calories: Around 160 kcal

- Fat: Around 0.5 g

- Protein: Around 3 g

- Fiber: Around 1 g
method:
- Wash and soak rice for a minimum of 2 hours.

- Cut off the ends of the cucumber and chop it roughly.

- Once the rice is soaked, drain water completely.

- Grind chopped cucumber, ginger, green chilli, rice, and salt together until slightly coarse. Add water only if needed in small quantities as cucumber tends to release water.

- The batter's consistency should be slightly runnier than idli or dosa batter.

- Heat a tawa (griddle) and spread 2 ladles of prepared batter.

- Cook both sides by flipping, each side for about a minute.

- Oil is not necessary; add only if needed, but after spreading.

name: Besan Chilla With Vegetables
ingredients:
- 60g Besan/Gram flour

- 20g Onion, finely chopped

- 15g Tomato, finely chopped

- 15g Beans, finely chopped

- 15g Capsicum, finely chopped

- 1 tsp Finely chopped ginger

- 2 tbsp Coriander leaves

- 1/2 tsp Ajwain/Carom seeds

- 1 tsp Salt

- 2-3 pinches of Turmeric powder

- 1/2 tsp Chilli powder

- 1/2 tsp Oil
nutrition:
- Calories: Around 215 kcal

- Fat: Around 6 g

- Protein: around 12 g

- Fiber: Around 6 g
method:
- Pour 30g of besan into a mixing bowl.

- Add all the finely chopped vegetables, chopped ginger, and mix thoroughly.

- Then add all the spices and salt, mix again.

- Add water accordingly to make it a flowy consistency batter and mix well.

- Continue whisking until the batter is smooth and flowy, without any lumps.

- Heat a pan, add oil. Pour a ladle full of the batter on the pan and gently spread it using the ladle.

- Cook the chilla on low-medium heat until the top begins to look cooked or air-pockets appear.

- Flip and continue to cook until the base gets light golden.

- Once properly cooked from both sides, fold the besan chilla and serve hot.

name: Broken Wheat Khichdi
ingredients:
- 30g Broken wheat (Daliya)

- 15g Green gram dal

- 15g Onion

- 10g Tomato

- 10g Capsicum

- 10g Cabbage

- 10g Cauliflower

- 1 tsp Ginger-garlic paste

- 2 Chopped green chillies

- 1 Bay leaf

- 1/2 tsp Jeera (Cumin seeds)

- 1/2 tsp Turmeric powder

- 1/2 tsp Chilli powder

- 1/2 tsp Jeera powder

- 1 tsp Dhania powder (Coriander powder)

- 1 tbsp Freshly chopped coriander leaves

- 1 tsp Salt

- 1/2 tsp Oil
nutrition:
- Calories: Around 170 kcal

- Fat: Around 1.5 g

- Protein: Around 7 g

- Carbohydrates: Around 33 g

- Fiber: Around 7 g
method:
- Dry roast the green gram dal and set it aside.

- In a pressure cooker, heat oil.

- Add 1 bay leaf and 1/2 tsp jeera. Allow it to crackle.

- Add ginger-garlic paste and stir for 1 minute. Then add all the vegetables and stir for 2-3 minutes.

- Add all the spices, mix well, and cook for 1-2 minutes.

- Add broken wheat, roasted green gram dal, water, and salt into the pressure cooker. Mix thoroughly.

- Close the pressure cooker and cook after 3 whistles.

- Add freshly chopped coriander leaves and serve hot.

name: Green Moong Dal Chilla
ingredients:
- 60g whole green moong dal

- 30g onion grated

- 15g capsicum grated

- 1 tsp ginger chopped

- 15g coriander leaves

- 1 green chilli chopped

- ½ tsp salt
method:
- Soak the whole moong dal in water for 6- 8 hours. Drain thoroughly and grind to a coarse paste without adding water.

- Take the ground dal in a bowl and add grated onion, capsicum, chopped ginger, chilli, coriander leaves, salt and mix well.

- Add ½ cup water and mix well.

- Heat a non stick pan and pour the batter and spread it into a thick small circle.

- Cook on medium flame till the chilla becomes golden and crispy on the edges.

- Flip and cook on the other side as well.

- Serve moong dal chilla hot with curd, coriander chutney, mint chutney or tomato chutney.

name: Mini Uttapam
ingredients:
- 30g rice

- 15g urad dal

- 15g onion chopped

- 15g tomato chopped

- 15g capsicum chopped

- 15g beans

- 2 green chillies chopped

- 3 tbsp coriander leaves chopped

- 1 tsp salt (add it to the batter)

- ½ tsp oil
method:
- Soak rice and dal for 5-6 hours, grind it into a batter (semi- liquid consistency) and leave it overnight to ferment.

- Mix together all the chopped vegetables and keep it aside.

- Heat oil in a pan and drop a small ladleful of batter. Slowly place the mixed vegetables on it and cook on medium flame for 1- 2 minutes.

- Flip it over and let it cook further for a minute.

- Once it is cooked from both the sides, transfer into a plate and serve hot.

- It can be served with mint chutney or coriander chutney or with sambar.

name: Pongal
ingredients:
- 40g rice

- 15g green gram dal (split)

- 4-5 curry leaves

- 5-6 black pepper corn

- ½ tsp whole cumin seeds

- ¼ tsp asafoetida

- ½ tsp ginger paste or finely chopped

- 1 slit green chilli

- pinch of turmeric powder

- 1 tsp salt

- ½ tsp oil
method:
- Soak rice for 30-45 minutes and keep it aside.

- Add dal to a pressure cooker. Dry roast on a low to medium flame till it begin to smell nice and aromatic. Do not brown or discolour the moong dal.

- Add soaked rice to the roasted dal. Drain the water from the rice completely.

- Pour water accordingly. Add salt and cook the rice and dal to a soft texture on medium flame (2-3 whistles).

- Heat a small pan with ½ tsp oil. Add ½ tsp whole cumin, 5-6 crushed pepper.

- When the seeds splutter, then add curry leaves, slit green chilli and ginger.

- Saute well until the tempering turns aromatic and curry leaves turn crisp.

- Then add hing (asafoetida) and a pinch of turmeric powder.

- Pour this to the cooked pongal. Mix and simmer for 1- 2 minutes so the flavours are absorbed.

- Serve hot.

name: Roasted Eggplant
ingredients:
- 100g of eggplant

- 1 tsp chilli powder

- ½ tsp salt

- ½ tsp oil

- 1 tsp lemon juice
method:
- Preheat the oven to 400 degrees F (200 degree C). Line a baking sheet with parchment paper or lightly grease with oil.

- Slice the eggplant in round shape medium size (do not slice it too thin or too thick). Marinate it with salt and chilly powder and keep aside for 10 minutes. Place the eggplant onto the greased baking sheet. Roast in the preheated oven until softened and golden brown on both the sides of the eggplant.

- Remove from the oven and sprinkle with lemon juice. Serve hot.

Method(if roasted in pan)

- Preheat the pan for 5-7 minutes.

- Slice the eggplant in round shape medium size (do not slice it too thin or too thick). Marinate it with salt and chilly powder and keep it aside for 10 minutes.

- Make small cuts in between, so that the spices go in properly. Brush each slice with oil.

- Place the slices on the pan, cover the pan and roast from both sides until softened and golden brown.

- Remove from the pan and sprinkle with lemon juice. Serve hot.

name: Sprouts Sandwich
ingredients:
- 30g whole wheat bread/multigrain bread

- 30g mixed sprouts

- 20 grams onion

- 20 grams tomato

- 20 grams capsicum

- 5 ml oil

- green chilli

- coriander
method:
